electronic_structure_description: Ground term: S0. Vertical 1(pi,pi*) transition energy at the Franck-Condon geometry: 5.18 eV with 6-31G*, 4.83 eV with ANO-S 321/21, 4.83 eV with ANO-L 321/21 and 4.72 eV with ANO-L 432/21, against an experimental band maximum near 4.8 eV; the Pople basis overestimates while the ANO sets agree with experiment and with coupled-cluster references. The 1(nO pi*) minimum has an elongated C4=O bond of about 1.37 A at CASSCF with a C6C5C4O dihedral of -165.5 degrees, versus about 1.365 A and a nearly planar -178 degree dihedral at CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2
Other: The central result is how strongly the predicted photochemistry depends on basis set, active space, optimization technique and convergence thresholds. With 6-31G the minimum energy path reaches a planar 1(pi,pi*) minimum; with the more flexible 6-31G* the same active space instead decays barrierlessly to the ring-puckered ethene-like 1(pi,pi*/S0) conical intersection, and adding correlating orbitals as CASSCF(10,11) reproduces that. Tightening the optimization thresholds also moves the outcome from a minimum to the conical intersection, and independent stationary-point optimization plus LIIC gives a well-defined excited-state minimum where the MEP at the same level does not. At CASPT2 no planar structure is found by MEP; instead a twisted boat-like 1(pi,pi*) minimum appears, and whether the path is barrierless depends on the hypersphere radius r (r = 0.09 and MS-CASPT2 r = 0.18 reach a minimum, r = 0.30 is barrierless to the conical intersection). The covalent 1(nO pi*) state depends far less on dynamic correlation than the zwitterionic 1(pi,pi*) state. CASPT2 used a 0.2 a.u. imaginary level shift with all core electrons frozen. The authors caution that although CASPT2//CASSCF and CASPT2//CASPT2 agree qualitatively for static calculations, the overly steep CASSCF gradients are expected to give too-short decay times in on-the-fly nonadiabatic dynamics.

Other: Explicitly framed as a test of how far the active space can be reduced. The key negative result is that reducing the active space gives erroneous results specifically in the dissociation region, because orbital rotations change the composition of the active space along the C-N dissociation coordinate; the authors flag this as a serious drawback for automated active-space selection procedures and for CASSCF-like methods that automatically shrink or grow the active space. geometry_source: QM/MM optimized in this work. software: TeraChem for the QM part coupled to OpenMM for the MM part

active_space_protocol: (8,9) sized around the breaking O-O bond; state-averaging over four singlets and two triplets, with dynamic weights referenced to S0 using a 3 eV bandwidth. A separate, much smaller SA(2)-CASSCF(4,3)/3-21G space was used only on an HBDI-valine model to parametrize the force field and to compare link-atom schemes
nroots_per_mult: 4 singlets and 2 triplets in the state-average
Other: State characters from attach-detach density analysis at image 20 of the gas-phase path: S1, S2 and S3 are all local 1(n,sigma*) excitations in the O-O region; T1 is 3(n,sigma*) and T2 is 3(sigma,sigma*). Environment changes the picture qualitatively. For the benzene reference calculations in this same paper the conventional pi-space CASSCF(6,6) was used instead
Other: A clear worked example of CASSCF state-ordering error. CASSCF(22,16) makes 1 1B1u the lowest singlet and puts 1 1Au second, whereas every coupled-cluster method (CCSD, CCSDR(3), CC3) puts 1 1Au first - so the identity of S1 itself depends on the method. ligand_set: meso-perfluoroalkyl-substituted porphyrin macrocycle (four pyrrole N donors)
geometry_source: singlet ground state optimized at B3LYP/def2-TZVP with the RI approximation under C1 symmetry in Turbomole, then re-optimized to the triplet state at B3LYP/def2-TZVP without symmetry constraints in ORCA
method: CASSCF for the EPR zero-field splitting parameters of the photoexcited triplet state, compared against B3LYP DFT using the spin-unrestricted natural orbital (UNO) approach, and against multifrequency transient EPR (X-band ~9.75 GHz and W-band ~94 GHz, 532 nm photoexcitation) and pulse ENDOR on 0.2 mmol/dm3 frozen 2-MeTHF solutions
software: ORCA 4.1.2 for the property and CASSCF calculations; Turbomole 6.1 for the singlet ground-state optimizations
basis_set: def2-SVP with def2-TZVPP on zinc for the CASSCF EPR parameters; B3LYP/def2-TZVP for the geometries; 6-31G(d) on zinc with EPR-II elsewhere for the DFT EPR parameters
ss_included: yes - the zero-field splitting is treated through the spin-spin (magnetic dipolar) contribution only
active_space_orbital_description: the four Gouterman-model frontier orbitals of the porphyrin macrocycle
active_space_protocol: CAS(4,4): four electrons in four molecular orbitals, chosen so that the active orbitals correspond to the Gouterman four-orbital model long used to interpret porphyrin optical spectra. Initial active orbitals were taken from a restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock (ROHF) calculation. The motivation is explicit: the lowest triplet state of a porphyrin is an admixture of more than one of the canonical triplet wave functions available to DFT, so a multireference treatment is needed, and CAS(4,4) captures enough of that character to improve both the magnitude and, more importantly, the trend of the calculated D values relative to DFT. The authors state plainly that enlarging the active space is the necessary next step for these highly delocalized triplets.
Other: Experimental trEPR simulation parameters: D = –1017 MHz, E = +333 MHz, g = (2.0033, 2.0033, 2.0003), relative triplet sublevel populations (PX, PY, PZ) = (0.81, 0.00, 0.19); asymmetry parameter eta_D = |E/D| = 0.33. Calculated D and eta_D: DFT –863 MHz / 0.16; CASSCF(4,4) +939 MHz / 0.29. The starkest sign disagreement in the set: experiment gives D = -1017 MHz, DFT agrees on the sign at -863 MHz, but CASSCF returns +939 MHz. The authors leave this open, tentatively attributing it to the complex electronic symmetry - with a strongly orthorhombic ZFS interaction (eta_D = 0.33) a small error in the computed tensor can swap the principal-axis assignment and with it the sign of D. Across the whole series CASSCF(4,4) tracks the experimental magnitudes and trend much better than DFT, but neither method reliably reproduces the sign of D - the paper's blunt conclusion is that both clearly fail on the sign, and that further theoretical development is needed before a computed sign of D can be used to infer spin delocalization. The non-Boltzmann sublevel populations reflect the spin-polarized triplet formed by anisotropic intersystem crossing.

compound_name: Cyclopropanone, photodissociation to carbon monoxide and ethylene (Norrish-type CO release) plus a polymerization channel
geometry_source: initial conditions from ground-state molecular dynamics sampling at constant excitation energy, mimicking continuous-wave excitation in resonance with the laser; 100 geometries sampled across the spectrum. The cheaper (2,4) active space was used for this ground-state sampling stage
method: a controlled comparison of eight electronic structure methods - SA-CASSCF, SS-CASPT2, MS-CASPT2, XMS-CASPT2, MRCI, FOMO-CASCI, MR-CISD/OM3 and SI-SA-REKS - crossed against several nonadiabatic algorithms (Landau-Zener surface hopping, fewest-switches surface hopping, AIMSWISS), to separate the influence of electronic structure from that of the coupled electron-nuclear algorithm
software: BAGEL for the CASPT2 simulations; other packages per method
basis_set: 6-31G* for most calculations; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 runs in BAGEL where 6-31G* is unavailable; a pseudominimal basis by default for MR-CISD/OM3
active_space_orbital_description: two sigma(CC), pi(CO), n(O), pi*(CO) and two sigma*(CC)
active_space_protocol: (8,7) - two sigma(CC), pi(CO), n(O), pi*(CO), two sigma*(CC) - used for every method except SI-SA-REKS. The choice was triangulated three ways rather than assumed: previous studies of this molecule, automated selection with the AutoCAS code, and the authors' own benchmarking of potential energy surfaces and absorption spectra. Two reduced spaces appear for practical reasons: (2,4) for the cheaper ground-state sampling, and (2,2) containing only n(O) and pi*(CO) for SI-SA-REKS, which has no other space implemented. All CASPT2 calculations used a 0.5 a.u. level shift, tested to be insensitive across a wide range. Only S0 and S1 were treated, equally weighted in the SA-CASSCF state-averaging
Other: The paper's central result is that the electronic structure method matters far more than the nonadiabatic algorithm. Excited-state lifetimes across the ab initio family span nearly a factor of two: XMS-CASPT2 39 fs, MS-CASPT2 54 fs, FOMO-CASCI 58 fs, SA-CASSCF 68 fs - a spread the authors call surprising given that the underlying potential energy surfaces differ negligibly. Semiempirical MR-CISD/OM3 is fastest at 36 fs (within XMS-CASPT2 error bars); SI-SA-REKS is an outlier at 90 fs whose population transfer stops abruptly at 140 fs. CO release quantum yields: all ab initio methods agree within error bars and sit close to the experimental 0.73 (intensity-weighted average); MR-CISD/OM3 overestimates at 0.89; SI-SA-REKS fails outright at 0.20 (the authors could not reproduce the 0.44 +/- 0.11 previously published for that method). All ab initio methods find the polymerization channel at least once while the DFT and semiempirical ones never do. By contrast the coupled electron-nuclear algorithms give identical quantum yields within statistical error and consistent population transfer, with FSSH and LZSH essentially equivalent - so when conical intersections are well defined the cheaper LZSH is sufficient.

geometry_source: initial geometries and velocities sampled from the Wigner distribution without temperature broadening using SHARC tools; 100 trajectories propagated for 150 fs with a 0.5 fs time step
method: trajectory surface hopping (fewest switches, energy-based decoherence correction with a 0.1 Hartree decay factor) with XMS-CASPT2 using analytical nonadiabatic coupling vectors as the reference, compared against XMS-CASPT2 with local diabatization, MS-CASPT2, CASSCF, CC2, ADC(2), CIS, and TD-/TDA-DFT (PBE, PBE0, CAM-B3LYP)
software: SHARC for the dynamics; BAGEL for the reference XMS-CASPT2 (NACV and local diabatization); OpenMolcas for XMS-CASPT2 (lLD), MS-CASPT2 and CASSCF with the RI approximation and analytical Cholesky decomposition; Turbomole 7.3 for CC2 and ADC(2); Gaussian 16, Turbomole and ORCA 5.0.3 for the CIS and DFT variants
active_space_orbital_description: the pi and pi* orbitals plus the two nitrogen lone pairs
active_space_protocol: (6,4): pi, pi* and the two nitrogen lone pairs, used identically for XMS-CASPT2, MS-CASPT2 and CASSCF so the methods are compared on equal footing. The reference XMS-CASPT2 used no level shift and had IPEA deactivated. Note the independent convergence on this same (6,4) space for azomethane in 10.1021/acs.jctc.9b00917 and 10.1021/acs.jctc.3c00137, though those papers do not all spell out the orbital composition
Other: Reference XMS-CASPT2 dynamics resolves four time regimes: (I) about 30 fs during which all molecules stay cis on S1; (II) crossing of a first conical intersection region up to about 60 fs, giving 20-25 percent nonadiabatic S1-to-S0 decay and complete cis-to-trans isomerization; (III) a roughly 40 fs plateau with most molecules trans; (IV) a second strong-coupling region with further decay, during which some molecules return to cis. The 90 degree conical intersection is reached after about 40 fs and the 270 degree one from about 120 fs. The end of regime II appears at about 60 fs regardless of electronic structure method. Method verdict: multireference methods are the preferred choice. CC2, TD-PBE, TDA-PBE, TD-PBE0 and TD-CAM-B3LYP are too unstable near electronic degeneracies to give trustworthy statistics. ADC(2) with local diabatization, TDA-PBE0 and TDA-CAM-B3LYP reproduce the timescale (despite up to 40 percent of trajectories crashing) but predict almost total decay through the first crossing and so badly describe the 'rotator' trajectories. CIS additionally fails to reproduce the population plateau. The authors' most transferable caution: which methods would succeed could hardly be predicted from a static analysis of the potential energy surfaces, so the usual practice of validating an electronic structure method on static energetics before running dynamics may not be sufficient.

compound_name: PSB3 (penta-2,4-dieniminium cation), the minimal retinal chromophore model
geometry_source: S1 potential energy scans built by constraining the torsional coordinate; quantum-classical trajectories from sampled initial conditions
method: quantum-classical (surface hopping) trajectories driven by CASSCF, XMS-CASPT2, RMS-CASPT2 and the REKS-family SSR(2,2) and SSR(3,2) methods (BHHLYP functional), compared on identical footing
software: OpenMolcas for the CASPT2-level QM calculations and OpenMolcas/Tinker for QM/MM; the OpenMolcas-GAMESS-US/Tinker interface for the REKS calculations
active_space_orbital_description: all pi and pi* orbitals of the conjugated polyenic chain
active_space_protocol: Active spaces are set by the conjugated chain: all pi and pi* orbitals of the polyenic backbone. That gives CAS(6,6) for PSB3 and its methylated derivatives, CAS(8,8) for PSB4, and CAS(12,12) for the full retinal chromophore in the rhodopsin QM/MM model. A deliberate CAS(2,2) - HOMO and LUMO, pi and pi* only - was run alongside CAS(8,8) in XMS-CASPT2 scans of PSB4 specifically to isolate what the small active space of the REKS/SSR methods costs. The answer is directly useful: XMS-CASPT2(2,2) energy profiles resemble the REKS ones much more closely than XMS-CASPT2(8,8) does, especially along the C4=C5 coordinate, so the REKS discrepancies are substantially an active-space-size effect rather than purely a functional effect. Follow-up tests showed that increasing exact exchange (BHHLYP 50 percent, PBE-2X 54 percent, HFLYP 100 percent) brings SSR much closer to XMS-CASPT2(8,8), and that HF-REKS, which has no dynamic correlation, agrees better with CASSCF(2,2) than with any CASPT2 variant.

method: SA-CASSCF for geometry optimization and conical-intersection searches, with MRCI (with and without Davidson correction), MS-CASPT2 (0.2 level shift) and EOM-CCSD single points for the vertical excitation energies; natural population analysis and Wiberg bond indices for the electronic structure characterization

active_space_orbital_description: the eight pi orbitals and two oxygen lone-pair nO orbitals of the uracil fragment plus the six pi orbitals of the benzene fragment define the ideal 16-orbital space; the (20,14) space actually used for optimization drops two of these
active_space_protocol: A worked example of choosing an active space under a cost ceiling, with the reasoning spelled out. The chemically correct space is (20,16): eight pi plus two nO lone-pair orbitals on uracil, and six pi orbitals on benzene. That space generates 14 158 144 CSFs and 64 128 064 determinants and is affordable only for single points, not for geometry optimization or conical-intersection searches. Dropping the highest unoccupied orbital gives (20,15), 2 186 184 CSFs and 9 018 009 determinants, which the authors identify as the best compromise for vertical excitation energies - explicitly better than the alternative of transplanting the previously used reduced spaces for the separate fragments, (12,9) for uracil plus (6,6) for benzene, which would give (18,15). All geometry optimizations were then done at (20,14), the largest space they could afford for optimization, and MRCI and MS-CASPT2 single points were computed on top of it. 5BU has 106 electrons in 53 doubly occupied orbitals; during MCSCF optimization the lowest 43 orbitals were closed but still fully optimized, and for the correlated single points those same 43 were frozen.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: S0. Vertical excitation energies in eV, S1 (n-pi*) then S2 (pi-pi*), in the printed order of Table 2: SA-CASSCF(20,14) 4.85 / 7.92; SA-CASSCF(18,14) 4.94 / 5.34; SA-CASSCF(20,15) 5.02 / 7.02; SA-CASSCF(18,15) 4.94 / 5.21; SA-CASSCF(20,16) 4.94 (f = 0.003) / 7.10 (f = 0.571); MS-CASPT2(20,13) 5.02 / 6.83; MS-CASPT2(20,14) 4.93 / 6.28; MRCI(20,14) 5.08 / 7.12; MRCI+D(20,14) 5.11 / 6.90; EOM-CCSD 5.13 / 5.44; LT-DF-LCC2 4.94 / 5.07
Other: The active space controls S2 far more than S1. Removing two active electrons at fixed orbital count collapses S2 from 7.92 to 5.34 eV at (20,14) versus (18,14), and from 7.02 to 5.21 eV at (20,15) versus (18,15), while S1 moves by only 0.01-0.09 eV. Enlarging the virtual space from (20,15) to (20,16) shifts S2 only from 7.03 to 7.10 eV and leaves S1 unchanged, so the virtual orbitals matter much less than the occupied ones. Dynamic correlation then brings the CASSCF values of 6.93 and 8.48 eV down to 5.83 and 6.93 eV at MS-CASPT2. Because the saturated methylene bridge blocks pi communication between the two rings, the 5BU excited states track the isolated fragments closely: the first two excited states at 5.13 and 5.44 eV match isolated uracil (5.17 eV) and isolated benzene (5.30 eV), and the third and fourth lie at 5.78 and 6.55 eV. At the correlated level the uracil-benzene difference falls below 0.02 eV.

active_space_protocol: Full valence for ethane is 14 electrons in 14 orbitals, which produced a prohibitively large CASSCF-CI expansion, so a (10,10) was used instead by demoting the totally symmetric CH-bond combinations and their antibonding partners. The authors state they expect MRCI on (14,14) and on (10,10) to give very similar results. The paper's central and directly transferable active-space result: MRCI based on a CASSCF that puts only the electrons of the C-C or N-N bond itself in the active space reproduces full-valence CASSCF/MRCI very well. This worked because the bond orbitals could be cleanly distinguished from those involved in the C-H or N-H bonds. There is in fact more variation among full-valence MRCI results with the reference-selection threshold than between the two choices of active space. The small space carries a second practical advantage: full-valence MRCI and ACPF expansions were prohibitively long and required reference selection (keeping occupations whose spin-coupling coefficients exceeded about 0.05), whereas with the smaller spaces the entire CASSCF could be used as the reference with no selection at all. The authors judge their best numbers to be the ACPF values on the smaller active space, precisely because it avoids reference-selection error.
Other: Single-bonded reference case. The discrepancy between the single-reference MCPF and the multireference ACPF dissociation energies is only 0-1 kcal/mol for single bonds, rising to 3-4 kcal/mol for double bonds and about 6 kcal/mol for triple bonds - consistent with higher excitations mattering more as bond multiplicity increases. compound_name: Fe(II)-porphyrin model complex, quintet-triplet spin gap (5A1g vs 3Eg)
ligand_set: porphyrin macrocycle (four pyrrole N donors), four-coordinate ferrous porphyrin model
geometry_source: four-coordinate ferrous porphyrin model system from earlier work
method: FCIQMC-tailored distinguishable cluster (TDCSD) and tailored coupled cluster (TCCSD, TCCSD(T)), with perturbative F12 basis-set corrections, benchmarked against CASPT2, CCSD(T), DLPNO-CCSD(T1), MC-PDFT, diffusion Monte Carlo and DFT-PBE[U]
relativistic_treatment: semicore Fe (3s3p) correlation included in the coupled-cluster steps
active_space_orbital_description: largest space CAS(32,34): the entire porphyrin pi system plus the orbitals of CAS(14,18); progression of four spaces detailed in active_space_protocol
active_space_protocol: A four-space progression that is itself the key result. CAS(8,11): five Fe 3d orbitals, five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals and one sigma(Fe-N) bond. CAS(12,15): adds the four Gouterman pi frontier orbitals, shown to be crucial for stabilizing the triplet over the quintet. CAS(14,18): NOT an extension of (12,15) - instead it adds four Fe 4s4p orbitals and the remaining three sigma(Fe-N) bonds on top of (8,11), deliberately omitting the Gouterman pi orbitals. CAS(32,34): the largest, containing the entire pi system together with the CAS(14,18) orbitals. CAS(32,34) is too large for conventional CASSCF, so Stochastic-CASSCF optimized its orbitals. Active-space design for transition-metal spin gaps, stated explicitly: small CASSCF-optimized spaces are CAS(6,5) - the five Fe 3d orbitals with six electrons - and CAS(6,10), which adds the five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals to capture 3d double-shell correlation. Large spaces (over 30 electrons in 30+ orbitals) are built from DCSD natural orbitals whose occupations deviate strongly from 0 and 2, with the explicit requirement that both spin states get a similar space - if an orbital type matters for one spin state it is included for both, so the states are balanced. FCIQMC then supplies the CI vectors inside these large spaces to tailor the distinguishable-cluster/coupled-cluster amplitudes.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 3Eg (triplet), stabilized over 5A1g (quintet). Quintet-triplet spin gap dE = E(Q) - E(T), a few kcal/mol with the triplet below the quintet. At CAS(32,34): tailored TDCSD-F12a and TCCSD(T)-F12a both give 5.8 kcal/mol; recent Stochastic-MRCISD on the same CAS(32,34) (correlating 96 electrons in 159 orbitals) gives 6.8 kcal/mol; CCSD(T)-embedded CAS(32,34)+dF12 gives 5.7 and DCSD-embedded 3.6 kcal/mol. Largest doubles amplitude in CAS(32,34): 0.242 (LS/triplet) and 0.221 (HS/quintet) - much more multiconfigurational than the octahedral complexes.
Other: The clearest active-space lesson in the paper: the entire porphyrin pi system must be in the space to stabilize the triplet ground state. Smaller CASs erroneously predict a quintet ground state; only once the full pi system is included (via the Gouterman orbitals and ultimately CAS(32,34)) does the correct triplet-below-quintet ordering emerge, already at the Stochastic-CASSCF level, and tailoring plus F12 enlarges the gap further. Small active spaces demonstrably reduce tailored-method accuracy here - fixed amplitudes in a small space shrink the TCCSD(T) gap far below CCSD(T) - so large active spaces are indispensable when multiconfigurational character is high. All the large-CAS(32,34) tailored methods agree with each other to within a fraction of a kcal/mol.

compound_name: Nitrobenzene, photorelease of NO2 (and NO via a roaming mechanism) along the C-NO2 dissociation coordinate
geometry_source: stationary points and C-NO2 scans/minimum energy paths optimized at CASSCF(14,11); the 3(nB pi*) minimum was numerically reoptimized at CASPT2(14,11), which is itself the first point of a numerical CASPT2 minimum energy path from the CASSCF minimum
method: CASSCF and CASPT2 for the electronic structure with classical CASSCF (and CASPT2) dynamics; DFT-B3LYP for comparison
software: OpenMolcas for the wave function calculations; Gaussian16 for DFT-B3LYP
basis_set: ANO-L contracted to C,N[4s3p1d]/H[2s1p] for the wave function calculations; 6-311++G(d,p) for DFT
active_space_orbital_description: the well-tested 14-electron 11-orbital nitroaromatic pi/lone-pair space, extended by the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C-NO2 bond to give (16,13)
active_space_protocol: two spaces used in sequence: the well-established CAS(14,11) for the nitroaromatic system (used for most geometry optimizations and the classical dynamics), and CAS(16,13) for the final energetics, which adds the sigma and sigma* electrons and orbitals of the C-NO2 bond. The C-NO2 sigma/sigma* orbitals are the key addition because the mechanism is a C-NO2 bond dissociation - a (sigma sigma*) triplet state appears only at the stretched geometry and drives the cleavage.
electronic_structure_description: CASPT2(16,13) low-lying triplet energies (eV, relative to the ground-state minimum) at the first (C1-N7 = 1.47 A) and last (2.15 A) points of the C-NO2 scan, with the difference: 3(nA pi*) 3.22 / - ; 3(pi_O pi*) 3.45 / 5.70 (dE 2.25); 3(La pi pi*) 3.67 / 5.67 (dE 2.00); 3(nB pi*) 3.88 / 5.61 (dE 1.73); 3(sigma sigma*) - / 4.07. Experimentally NO2 products are detected after 280-222 nm excitation (4.43-5.58 eV).
Other: Mechanistic proposal: a triplet n-pi* state evolves toward C-NO2 elongation and eventually dissociates; it is the only low-lying excited state favoring that deformation. Along the triplet dissociation path the possibility of decay to the singlet ground state frustrates the dissociation and can drive rearrangement (nitro-to-nitrite isomerization) or recombination. The 3(sigma sigma*) state, absent near equilibrium, drops to 4.07 eV at 2.15 A and becomes the dissociative channel. NO2 was proposed to arise from nonradiative repopulation of a hot ground state via an S1/S0 conical intersection at a shorter C-NO2 distance; NO forms through a roaming mechanism. The ground-state C-NO2 distance is sensitive to dynamic correlation, which is why the triplet minimum was reoptimized at CASPT2 rather than CASSCF.
reference_short: A First Proposal on the Nitrobenzene Photorelease Mechanism of NO2 and Its Relation to NO Formation through a Roaming Mechanism, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. (2024)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. Metal-free organic (metal_center = none). A clear worked case of active-space extension driven by the chemistry: the standard (14,11) nitroaromatic space is augmented to (16,13) specifically to put the breaking C-NO2 sigma bond in the active space, without which the dissociative (sigma sigma*) triplet cannot be described.

compound_name: Ionic-character benchmark set: ethene, butadiene, hexatriene, octatetraene, naphthalene, pyridine, pyrimidine, triazine, acrolein, cyanoformaldehyde, cyclopentadienone (11 molecules, 34 singlet states)
geometry_source: ground-state geometries optimized at CC3/aug-cc-pVTZ
method: state-averaged CASSCF benchmarked against MR-CIS, MR-CISD and MR-CISD with Pople size-extensivity correction (MR-CISD+P), against CC3/theoretical-best-estimate references; the paper introduces the Qat diagnostic of ionic character computed from the transition density
active_space_orbital_description: minimal valence pi/pi* spaces per molecule (see protocol); the paper's whole point is that these minimal spaces fail for ionic states
active_space_protocol: Per-molecule minimal valence pi/pi* active spaces used with SA-CASSCF (states averaged listed in the paper's Table 1): ethene (2,2); butadiene (4,4); hexatriene (6,6); octatetraene (8,8); naphthalene (10,10) for SA-CASSCF/MR-CIS and (8,8) for MR-CISD; pyridine (8,7); pyrimidine (10,8); triazine (12,9); acrolein (6,5); cyanoformaldehyde (10,8); cyclopentadienone (8,7). The central lesson for active-space selection: a minimal pi/pi* CASSCF space overestimates the excitation energies of IONIC states (typically the La / Pariser '+' / bright HOMO-LUMO states) by about 1-2 eV, because ionic states require enhanced sigma-correlation that a pi-only space cannot provide, while COVALENT states (Lb / '-') are described well. Known remedies - doubling the pi active space, adding sigma orbitals, or changing the one-electron basis - all help but it is not obvious a priori when they are needed, and the error often resurfaces even after MRCI or CASPT2. The Qat diagnostic, computed from the transition density, quantifies ionic character and predicts which states will be problematic.
nroots_per_mult: varies per molecule; 34 singlet states total across the set
electronic_structure_description: Aggregate accuracy against theoretical best estimates (aug-cc-pVDZ): SA-CASSCF mean absolute error 0.87 eV for the 34 singlet states; MR-CIS reduces it, MR-CISD gives MAE/MSE 0.27/0.25 eV for singlets, and MR-CISD+P (Pople size-extensivity correction) gives an excellent MAE of 0.11 eV (MR-CISD+P singlet MAE/MSE 0.19/-0.07 eV). Triplet MAEs are largely unaffected by method because triplet states here are covalent. The SA-CASSCF errors correlate strongly with the Qat ionic-character diagnostic.
Other: The paper is a diagnostic/methodology study rather than a chemistry study, but it is unusually directly useful for active-space selection: it demonstrates quantitatively that the failure of minimal pi/pi* CASSCF is specific to ionic states, gives a per-molecule catalogue of which minimal spaces were used, and provides a transition-density metric (Qat) to flag in advance when a larger space or added sigma correlation is required. Ethene is the archetype - its ionic 1Bu singlet is badly overestimated by CAS(2,2) while its covalent 3Bu triplet is fine.
reference_short: Lischka and Plasser, Quantification of the Ionic Character of Multiconfigurational Wave Functions: The Qat Diagnostic, J. Phys. Chem. A 127, 9842 (2023)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. Metal-free organic set (metal_center = none). Directly relevant to the decision agent: gives the rule 'minimal pi/pi* fails by 1-2 eV for ionic states; add sigma or double the pi space' plus a way to predict when.

compound_name: Model systems for the state-specific CASSCF energy landscape: H2, methylene (CH2) conical intersection, and LiF avoided crossing
geometry_source: H2 at R = 1 a0; CH2 near its conical intersection; LiF across its avoided crossing - all illustrative single points/scans in a 6-31G basis
method: state-specific CASSCF (SS-CASSCF) versus state-averaged CASSCF (SA-CASSCF) and full CI, mapping all stationary points of the CASSCF energy landscape and characterizing their topology (Hessian index, spin contamination)
active_space_orbital_description: minimal (2,2) for H2; also (3,2) tested
active_space_protocol: The paper's transferable message about active-space sizing, stated as a dichotomy: unphysical stationary points on the CASSCF energy surface arise from REDUNDANT orbitals when the active space is too LARGE, and from SYMMETRY BREAKING when the active space is too SMALL. For H2/6-31G, a CAS(2,2) landscape has 25 stationary points (19 singlet, 6 triplet); every exact FCI state has a corresponding SS-CASSCF(2,2) solution, whereas SA-CASSCF(2,2) can only describe the lowest triplet and three lowest singlets, and enlarging to SA-CASSCF(3,2) reaches only the lowest nine excitations. XS-CASSCF is the corrective follow-up to this group's Qat ionic-character diagnostic (10.1021/acs.jpca.3c05559): SA-CASSCF overestimates singlet ionic pi-pi* states by 1-2 eV because the transition-density self-repulsion (two-electron exchange integrals) is not screened by sigma-correlation. XS-CASSCF scales those exchange terms down with two parameters [mu, nu] to mimic sigma-correlation at NO extra cost - mu scales the diagonal exchange (controls the ionic S1), nu the off-diagonal coupling (controls multiconfigurational covalent states). Practical guidance the paper establishes: mu = 0.0 (simply dropping the exchange integral g_pq,qp) is usually optimal and makes the S1 energy independent of the exchange integral, halving the CASSCF singlet-triplet gap to one exchange integral rather than two; nu = 0.0 is best when only the HOMO-LUMO transition matters, but nu = 0.5-0.7 is safer when higher multiconfigurational covalent states are of interest. The recommended default is [0.0, 0.5].

active_space_protocol: CAS(4,4): the four electrons and four frontier orbitals of the two-bond reorganization, validated against CAS(12,12)/def2-TZVP (occupation numbers agree to within 0.06). A useful active-space validation for pericyclic reactions. The electrocyclizations are studied with a minimal CAS(4,4) - the frontier pi/sigma orbitals and electrons directly involved in the bond being made/broken - at def2-SVP. The authors validated this against a much larger CASSCF(12,12)/def2-TZVP and found the natural-orbital occupation numbers almost identical (largest difference 0.06, for the LUMO of the disrotatory TS), concluding CAS(4,4)/def2-SVP is quantitatively adequate. Reaction energies come out ~5-6 kcal/mol above high-accuracy/experimental references. So for a symmetry-controlled electrocyclic reaction, a (4,4) space capturing the two bonds that change is enough - a helpful lower bound on active-space size for this reaction class.
Other: The four-electron electrocyclization. Modern re-examination of the Woodward-Hoffmann rules: the thermally allowed conrotatory path proceeds smoothly, while the forbidden disrotatory path shows an occupied-orbital level crossing (bonding HOMO to antibonding LUMO) that creates a diradical situation and a high barrier. method: RASSCF/RASPT2 with a highly-excited-state (HEXS) core-hole projection, plus a displaced-harmonic-oscillator (DHO) vibronic model for line shapes, to simulate XPS and XANES (K-edge) soft X-ray spectra to sub-eV accuracy

active_space_protocol: A detailed, transferable RAS active-space-selection recipe for core (X-ray) excitation/ionization, tested on 1,1-difluoroethene at the C K-edge. The space must contain: (i) the core orbital(s) of interest, placed in the subspace to which the HEXS core-hole projection is applied; (ii) virtual orbitals, chosen deliberately by the user - more virtuals give a more complete spectrum, since they are the arrival orbitals of the excited 1s electron and enable multiple-excitation intensity; (iii) occupied valence orbitals for correlation and shake-up states, where often just the highest occupied (HOMO) suffices. No molecular symmetry was imposed, to keep the recipe general.

Sub-eV accuracy against high-resolution experiment, with the DHO vibronic treatment quantitatively reproducing line shapes. The core-hole formation modulates (weakens or strengthens) bonds, rationalized via an ESCA-potential/chemical-shift picture.

The chemically ideal space is the full valence of Be3 - 12 electrons in the fifteen 2s/2p orbitals, CASSCF(12,15) - but with the large basis this gives >1.6e6 CSFs (D3h) and computationally intractable (>9e10 uncontracted CSFs) MRCI. Other: Binding energy 27.3 kcal/mol (aug-cc-pV5Z, CASSCF+AQCC), more stable than the linear isomer. The CASSCF(12,15) analysis shows the in-plane (2px, 2py) orbitals dominate the bonding of this equilateral form. The (12,15) reference generates >1.6 million CSFs in D3h symmetry; a CASSCF(12,14) reference reaches ~4.7e10 CSFs in the correlated treatment.

active_space_protocol: Active orbitals chosen by a natural-orbital-occupation-number (NOON) criterion — keep as active the MOs with NOONs between 0.02 and 1.98 in the state-averaged first-order density matrix, which is argued to give the lowest energy for a fixed CI expansion size. Applied strictly, this criterion gives a DIFFERENT space per reactive channel — (14,12) for the NO+NO channel and (12,10) for the N2+O2 channel — hence inconsistent at, e.g., reactants; the authors instead adopt a homogeneous space over the whole PES even where NOONs fall outside those limits, accepting spaces that are not strictly homogeneous, and aiming at the lowest-energy ground-PES stationary points (NOONs maximally different from 0.0/2.0). Full valence is not feasible for this system, so trial and error plus comparison with experiment was needed. Sequence: (14,12)B all 2p-derived MOs; (14,12)A swaps one for an N 2s MO — needed because nitrogen is a limiting case for which orbitals to make active; (18,14)A/B add two 2s(N,O) MOs (+4 electrons). At CASSCF, space A is clearly favoured for (14,12) and the A/B differences shrink for (18,14); once point-wise CASPT2 is applied all four spaces give similar results. B-type spaces were always used in products and describe some regions better

method: DMRG-SCF with MPSSI (matrix product state state interaction) and multi-state CASPT2, compared against equivalent CASSCF/CASSI; SINGLE_ANISO for magnetic properties; active space rationalized with the AutoCAS automated selection protocol
active_space_orbital_description: orbitals 4-10 are predominantly U 5f orbitals of the central U ion; orbitals 1-3 are mainly U 6p in character with small contributions from the N centres of the amido ligands. Orbital No. 8 (U 5f-delta) shows seemingly small orbital entanglement but is included automatically by the selection protocol because it is singly occupied in the electronic ground state
active_space_protocol: (1,7) the seven U 5f orbitals holding the single 5f electron; (7,10) additionally includes the three mainly U 6p orbitals (+6 electrons). Selection guided by the AUTOCAS state-averaged orbital entanglement diagram: the 5f-delta orbital No. 8 has low entanglement but is auto-included because it is singly occupied in the ground state, in agreement with scalar-relativistic DFT on the same model; the case for the 6p-based orbitals Nos. 1-3 is less clear-cut. Effect of going (1,7) -> (7,10): MS-CASPT2 excitation energies of the two sets of lowest-lying three-fold degenerate spin-free states drop by ~10% and ~5% respectively, and the isotropic ground-state g-factor moves from -1.06 to -1.10 (vs measured |g| = 1.12). (7,10) was also chosen small enough to permit a direct DMRG-SCF/MPSSI vs CASSCF/CASSI comparison, with the number of renormalized block states m set to reproduce CASSCF exactly for each space

electronic_structure_description: Two sets of lowest-lying three-fold degenerate spin-free states are discussed; their MS-CASPT2 excitation energies decrease by about 10% and 5% respectively on enlarging the active space from CAS(1,7) to CAS(7,10). Absolute excitation energies are not tabulated in this software-overview article, so no eV values are recorded here
Other: Magnetic properties (the point of the application): isotropic ground-state g-factor gxx = gyy = gzz = -1.06 with CAS(1,7) and -1.10 with CAS(7,10) at the DMRG-SCF/MS-PT2/MPSSI level, in very good agreement with the measured isotropic |g| = 1.12 for the real hexakisamidouranium(V) complex of their Ref. 124. Calculated effective magnetic moment mu_eff = 0.95 mu_B over 5-35 K, compared with mu_eff = 1.16 mu_B determined by SQUID measurements over the same temperature range for the larger experimental complex. This is presented as the first application of the MPSSI approach combining AutoCAS active-space selection with SINGLE_ANISO magnetic-property evaluation. The same article separately illustrates POLY_ANISO on Dy3 triangle single-molecule magnets (exchange-coupled polynuclear treatment), but without a stated active space for that system

compound_name: Nb3N2 cluster and its cation Nb3N2+ (niobium trimer dinitride)
ligand_set: 2 N atoms bound to a Nb3 triangle (bridging/triply bridging geometries discussed)
point_group: C2v (all calculations performed in C2v; note the arbitrary sigma_v/sigma_v' assignment means B1/B2 labels were swapped to make MOLPRO and GAUSSIAN output consistent)
geometry_source: full geometry optimizations of each electronic state up to the octet, performed in this work in C2v at both B3LYP/srsc (GAUSSIAN03) and CASSCF (MOLPRO-2006) levels
method: CASSCF (Werner-Meyer-Knowles) with single-point MRCI and MRCI+Q (Davidson correction), compared against B3LYP DFT
software: MOLPRO-2006 for CASSCF/MRCI; GAUSSIAN03 for DFT
basis_set: Nb: Stuttgart (srsc) basis with quasirelativistic ECP replacing the first 28 electrons; N: cc-pVDZ. For basis-set tests on the ground states, Dunning bases cc-pVDZ to aug-cc-pVTZ on N with a (10s9p8d2f1g)/[5s5p4d2f1g] basis on Nb
relativistic_treatment: quasirelativistic effective core potential on Nb (first 28 electrons replaced)
active_space_orbital_description: final active space is the 3a1, 2a2, 2b1 and 3b2 orbitals (10 orbitals) lying above the closed 9a1/2a2/5b1/5b2 set, holding 11 electrons (10 for the cation). Nb 4s/4p and N 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are always doubly occupied
active_space_protocol: Explicit reduction from a full valence space: the full valence active space of Nb3N2/Nb3N2+ is 40 orbitals in C2v (16a1, 5a2, 13b1, 6b2), which gives an intractable number of CSFs. First reduction — the Nb 4s and 4p and N 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are frozen closed (doubly occupied). The remaining 26 orbitals were still too large, so preliminary CASSCF calculations with a large active space were run and used as a screen: orbitals doubly occupied in ALL configurations were made closed, and high-energy orbitals not occupied in ANY configuration were removed. The resulting space closes the lowest 9a1, 2a2, 5b1, 5b2 and makes active the next 3a1, 2a2, 2b1, 3b2 — 11 electrons (10 for the cation) in 10 orbitals, totalling 7000 CSFs. No excitations were allowed from the closed orbitals but they were allowed to relax. In the MRCI, all CASSCF configurations with absolute coefficients >= 0.05 were used as references, giving up to 125 million configurations
multiplicities_studied: 1,2,3,4 — neutral: doublets and quartets at MRCI (geometries optimized for all states up to the octet, 2S+1 = 8); cation: singlets and triplets at MRCI (up to septet optimized)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2B2 for neutral Nb3N2 (1A1 for Nb3N2+). The MRCI leading configuration of each ground state agrees with DFT but accounts for only up to 70% of the total wave function. Excited states of neutral Nb3N2 (eV above ground state): B3LYP puts three states (2A1, 4B2, 4B1) 0.64-0.94; CASSCF puts the first three (2A1, 4B2, 2A2) at 1.0 <= dE <= 1.2; at MRCI and MRCI+Q the 2A1 and 2A2 states rise sharply and only 4B2 remains below 2 eV, so 4B2 is the true first excited state. The 4B2 leading configuration is obtained from the 2B2 ground configuration by exciting an electron from 11a1 into 12a1 and is only 54% of the MRCI wave function. The Nb3N2+ ground 1A1 state is highly multireference with three major configurations. Adiabatic ionization potential (2B2 -> 1A1, removing the unpaired 7b2 electron): experiment 5.44315 eV (ZEKE origin at 43901.7 cm-1, their Ref. 10); this work B3LYP 5.67; MRCI 4.55 and MRCI+Q 4.80 with the smallest basis, MRCI 4.51 with cc-pVTZ on Nb (MRCI+Q unchanged to 3 s.f.); increasing the N basis quality did not affect the IPs
Other: Central finding: transition energies between the neutral and cationic manifolds are predicted POORLY by MRCI relative to the computationally cheap DFT — the MRCI/MRCI+Q adiabatic IPs sit ~0.6-0.9 eV below the very precisely measured ZEKE value while B3LYP is within ~0.23 eV. Adding unlinked quadruple excitations (Davidson) raises the IP by 0.25 eV but not enough. Literature DFT comparisons for the IP: BP86 (ADF) and LSDA (DEMON) both 5.60 eV; B3P86 (GAUSSIAN94) 6.37 eV, ~1 eV too high, consistent with that functional's known 0.3-1.0 eV overestimation. CASSCF and DFT geometries are in general agreement. At CASSCF, the 8A2, 4B1 and 2B1 states are the only ones with triply bridging geometries. A CASSCF-vs-MRCI discrepancy of 2.75 versus 4.75 eV is noted for one state. Geometric, frequency and energetic data for all species are in the supplementary material

compound_name: Nb3C2 cluster and its cation Nb3C2+ (niobium trimer dicarbide), doubly bridging (DB) and triply bridging (TB) isomers
ligand_set: 2 C atoms bound to a Nb3 triangle, in doubly bridging (DB) and triply bridging (TB) arrangements
point_group: C2v (all calculations in C2v; B1/B2 labels swapped for MOLPRO to match GAUSSIAN, see companion row -a)
geometry_source: full geometry optimizations of each electronic state up to the octet, performed in this work in C2v at both B3LYP/srsc (GAUSSIAN03) and CASSCF (MOLPRO-2006) levels; triply bound structures have angle(Nb'NbNbC) < 75 deg with approximately equal Nb-C and Nb'-C bond lengths
method: CASSCF (Werner-Meyer-Knowles) with single-point MRCI and MRCI+Q (Davidson correction), compared against B3LYP DFT
software: MOLPRO-2006 for CASSCF/MRCI; GAUSSIAN03 for DFT
basis_set: Nb: Stuttgart (srsc) basis with quasirelativistic ECP replacing the first 28 electrons; C: cc-pVDZ
relativistic_treatment: quasirelativistic effective core potential on Nb (first 28 electrons replaced)
active_space_orbital_description: final active space is the 4a1, 1a2, 2b1 and 3b2 orbitals (10 orbitals) above the closed 9a1/2a2/5b1/5b2 set, holding 9 electrons (8 for the cation). Nb 4s/4p and C 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are always doubly occupied
active_space_protocol: Same reduction strategy as for Nb3N2 (companion row -a): the full valence active space of Nb3C2/Nb3C2+ is the same 40 orbitals in C2v (16a1, 5a2, 13b1, 6b2), too large to use directly. The Nb 4s and 4p and C 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are frozen closed; preliminary CASSCF calculations with a large active space then identified which further orbitals to close (doubly occupied in all configurations) or discard (unoccupied in all configurations), leaving the lowest 9a1, 2a2, 5b1, 5b2 closed and the next 4a1, 1a2, 2b1, 3b2 active — 9 electrons (8 for the cation) in 10 orbitals, 7000 CSFs. Note the a1/a2 split differs from the Nb3N2 case (4a1,1a2 here versus 3a1,2a2 there) even though both end at 10 active orbitals. No excitations from the closed orbitals, but they were allowed to relax; MRCI references are all CASSCF configurations with absolute coefficients >= 0.05
multiplicities_studied: 1,2,3,4 — neutral: doublets and quartets at MRCI (all states up to the octet optimized); cation: singlets and triplets at MRCI (up to septet)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2B2 (B3LYP/srsc global minimum, a triply bridging structure). Unlike Nb3N2, Nb3C2 has low-energy doubly AND triply bound structures. At B3LYP the ground-state assignment is ambiguous — four states lie within 0.55 eV, two of them transition states; the two lowest excited states are 3B1 at 0.40 eV and 1B1 at 0.51 eV, both triply bridging. At CASSCF and MRCI+Q the assignment is unambiguous: the next lowest states are 3B2 at 0.62 eV and 1B2 at 0.63 eV, both doubly bridging, and the lowest triply bridging states are 5A1 at 1.51 eV and 3B1 at 1.59 eV (CASSCF). A triply bridging 2A1 search located a transition state with one short and two long Nb-Nb bonds, separated from the 2B2 state by only 1e-5 hartree, indicating Jahn-Teller components of a distorted D3h structure. Ionization potentials (eV, srsc on Nb / cc-pVDZ on C) vs experiment 5.04 (their Ref. 11): MRCI (TB) 2A1 -> 1A1 4.56, MRCI+Q 4.69; MRCI (DB) 2A1 -> 3A2 4.55, MRCI+Q 5.07; B3LYP (TB) 2B2 -> 1A1 5.13; B3LYP (DB) 2B2 -> 1A1 5.93 and 2B2 -> 3A2 5.75
Other: Main chemical conclusion for this cluster: a higher-energy isomer of Nb3C2 may have an electronic transition in the same spectral vicinity as the lowest-energy isomer, which matters for interpreting the observed spectrum (the Nb3C2 spectrum has much richer vibronic structure than Nb3N2). The DB/TB isomer barrier lies between 0.05 and 0.10 eV. As for Nb3N2, DFT electronic configurations agree universally with the MRCI leading configurations, but those leading configurations contribute no more than 70% of the total wave function. One MRCI+Q IP agreeing with experiment is described by the authors as 'fortuitously close'

point_group: C2v used for the state-averaged CASSCF (irreps A1, A2, B1, B2)
geometry_source: ground-state equilibrium geometry optimized in this work; computed R(IBr) = 2.467 (Def2QZVP), 2.460 (aug-cc-pVQZ-PP), 2.473 (ANO-RCC-VQZP), 2.472 A (Sapporo-DKH3-QZP) vs experimental 2.469 A
method: SA-CASSCF / MS-CASPT2 with IPEA shift 0.25 a.u. / SO-RASSI (spin-orbit restricted-active-space state interaction); spin-free and spin-orbit states both reported
software: MOLCAS-family (CASSCF/MS-CASPT2/SO-RASSI approach; program not named explicitly in the extracted text)
basis_set: compared across four: Def2QZVP, aug-cc-pVQZ-PP (ECP), ANO-RCC-VQZP (all-electron) and Sapporo-DKH3-QZP-2012 (all-electron)
relativistic_treatment: all-electron relativistic bases (ANO-RCC, Sapporo-DKH3) and ECP-based bases (aug-cc-pVQZ-PP) compared
active_space_orbital_description: sigma_p and sigma_p* (I 5pz +/- Br 4pz), 2 pi_p and 2 pi_p* (I 5px/y +/- Br 4px/y), 2 pi_d (I 5dxz/yz - Br 4dxz/yz), 2 delta and 2 delta* (I 5dxy/x2-y2 +/- Br 4dxy/x2-y2), and sigma_d (I 5dz2 + Br 4dz2)
active_space_protocol: Active space chosen by combining three sources of information: recommendations from previous theoretical studies, the occupation numbers of quasi-canonical orbitals from initial MP2 computations, and the occupation numbers of natural orbitals from several trial CASSCF computations with different active spaces. This yielded CAS(10,13) for IBr, much larger than in previous theoretical work. Earlier studies used an active space of the Br 4p and I 5p shells only — (10 electrons, 6 orbitals) — or that plus the Br 4d shell — (10,11); the authors note those give good agreement with experiment but argue the iodine 5d orbitals deserve inclusion, giving more symmetric active spaces. Caveat stated by the authors: for a balanced description at the dissociation limit the CAS should include non-truncated p and d shells; since the aim here is transitions at and near the ground-state equilibrium geometry, the CAS was optimised for that region instead
nroots_per_mult: 6 averaged roots in each irrep of C2v (A1, A2, B1, B2)
Other: The 2.44 eV experimental band is only recovered once spin-orbit coupling is included — it corresponds to the (2)0+ (1 3Pi_0+) SO state — which is the central methodological point: SOC is essential for these heavy interhalogens. Deviations of the computed maxima from experiment are not higher than 0.16 eV. Basis-set sensitivity is modest: for the ECP-containing basis sets the VEE and f values do not change appreciably. Oscillator strengths of the SO states vary over orders of magnitude between basis sets for the weakly allowed transitions

Other: Thermodynamics and transition temperatures. Computed Delta_S_HL(T1/2) (J K-1 mol-1), Delta_H_HL (cm-1), experimental Delta_H_HL, computed T1/2 (K) and experimental T1/2: [Fe(mtz)6]2+ 29 / 69 / 120 / 28 / 78 (and 63); [Fe(iso)6]2+ 35 / 149 / - / 41 / 91 (site A); Fe(phen)2(NCS)2 55 / 568 / 719 / 136 / 176; [Fe(pic)3]2+ 51 / 349 / 744 / 82 / 114-121; [Fe(bpy)3]2+ 84 / 5138 / ~6000 / 727 / >450; [Fe(terpy)2]2+ 93 / 7097 / - / 911 / -. compound_name: HXeC2H (H-Xe-C(triple)C-H, xenon-inserted acetylene) and the parent acetylene HC2H — excited states underlying the linear and nonlinear optical (L&NLO) properties

active_space_protocol: Different active spaces were tested to assure the reliability of the results; the final calculations use CASSCF(10,14) comprising 3 sigma, 2 pi, 3 sigma*, 2 pi* valence orbitals plus four Rydberg orbitals (one s, three p). The Rydberg orbitals matter here because the lowest excited state of HXeC2H involves a sigma(Xe-H)* antibonding orbital with diffuse Rydberg-like s character. Separately, CASSCF calculations on the ground states of all studied molecules confirmed that a single electronic configuration dominates the wave function by at least 87%, justifying the single-reference MP2/CCSD(T) treatment of the L&NLO properties

By contrast, in acetylene the low-lying pi-sigma* state (sigma mainly the antibonding CC orbital) is expected above 9.0 eV. Acetylene excitation energies compare favourably with other experimental and theoretical values

Bonding analysed with CASVB, whose nonorthogonal VB orbitals allow maximum localization without loss of accuracy relative to CASSCF. Effect of Xe core electrons tested by correlating 18 versus 26 electrons explicitly, giving practically the same properties. Experimental harmonic frequencies for H-Xe-C(triple)C-H: 3273, 1748, 1486, 626 cm-1

compound_name: O2-O2 van der Waals complex — triplet states of O2(X 3Sigma_g-) with O2(X 3Sigma_g-, a 1Delta_g, b 1Sigma_g+); collision-induced absorption
point_group: benchmarks at high-symmetry geometries (H-shaped: theta_A = theta_B = pi/2, phi = 0); full surfaces computed at general low-symmetry geometries
geometry_source: global potential energy and dipole moment surfaces computed as functions of the intermolecular separation R and the three angles; the H-shaped geometry at R = 6 a0 corresponds to the minimum of the triplet O2(X)-O2(X) potential
method: explicitly correlated multireference configuration interaction with Davidson size-consistency correction (F12-MRCI+Q) for the potentials; dipole surfaces at both MRCI and CASSCF; F12-CASPT2 also used for benchmarks. Potentials and dipole surfaces transformed to a diabatic basis with a multiple-property-based diabatization algorithm
basis_set: augmented correlation-consistent aug-cc-pVnZ (n = D, T, Q) with the corresponding standardized auxiliary basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: three nested spaces: sCAS = four electrons in the four pi* orbitals; mCAS = 12 electrons in the pi shell; lCAS = 16 electrons in the p shell. The orbital counts for mCAS and lCAS are not given numerically
active_space_protocol: Three explicitly defined choices, used as a convergence ladder: (1) sCAS — four electrons in the four pi* orbitals, the MINIMAL active space that gives a zeroth-order description of all states of interest, i.e. all states arising from the (pi)4(pi*)2 configuration of the O2 monomers; (2) mCAS — 12 electrons in the pi shell, which additionally captures the static correlation of the pi electrons, important for O2 because of the well-known Hartree-Fock instability associated with artificial breaking of inversion symmetry; (3) lCAS — 16 electrons in the p shell. lCAS is prohibitively expensive at low-symmetry geometries, so the full potential energy and dipole moment surfaces could NOT be computed with it; mCAS is the production space for the surfaces, with lCAS used only for benchmarks at high-symmetry geometries. Benchmarking shows the interaction energy converges reasonably smoothly, albeit slowly, with active space and basis set, so accurate energies are obtainable from affordable MRCI; the transition dipole moment behaves quite differently and depends strongly on the level of theory. Prior systematic work (their Ref. 18) comparing MRCI, CASPT2 and ACPF against CCSD(T) for the high-spin quintet suggests treating MRCI and CASPT2 as upper and lower limits to the potential respectively, with CASPT2 the more reliable; MRCI is nevertheless used here because it gives straightforward access to the transition properties needed for the dipole surface and the diabatization
multiplicities_studied: 3 (seven triplet states of the dimer); monomer states X 3Sigma_g-, a 1Delta_g, b 1Sigma_g+
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: triplet O2(X 3Sigma_g-)-O2(X 3Sigma_g-). Seven triplet states of the dimer are treated. The monomer transitions underlying the collision-induced bands are X 3Sigma_g- -> a 1Delta_g at 7883 cm-1 and X 3Sigma_g- -> b 1Sigma_g+ at 13 122 cm-1. Interaction energies for the seven triplet states are tabulated at the H-shaped geometry at R = 6 a0 using F12-MRCI+Q with all three active spaces and with mCAS F12-CASPT2, but the individual values are not reproduced here
Other: For the triplet ground state of the complex the potential energy surface agrees reasonably with previous calculations, while global EXCITED state potentials are reported here for the first time. Central caveat: the transition dipole moment surfaces depend strongly on the level of theory at which they are computed, as confirmed by the high-symmetry benchmarks, so the authors conclude that ab initio calculations of collision-induced absorption spectra cannot become quantitatively predictive until more accurate transition dipoles are available. The paper also derives the angular expansion of the surfaces and the symmetry constraints on the expansion coefficients, gives working equations for obtaining them by numerical integration over angles, and presents an interpolation scheme with exponential extrapolation to short and large separations for the R dependence

compound_name: furan (C4H4O) — photoionization from the ground and excited electronic states, at planar and bent geometries
point_group: C2v for the ground-state (planar) geometry; a bent geometry is also treated
geometry_source: ground-state (planar, C2v) geometry and a bent geometry; the same active space was selected for both
method: CASSCF with NEVPT2 (partially contracted, PC(2) level) corrections for residual dynamical correlation, used to build Dyson orbitals; TDDFT and ADC(2) also used for comparison; continuum dipole matrix elements from a B-spline static-exchange DFT scattering treatment
software: MOLPRO for the HF, CASSCF and NEVPT2 calculations (plus in-house modules); Turbomole for TDDFT and ADC(2)
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ (polarization and diffuse functions) for O, C and H; Dyson orbitals projected onto a B-spline basis
active_space_orbital_description: six valence electrons distributed among nine orbitals: one a1, four b1, one b2 and three a2 — comprising 3 occupied (1b1-2b1, 1a2) and 6 virtual (1a1, 3b1-4b1, 7b2, 2a2-3a2)
active_space_protocol: (6,9) used throughout, itemized by irrep (one a1, four b1, one b2, three a2; 3 occupied + 6 virtual), and deliberately kept IDENTICAL for the bent geometry so that planar and bent results are directly comparable. No build-up sequence. Both excitation and ionization energies are then corrected for residual dynamical correlation via partially contracted PC(2)-NEVPT2. For the Dyson orbitals, the overlap between CASSCF wave functions separately optimized for the neutral molecule and for the ion is evaluated, with the N-electron wave function expanded in minors
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet in C2v. The valence-shell molecular orbital sequence of ground-state furan is (4a1)2(5a1)2(3b2)2(4b2)2(6a1)2(7a1)2(1b1)2... The paper's quantitative outputs are photoionization cross sections and asymmetry parameters computed from Dyson orbitals rather than a table of vertical excitation energies, so no eV state energies are transcribed here. Ionization energies calculated with the NEVPT2 approach are described as in excellent agreement (with experiment/previous work)
Other: Methodological point: Dyson orbitals are computed at three levels — TDDFT, ADC(2) and CASSCF — and then projected onto a B-spline basis, which decouples the Dyson orbital calculation from that of the continuum dipole matrix elements and lets different electronic structure methods be used interchangeably. The B-spline static-exchange DFT scattering procedure gives a quantitative description of dynamical photoionization observables and generally agrees excellently with experiment. Photoionization from excited electronic states, as well as from the ground state, is treated — relevant to time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy

compound_name: NO + O2 scattering system — multistate electronic quenching of NO A 2Sigma+ by O2, nonadiabatic pathways
point_group: C1 used for the potential energy surfaces in general orientations (unless specified otherwise); Jacobi coordinates used throughout
geometry_source: potential energy surfaces computed in this work over Jacobi coordinates; asymptotic state ordering evaluated at R = 15 A with fixed monomer bond lengths (O2 1.0634 A)
method: state-averaged CASSCF (SA(20)-CASSCF) for the potential energy surfaces, chosen because it models nonadiabatic effects and multiconfigurational character accurately; XMS-CASPT2 with IPEA level shift 0.25 for dynamic correlation; a spline/switched (SW-)CASSCF variant also used
basis_set: t-aug-cc-pVTZ for the SA-CASSCF(19,13) surfaces; t-aug-cc-pVDZ for the XMS-CASPT2(11,9) calculations
active_space_orbital_description: NO and O2 2sigma*, 3sigma, pi_x, pi_y, pi*_x, pi*_y orbitals plus the NO 4sigma orbital, giving CAS(19,13). The reduced space contains only the pi and pi* orbitals together with the NO 4sigma orbital, giving (11,9)
active_space_protocol: (19,13) — NO and O2 2sigma*, 3sigma, pi_x, pi_y, pi*_x, pi*_y plus NO 4sigma — used for the CASSCF potential energy surfaces, with a schematic of the orbital energetic ordering at asymptotic separation given in the paper. (11,9) — only the pi and pi* orbitals plus NO 4sigma — used for the XMS-CASPT2 calculations purely because the full space is too expensive at the CASPT2 level. The number of states is coupled to the active-space choice: because the O2 a 1Delta_g and b 1Sigma_g+ states lie BELOW the NO A 2Sigma+ state, the NO X 2Pi degeneracy couples with the O2 X, a and b states, producing eight doublet and two quartet surfaces below NO A 2Sigma+ + O2 X 3Sigma_g-. The active-space/number-of-states combination was therefore fixed for the spin-doublet states first, giving a minimum of 9 spin-doublet states required, and the production runs used a 20-state average. An IPEA level shift of 0.25 was applied to compensate the usual CASPT2 bias
multiplicities_studied: 2,4 — 2 and 4 (eight doublet and two quartet surfaces below the entrance channel)
nroots_per_mult: SA(20)-CASSCF (20-state average); minimum of 9 spin-doublet states required by the state-ordering analysis
electronic_structure_description: Asymptotic state ordering (R = 15 A, fixed bond lengths), energies in eV, SW-CASSCF then XMS-CASPT2, labelled by NO state / O2 state: A 2Sigma+ / b 1Sigma_g+ 5.569 (CASSCF); X 2Pi / A 3Sigma_u 5.267 / 6.670; X 2Pi / A' 3Delta_u 5.128 / 6.522; A 2Sigma+ / a 1Delta_g 5.095 / 5.582; X 2Pi / c 1Sigma_u- 4.978 / 6.313. Computed with SA(20)-CASSCF(19,13)/t-aug-cc-pVTZ and XMS-CASPT2(11,9)/t-aug-cc-pVDZ
Other: The paper examines how dynamic correlation affects the accessibility and relaxation of the quenching event — comparing SW-CASSCF and XMS-CASPT2 shows dynamic correlation raises the X 2Pi-based channels by roughly 1.3-1.4 eV while affecting the A 2Sigma+/a 1Delta_g channel much less (5.095 -> 5.582 eV), i.e. it substantially reorders the quenching channels. O2 c 1Sigma_u- was suggested by Few et al. (their Ref. 9) as a potential quenching product, which is why the state selection was built around the spin-doublet manifold. Triply augmented Dunning basis sets were chosen as optimized for modelling electronic correlation

compound_name: Model phenylalanine protein chains: NAPA B (N-acetylphenylalaninylamide), Ac-Gly-Phe-NH2 A, and Ac-Gln-Phe-NH2 C — singlet pipi* and npi* excited states
geometry_source: conformers of the model peptide chains (the NAPA B conformer corresponds to a specific folded structure, see their Fig. 1 and Ref. 6)
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 with RASSCF, GASSCF and ORMAS (occupation-restricted multiple active space) as determinant-reduction alternatives beyond the CASSCF limit; RASPT2 and Q+DDCI (difference-dedicated CI) for dynamic correlation; benchmarked against CC2
software: MOLCAS for RASSCF/GASSCF (with DoLo orbital localization and Cholesky decomposition, threshold 1e-8 a.u.); GAMESS for ORMAS (with Pipek-Mezey localization)
basis_set: cc-pVDZ throughout; cc-pVTZ also tested for NAPA B (CASSCF/CASPT2, Q+DDCI and CC2) but the effects were weak at very high computational cost, so cc-pVDZ was retained for the other systems
active_space_orbital_description: all the pi and pi* orbitals of the phenyl and of the carbonyl groups, plus the nitrogen and oxygen lone pairs (the highest in energy, i.e. the pure-p lone pair). This is what is required to describe the low-lying local excitations: pi -> pi* centred on the phenyl group and n -> pi*(CO) centred on the peptide bonds
active_space_protocol: Active space built from the states that must be described — all phenyl and carbonyl pi/pi* orbitals plus the pure-p N and O lone pairs — and it then scales with the number of peptide bonds: CAS(18,14) for NAPA B (4 008 004 determinants), CAS(24,18) for Ac-Gly-Phe-NH2 A with one more peptide bond (344 622 096 determinants, 'cumbersome but still tractable'), and CAS(30,22) for Ac-Gln-Phe-NH2 C with two more (29 085 255 936 determinants, UNFEASIBLE). Beyond the CASSCF limit three determinant-reduction strategies are benchmarked: (i) RASSCF with subspaces (18,n,n; 9,0,5), (24,n,n; 12,0,6) and (30,n,n; 15,0,7) for the three systems — note RAS2 is empty, all orbitals sit in RAS1/RAS3 — giving for n = 3/4/5 respectively 36 916 (0.9%) / 243 376 (6.1%) / 905 128 (22.6%) determinants for NAPA B, 158 669 (0.05%) / 1 787 219 (0.5%) / 11 577 923 (3.4%) for Ac-Gly-Phe-NH2 A, and 510 546 (0.002%) / 8 812 371 (0.03%) / 89 200 497 (0.3%) for Ac-Gln-Phe-NH2 C; (ii) GASSCF/ORMAS partitioning into (6,6)/(6,4) blocks — (6,6)/(6,4)/(6,4) for NAPA B (220 192 det, 5.5%), with one extra (6,4) block per additional peptide bond, giving 5 510 848 (1.6%) and 140 843 008 (0.5%) for the larger two. Percentages are relative to the full CASSCF determinant count. Orbital localization (DoLo or Pipek-Mezey) is required because orbitals must be assigned to distinct subspaces. In RASSCF the orbitals with notably varying occupation numbers must be placed in RAS2
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet. The low-lying excited states are local excitations: singlet pi -> pi* centred on the phenyl group and singlet n -> pi*(CO) centred on the peptide bonds (n being N or O pure-p lone pairs). Vertical excitation energies for Ac-Gly-Phe-NH2 A around 5.6-6.1 eV are tabulated across the different optimized-MO sets (RASSCF with n = 3, 4, 5; GASSCF MOs; CASSCF MOs) at the RASPT2, CASPT2 and Q+DDCI levels — e.g. CAS(12,8)-based values of 5.72, 5.61, 5.76, 5.67, 5.68 eV for one state across the five MO sets, and rows at 5.82/5.82/5.84/5.83/5.82 and 6.05/6.02/6.05/6.03/6.02 eV, with CAS1/CAS2 entries at 5.89/5.77/5.92/5.85/5.83 eV. The paper's conclusion is that these alternative schemes reproduce both the nature and the excitation energies of the singlet pipi* and npi* states without loss of accuracy relative to full CASSCF
Other: The point of the paper is active-space scaling: it quantifies how far the determinant count can be cut (to 0.002%-23% of full CASSCF) while preserving excited-state accuracy, which is exactly the regime where CASSCF becomes unaffordable for biomolecular chromophores. CC2 is assessed as an alternative for such large systems. Dynamic electron correlation is noted to be a local effect, motivating the localized-orbital subspace partitioning. Published in the JCP Special Collection in Honor of Women in Chemical Physics and Physical Chemistry

compound_name: TTF+ — tetrathiafulvalene monoradical cation, UV/Vis absorption spectrum
point_group: D2h (states labelled 1 2B1u, 2 2B1u, 2 2B2u, 4 2B2u, 5 2B2u, 8 2B1u; singly occupied active b3u orbital)
geometry_source: optimized with PBE0 (structure provided in the supplementary material; their Ref. 71)
method: MC-RPA (multiconfigurational random phase approximation, i.e. CASSCF linear response) compared with SA-CASSCF and SS-NEVPT2; AO-driven integral-direct implementation with natural transition orbitals for analysis
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(13,10) includes all pi orbitals and electrons (13 860 CSFs), well suited to describe the delocalization of the unpaired electron in the pi system; the singly occupied active orbital is of b3u symmetry. The augmented CAS(21,14) additionally contains four nonbonding orbitals at the sulfur atoms
active_space_protocol: CAS(13,10) — all pi orbitals and electrons, 13 860 CSFs — used for all multireference calculations. Its sufficiency was TESTED by running an augmented SA-CASSCF with CAS(21,14) that adds the four sulfur nonbonding orbitals, which could in principle give n -> pi* excitations: that test showed the low-energy n -> pi* excitations are all dipole-forbidden, so CAS(13,10) suffices to describe every characteristic electronic transition of TTF+. A second reason for excluding the sulfur nonbonding orbitals is convergence trouble in the SS-CASSCF energy minimization preceding MC-RPA; consistently, in the ground-state SS-CASSCF the four largest natural occupation numbers are nearly 2.0 because those orbitals take no part in the delocalization of the electron hole. In the SA-CASSCF the MOs were optimized for an average of the 30 lowest states
nroots_per_mult: 30 (SA-CASSCF orbitals averaged over the 30 lowest states)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: doublet radical cation with a singly occupied b3u orbital. The experimental spectrum (recorded in acetonitrile, their Ref. 77) shows three shouldered peaks between 2.0 and 4.0 eV. All three multireference treatments (MC-RPA, SA-CASSCF, NEVPT2) reproduce three characteristic peaks — 1 2B1u, 2 2B1u and 2 2B2u — falling near that window, allowing a tentative assignment; the singly occupied b3u orbital acts as electron donor or acceptor in all three low-energy transitions. For these three transitions both MC-RPA and NEVPT2 give excitation energies much LOWER than SA-CASSCF, as they do for the 5 2B2u NEVPT2 transition corresponding to the 4 2B2u MC-RPA one. The 8 2B1u SA-CASSCF transition is lowered by 1.39 eV (MC-RPA) and 1.99 eV (NEVPT2). In general MC-RPA and NEVPT2 lie below SA-CASSCF because of orbital relaxation and dynamic correlation respectively, and both agree better with experiment
Other: Method caveats stated by the authors: neither MC-RPA nor NEVPT2 is optimal for describing many excited states and their spectral properties — MC-RPA misses a large fraction of the dynamic correlation not captured by the CSFs in the active space, while NEVPT2 describes orbital relaxation only in a limited sense through redundancies. The experiment/theory comparison is only a rough estimate because TTF+ was measured in acetonitrile, a polar solvent that stabilizes the positive charge, while the calculations are in vacuum. The largest COSX grid was needed to avoid trailing convergence issues associated with the large high-angular-momentum diffuse basis

compound_name: Octahedrally coordinated Ni(II) complex with triazole ligands (231 atoms) — absorption and ECD spectra
ligand_set: triazole ligands, octahedral coordination
geometry_source: structure from Schweinfurth et al. (their Ref. 71)
method: CASSCF linear response (MC-RPA) in an efficient AO-driven implementation, used to simulate absorption and electronic circular dichroism (ECD) spectra of a 231-atom complex
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(2,2) containing the Ni dx2-y2 and dz2 orbitals, in accordance with the ligand-field picture for octahedral Ni(II) d8 complexes — i.e. the two eg-derived orbitals holding the two unpaired electrons. The larger CAS(8,5) contains all five d orbitals and eight d electrons
active_space_protocol: The paper deliberately uses a SMALLER space than previous work on this complex: a CAS(2,2) with a single CSF comprising the Ni dx2-y2 and dz2 orbitals, following the ligand-field picture for octahedral Ni(II) d8, i.e. a restricted open-shell high-spin wave function. The full d-shell alternative, CAS(8,5) with all d orbitals and electrons, was tried for the triplet ground state but gave three d orbitals (dxy, dyz, dxz) with natural occupation numbers of exactly 2.0 and converged slowly — those orbitals are doubly occupied and contribute no static correlation in this ligand field. For that reason the CASSCF response calculations are shown only for the CAS(2,2) restricted open-shell high-spin wave function. This is a useful negative result: for an octahedral d8 ion the t2g set is inert and enlarging the CAS to the full d shell buys nothing but convergence trouble
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: triplet — the energetically lowest spin state of this Ni(II) complex, as established by the CASSCF and NEVPT2 calculations of Schweinfurth et al. (Ref. 71) and Guo et al. (Ref. 17). Absorption and ECD spectra are simulated with CASSCF linear response; individual excitation energies are presented graphically rather than tabulated in the extracted text, so no eV values are recorded here
Other: This calculation is the paper's demonstration that the AO-driven CASSCF linear response implementation scales to genuinely large open-shell systems — 231 atoms with a def2-TZVPP basis — which is the practical claim of the method. Reported alongside the TTF+ benchmark (companion row -a)

compound_name: s-trans-1,3-butadiene — excited-state potential energy curves along the terminal twist coordinate
geometry_source: scan along a terminal twist coordinate with all other bonds and angles frozen at their S2 planar minimum values
method: SA-CASSCF compared with dynamically weighted CASSCF using a new dynamical-weight-with-spline (DWS) scheme; analytical gradients for DWS-CASSCF derived for the first time, enabling energy-conserving excited-state ab initio molecular dynamics
active_space_orbital_description: 4 electrons in 4 orbitals (the butadiene pi system)
active_space_protocol: (4,4) held fixed; the paper's subject is the STATE-AVERAGING scheme rather than the orbital space. SA-4-CASSCF/6-31G* (four states in the average) exhibits energy discontinuities in ALL states at the point where S3 — which is included in the state averaging — crosses S4, which is not. This is the general pathology: discontinuities appear in SA-CASSCF potential energy surfaces whenever a state left out of the average crosses one that is included, and they break energy conservation in excited-state dynamics. The remedy demonstrated here is dynamical weighting with a spline, DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF, which mimics SA-CASSCF while smoothly removing the discontinuities due to unweighted state crossings. Practical guidance: when choosing how many states to state-average, the risk is not only the orbital active space but which states are omitted from the average along the coordinate of interest
nroots_per_mult: 4 for SA-4-CASSCF; DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF uses a dynamical weight with an energy width parameter of 6 eV
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet (S0). States S0-S4 are followed along the terminal twist coordinate; the discontinuity arises at the S3/S4 intersection, with S3 included in and S4 excluded from the state averaging, and is visible even in S2. Absolute state energies are presented graphically rather than tabulated in the extracted text, so no eV values are recorded here
Other: Method contribution: a new dynamical weight with spline (DWS) scheme that reproduces SA-CASSCF behaviour while removing energy discontinuities from unweighted state crossings, plus the first derivation of analytical gradients for DWS-CASSCF and other dynamically weighted schemes. This enables energy-conserving excited-state ab initio molecular dynamics in cases where SA-CASSCF fails. Butadiene's terminal twist coordinate is used as the demonstration because SA-CASSCF discontinuities there are severe
reference_short: Communication: Smoothing out excited-state dynamics: Analytical gradients for dynamically weighted CASSCF, J. Chem. Phys. 141, 171102 (2014)

ligand_set: two uranyl oxo (O2-) plus three bidentate carbonate (CO3 2-) in the equatorial plane

Predicted intense bands near 550, 950 and 2300 cm-1. Electronic spectrum: within 10 eV, 12 symmetry-allowed states, none with oscillator strength above 7.3e-2; only two significant features, near 6.4 and 8.1 eV.

point_group: Cs for the pyramidal form (C2v in the planar limit); the out-of-plane angle alpha is the coordinate of interest
geometry_source: MCSCF/CASSCF geometry optimization; then multireference FOCI optimization; then SOCI scans of the inversion coordinate with NO, NH and HNH held fixed while alpha was varied
method: CASSCF (full valence) and internal-set-partitioned MCSCF, followed by multireference first-order CI (FOCI) and second-order CI (SOCI); Full Valence CI (FVCI) over the internal sets
software: Alchemy II (IBM version, on IBM 3090 and IBM RISC 6000)
basis_set: DZP plus diffuse functions (34 a' and 16 a'' molecular orbitals in Cs)
active_space_orbital_description: the full valence space of H2NO — the NH bonding and antibonding pair, the sigma(NO) and sigma*(NO), the oxygen sp lone pair, the pi and pi* of the NO group and the oxygen p lone pair — with only the O 1s and N 1s as core. active_space_protocol: a sequence of internal-set partitions was tested before the full space: [5] the pi system plus the pO lone pair (5 electrons) with everything else core — rejected because the resulting MCSCF orbitals could not be used further, the sigma-pi separation surviving only under the imposed C2v symmetry; [4,9] separating the NH fragment (4 electrons) from the NO fragment (9 electrons); [2,2,9] splitting the NH set further into two subsets; and finally [13], all 13 valence electrons in one complete active space, i.e. CASSCF. The authors' conclusion is that the aminoxyl group is an irreducible 9-electron entity: any partitioning of that {9 electrons in 6 orbitals} space gives a non-stable wavefunction and potentially qualitatively wrong potential surfaces, and the oxygen sp lone pair must be in the active space alongside the pO orbital for hybridization reasons.

Two excited states studied, sigma -> pi* and n -> pi*, matching the two absorptions seen experimentally for stable aminoxyls (an intense band and a weak one). Geometries: FOCI optimization gives NO 1.288 A, NH 1.033 A, HNH 115.2 deg, alpha 24.6 deg — only slightly changed from the CASSCF optimization, but with alpha reduced into agreement with earlier RHF+CI work. The SOCI treatment with wavefunction [2,2,9] gives NO 1.309 A, NH 1.012 A, HNH 121.3 deg, alpha 0 deg: the minimum is planar. Correlation increases pi delocalization of the NO bond and flattens the molecule. For the n -> pi* state the SOCI optimization gives an NO length of 1.642 A, the authors concluding that correlation matters a great deal for this state's NO bond. CSF counts: 6986 for the CASSCF/FVCI, 11156 for the FOCI, 193318 for the SOCI (and 666260 for the 12e-/1e- internal-external partition). Ground-state dipole moments computed at FVCI and FOCI agree well with the experimental values for aminoxyl radicals II and III (3.12 and 3.14 D); the SOCI value is slightly larger.
