compound_name: C2 dicarbon — high-spin sigma states probing the quadruple-bonding question (compared with N2, Be2, HC=CH, BN and CN+)
geometry_source: potential energy curves computed as a function of the internuclear distance; no equilibrium geometry optimization protocol stated
method: full-valence CASSCF, RASSCF with occupation restrictions on the pi orbitals, and MRCI
active_space_orbital_description: the full valence space of C2 — the 2s- and 2p-derived sigma_g, sigma_u, pi_u, pi_g manifold on the two carbons
active_space_protocol: full-valence CASSCF for the ground state and the 2S+1 = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 sigma states; then RASSCF with deliberate occupation restrictions used as the key device of the paper — for C2 the pi orbitals were restricted to exactly one electron each (removing any pi bonding), and for Be2 the pi orbitals were restricted to zero occupation, so that in both cases the dominant configurations reduce to four electrons in four sigma orbitals and the sigma-only bonding can be compared directly; MRCI then used to check the conclusions against dynamic correlation
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1Sigma_g+. Full-valence CASSCF shows pronounced multireference character, the two dominant CSFs carrying 70% and 13%; the authors note the second CSF is the one that could support two sigma bonds. The paper's central result: with pi bonding artificially suppressed by the RASSCF restriction, the 5Sigma_g+ state of C2 still shows a distinct deep minimum while 1Sigma_g+ Be2 is entirely dissociative, and the two low-lying 7Sigma_u+ states also retain deep minima. Their dominant CSFs are |2sigma_g2 3sigma_g1 1pi_u2 1pi_g2 2sigma_u1> and |2sigma_g1 3sigma_g2 1pi_u2 1pi_g2 2sigma_u1>, which the authors read as two sets of sigma electron pairs giving two genuine sigma bonds. MRCI leaves the trends unchanged: the 7Sigma_u+ state of C2 keeps a distinct minimum with an estimated dissociation energy of 69 kcal/mol and lies 9.4 eV above the ground state, while 9Sigma_g+ is purely dissociative. For the isoelectronic species, CN+ shows distinct minima in its lowest four spin states, whereas BN's 7Sigma_u+ state is dissociative — so the authors assign latent quadruple bonding to C2 and CN+ but not BN. electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 6H15/2 for Dy(III), 4f9. The magnetic anisotropy axis lies along the axial O-Dy-O bond, perpendicular to the ground-state beta electron density, minimizing electrostatic repulsion. Ground and first-excited Kramers doublets are strongly axial (gx = gy ~ 0.0), and the angle between the ground and first-excited anisotropy axes is under 6 degrees, so relaxation proceeds via higher excited states. Significant thermally-activated QTM at the second excited state sets the relaxation path |-15/2> -> |-13/2> -> |-1/2> -> |+1/2> -> |+13/2> -> |15/2>. Axial crystal-field parameters (k = 2, 4, 6; q = 0) exceed the non-axial ones, confirming substantial axiality in all three. For complex 1 (Cl): gz = 19.857 in the ground Kramers doublet; the eight ground Kramers doublets from 6H15/2 span up to 902.0 K; Ucal = 606.3 K. This is the smallest barrier of the series, attributed to the smaller, strongly hydrogen-bonded chloride and the correspondingly smaller axial B2-0 crystal-field parameter.

The CASSCF wavefunction has an 83% main contributor. DFT describes the complex as (dxy)2(dyz+Cpy)2(dxz)2(Cpy-dyz)1alpha(dz2-Csigma)0(dx2-y2)0 with the unpaired electron delocalized over the Co-C bond (spin density 0.50 on the carbene carbon, 0.16 alpha-spin excess on Co, Co-C bond order 1.21). A 6% multireference contribution populates the Co(dz2)-Csigma antibonding orbital, weakening that bond to an effective bond order of 0.98.

electronic_structure_description: Three unpaired electrons. Unlike the mono-nitrene and carbene complexes, here the quartet is slightly more stable than the broken-symmetry doublet: dG(298K) = -1.4 kcal/mol. The small gap and the very similar geometries of the two spin states suggest a significant Boltzmann population of the broken-symmetry doublet. Both states correspond to two nitrene radicals (N1 and N2) bearing alpha-spin unpaired electrons plus an unpaired electron on the porphyrin ligand — alpha-spin in the quartet, beta-spin in the broken-symmetry doublet. In the doublet, the two most stable alpha-spin SOMOs are Npy(1) at 63.5% and the second nitrene-based orbital. This species is the paper's clearest case that a multireference, multideterminant wavefunction is genuinely required: DFT cannot properly describe the broken-symmetry doublet arising from three unpaired electrons.

geometry_source: minima, conical intersections, minimum-energy paths and intersystem crossings optimized at CASSCF; conical intersections not found along MEPs computed at CASSCF with a degeneracy restriction via restricted Lagrange multipliers (no nonadiabatic coupling elements); linear interpolation in internal coordinates where MEPs were not possible. No symmetry restrictions (C1).
method: CASPT2//CASSCF protocol: CASSCF geometries with CASPT2 single points for dynamical correlation; imaginary shift 0.2 au to avoid intruder states, no IPEA shift (for consistency with earlier studies); spin-orbit couplings from atomic mean field integrals (AMFI); solvent by PCM
basis_set: ANO-L of double-zeta plus polarization quality: C, N, O (10s6p3d) / H (7s3p) primitives contracted to C, N, O (3s2p1d) / H (2s1p)
soc_included: yes (AMFI spin-orbit couplings, since the paper is about triplet population)
active_space_orbital_description: the full pi system (12 electrons in 10 orbitals) plus three n orbitals, giving 18 electrons in 13 orbitals for the vertical and adiabatic energies
active_space_protocol: Explicit three-tier reduction. Including all pi (12 electrons, 10 orbitals) and all n (8 electrons, 4 orbitals) character would give CAS(20,14), which the authors state is not feasible, so a systematic study was run to find the smallest space retaining the relevant orbitals. (18,13) = full pi system plus three n orbitals, used for the vertical and adiabatic energies and for the CASPT2 single points. (16,12) = nine pi orbitals plus three n orbitals, obtained from (18,13) by moving the pi orbital localized on the NH2 group into the inactive space on energy and occupation-number criteria, as done in earlier adenine studies; used for geometry optimizations of minima and conical intersections. (12,10) = pi only, used for the minimum-energy paths on the 1(pi pi)* surfaces.
electronic_structure_description: Photophysics of 8-azaadenine analysed with the CASPT2//CASSCF protocol, compared throughout with adenine. Singlet and triplet manifolds are mapped via minima, conical intersections and intersystem crossings, with AMFI spin-orbit couplings quantifying the singlet-to-triplet channels. Dynamical correlation for every optimized structure comes from single-point CASPT2(18,13) - 18 electrons in three n plus ten pi/pi* orbitals.
reference_short: On the Mechanisms of Triplet Excited State Population in 8-Azaadenine, J. Phys. Chem. B 116, 14000 (2012)

compound_name: molecular Mn18-ring complex [Mn3O(OAc)7(HOAc)]6 . x AcOH (x = 6-9), modelled as its Mn(III)3 subunit
ligand_set: oxo-centred Mn3 triangles bridged by acetate, with coordinated acetic acid; six such Mn3 units assemble the Mn18 ring
geometry_source: single-crystal X-ray diffraction geometry used directly for the Mn3 subunit models
method: CASSCF/NEVPT2 for the exchange couplings, alongside broken-symmetry DFT; parameters fitted to a Heisenberg Hamiltonian
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(12,15) on a (Mn(III), S = 2)3 subunit — 12 electrons (three Mn(III) d4 centres) in 15 orbitals
active_space_protocol: Fragment/diamagnetic-substitution strategy: to extract a pairwise exchange coupling, one Mn(III) of a Mn3 unit is replaced by diamagnetic Ga(III), leaving two magnetically coupled Mn(III) ions. The full (Mn(III), S = 2)3 trimer is then treated with CAS(12,15) to test whether the pairwise couplings are transferable, computing the lowest energy level for each total spin S = 0 to S = 6 and fitting exchange parameters directly to those computed energies.
multiplicities_studied: total spin S = 0 through S = 6 for the Mn3 subunit
electronic_structure_description: Exchange parameters for the 'small' Mn3 and 'extended' Mn6 Heisenberg Hamiltonians were obtained from both broken-symmetry DFT and CASSCF/NEVPT2. The CAS(12,15) trimer calculation gives the lowest spin level for every S from 0 to 6, from which couplings are extracted by direct fit, allowing the transferability of the Mn2+Ga pairwise couplings to be checked. Fitting the experimental susceptibility while excluding data above 50 K gives an improved J = -3.7 cm-1 for the coupling between the (Mn(III), S = 2)3 units.
reference_short: Exchange Interactions and Magnetic Properties of a Molecular Mn18-Ring Complex
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). The Mn3 units of the Mn18 ring are symmetry-related, so a single subunit model represents the ring. software: Gaussian 16 for the geometries; the multireference work uses the RASSI module (OpenMolcas family)

compound_name: highly anisotropic five-coordinate Fe(III) porphyrin complex (complex 1), square-pyramidal
ligand_set: porphyrin macrocycle with a single axial ligand, giving a square-pyramidal five-coordinate iron
geometry_source: molecular structures taken directly from experimental X-ray data at 100, 250 and 295 K, with only hydrogen positions normalized (Mercury). Separate DFT optimizations for S = 5/2, 3/2 and 1/2 at TPSSh-D3BJ/x2c-TZVPall were done for the Mossbauer calibration.
method: state-averaged CASSCF with NEVPT2 and Hermitian quasi-degenerate NEVPT2 (QD-NEVPT2); ab initio ligand field theory (AILFT) for d-orbital energies; DFT (ORCA 6.0, TPSSh-D3BJ) for 57Fe Mossbauer parameters
basis_set: ZORA-def2-TZVPP on iron, ZORA-def2-TZVP(-f) on other heavy atoms, ZORA-def2-SVP on C and H; SARC/J Coulomb fitting with RIJCOSX; DEFGrid3 and tightSCF
soc_included: yes (ZFS parameter D reported from the QD-NEVPT2 ligand-field multiplets)
active_space_orbital_description: largest space CAS(9e,12o): the five Fe 3d orbitals plus a pi-type ligand-based orbital, the five more diffuse 4d metal orbitals, and a sigma-type ligand-based orbital
active_space_protocol: A four-step expansion driven by disagreement with experiment. CAS(5e,5o), the usual d-orbital-only space, put the lowest quartet ligand-field term at 9396 cm-1 - far from the magnetic data - and gave a too-small axial ZFS D = 2.06-2.1 cm-1. Adding a pi-type ligand-based orbital gave CAS(7e,6o); adding the diffuse 4d metal orbitals gave CAS(7e,11o); finally a sigma-type ligand-based orbital was found essential, giving CAS(9e,12o). The quartet-sextet ligand-field gap falls 9396 -> 4679 (CAS(7e,11o)) -> 2749 cm-1 (CAS(9e,12o)) and D rises 2.06 -> 7.85 cm-1, the latter close to the experimental value. The authors state explicitly that the dominant changes came from the pi- and sigma-type ligand-based orbitals and that this 'points out the importance of balancing the active space'.
multiplicities_studied: 2,4,6 — 6, 4 and 2 (sextet, quartet and doublet ligand-field terms)
electronic_structure_description: Fe(III) d5. AILFT d-orbital ordering dxy < dxz, dyz < dz2 < dx2-y2, as expected for a square-pyramidal field. Active-space dependence of the key observables: quartet-sextet ligand-field gap 9396 cm-1 at CAS(5e,5o), 4679 cm-1 at CAS(7e,11o), 2749 cm-1 at CAS(9e,12o); axial ZFS D = 2.06 cm-1 at CAS(5e,5o) rising to 7.85 cm-1 at CAS(9e,12o). Temperature dependence at the largest space: the quartet-sextet gap decreases with the temperature at which the crystal structure was measured, and D rises from 7.85 cm-1 (100 K structure) to 10.08 cm-1 (295 K structure). Experimentally, out-of-phase susceptibility appears at 1.9 K above 100 Hz but without clear maxima, so the paper stops short of claiming SMM behaviour.
reference_short: Realizing the magneto-structural correlation of a highly anisotropic Fe(III) porphyrin complex through ab-initio approaches (ChemRxiv preprint, 2025)
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). An unusually clear worked example of active-space balancing in a TM complex: the d-only space is shown to be quantitatively wrong for the ZFS, and both a pi- and a sigma-type ligand orbital plus the 4d shell are needed to reach experiment. The same study also appears under DOI 10.1021/acs.inorgchem.5c02754; that duplicate index record was marked not_usable on 2026-07-30, so this key is the single record for this work.

compound_name: lutein (xanthophyll carotenoid, ten conjugated C=C double bonds) - excited states along the bond-length-alternation coordinate
geometry_source: potential energy curves computed along the bond-length-alternation (BLA) coordinate
method: CASSCF and DMRG-based large-active-space calculations for the four lowest singlet states
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(20,20), the chemically complete pi space: 20 pi-type molecular orbitals occupied by 20 electrons, corresponding to the ten conjugated C=C double bonds. This choice was independently confirmed by the authors' automatic UNO-based active-space selection procedure, making it both chemically motivated and unbiased. Four asymmetric alternatives were also studied, each with six more virtual orbitals than electrons: CAS(8,14), CAS(10,16), CAS(12,18) and CAS(14,20).
active_space_protocol: The paper's central result is a documented failure of the chemically complete space. CAS(20,20) - the full pi valence space, confirmed by automatic UNO selection - is adequate for the GROUND state but gives an unbalanced description of the excited-state manifold: the bright state is artificially shifted to high energy and the expected sequence of state crossings along the BLA coordinate is lost. Four deliberately asymmetric spaces were therefore tested, each carrying six more virtual orbitals than electrons - CAS(8,14), CAS(10,16), CAS(12,18), CAS(14,20) - the rationale being prior insight into the expected excitation patterns plus a qualitative orbital analysis.
electronic_structure_description: Potential energy curves for the four lowest singlet states of lutein along the bond-length-alternation coordinate. The bright state evolves along BLA through a series of crossings, but only with a suitably unbalanced active space: with the chemically complete CAS(20,20) the bright state is placed artificially high in energy and the crossing sequence is wrong. This makes the paper a direct counterexample to the assumption that the full valence pi space is the safe choice for excited states of long polyenes.
reference_short: Can CASSCF model the excited states of xanthophyll lutein? A Density Matrix Renormalization Group journey (ChemRxiv preprint, 2026)
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). Metal-free organic carotenoid. Among the most useful active-space results in this database: the chemically complete and automatically confirmed CAS(20,20) is shown to be WORSE than deliberately asymmetric spaces for the excited-state manifold, because balance between occupied and virtual orbitals matters more than completeness. Not peer reviewed (ChemRxiv).

ligand_set: porphine macrocycle (the model system used to describe ring correlation and connect the frontier pi orbitals to Gouterman's orbitals)
geometry_source: model system built on the TRIPLET geometry of Fe(II)-porphyrin, i.e. with a short Fe-N bond length. The authors state explicitly that this represents a bias towards the intermediate spin state which needs to be addressed.
method: Stochastic-CASSCF (FCIQMC-based), compared against conventional CASSCF/CASPT2
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(32,34) containing the metal 3d AND 4d orbitals together with the entire pi system of the porphyrin - a valence space, with (3s,3p) semi-core correlation treated separately.
active_space_protocol: CAS(32,34) valence-only space used with Stochastic-CASSCF. The paper documents that conventional CASSCF with active spaces up to CAS(14,16) followed by CASPT2 could NOT capture the higher-order correlation and orbital relaxation effects, over-stabilizing one spin state relative to the intermediate spin state. Three further strategies were then used to recover correlation outside CAS(32,34), one of them following Pierloot and co-workers' approach to semi-core correlation.
electronic_structure_description: Spin gap between the intermediate-spin 3Eg and high-spin 5A1g states. CASSCF valence correlation in the (32,34) space is necessary to stabilize the intermediate spin state at all. Semi-core (3s,3p) correlation adds a quantitatively significant but smaller correction of about 1.5 kcal/mol. Accounting for both enlarges the (3Eg - 5A1g) gap to about -5 kcal/mol. Within the (32,34) space the gap depends on the coupled-cluster truncation: -3.1 kcal/mol at CAS(32,34) and CCSDT, -0.8 at CCSD, -2.6 at DCSD, -2.7 at CCSD(T) and -3.6 at CCSDTQ.
reference_short: On the Role of Valence and Semi-Core Electron Correlation on Spin-Gaps in Fe(II)-Porphyrins
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). A key negative result for active-space practice: CASSCF/CASPT2 up to CAS(14,16) fails on this system, and even the large CAS(32,34) needs supplementary treatment of semi-core correlation.

compound_name: QUESTDB benchmark database - 542 vertical excitation energies with automated APC active-space selection
point_group: reduced to the highest available symmetry implementable for each molecule
geometry_source: QUESTDB benchmark geometries
method: state-averaged CASSCF with MC-PDFT (tPBE) and NEVPT2, using automated entropy-ranked active-space selection
active_space_orbital_description: Automated 'max(n,m)' spaces capped by a maximum CSF count: max(4,4) (N_max_CSF = 20), max(5,5), max(12,12) and others. Orbitals are ranked by occupancy and entropy pairs (n_j, S_j) and pruned until the CSF count falls under the cap.
active_space_protocol: Approximate pair-coefficient (APC) automated selection with a 'max(n,m)' cap set by a maximum CSF count: orbitals carry an occupancy and an approximated entropy (n_j, S_j) and are admitted in entropy order until the CSF count would exceed N_max_CSF. A worked example takes a max(4,4) target (cap 20 CSFs) and returns a (5,4) space with exactly 20 CSFs. Critically, the authors then FILTER: 20-30% of the automatically generated active spaces were poor and were eliminated by applying a threshold to the SA-CASSCF absolute error, leaving 373 of the 542 excitations for the method comparison.
electronic_structure_description: Largest benchmarking of MC-PDFT and HMC-PDFT to date, over the QUESTDB set of 542 vertical excitations. After discarding the 20-30% of automatically chosen active spaces that were poor, HMC-PDFT performs about as well as NEVPT2 and CC2 on the remaining 373 excitations. The optimal fraction of SA-CASSCF energy to mix into HMC-PDFT with the tPBE on-top functional was found to be 25%, i.e. the value already used in tPBE0. NEVPT2 performance is significantly affected by active-space quality, and at normal grid size tPBE is on average about 114x cheaper than NEVPT2 for large max(12,12) spaces.
reference_short: Large-Scale Benchmarking of Multireference Vertical-Excitation Calculations via Automated Active-Space Selection
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). Recorded as a benchmark-set row. The transferable content is the entropy-plus-CSF-cap selection algorithm and the NEVPT2-vs-tPBE cost scaling with active-space size.

active_space_protocol: A systematic comparison of active spaces and basis sets at conical intersections, classified as peaked/sloped and single-path/bifurcating. The most correlated treatment gives peaked and single-path; the (12,9) space gives peaked and bifurcating but very close to the classification boundary; the smaller (4,3) and (2,2) spaces come out as sloped and single-path by overestimating the P parameter.
electronic_structure_description: Characterisation of conical intersections in DNA/RNA nucleobases. The paper's central conclusion is that STRUCTURAL changes are NOT the key factor: the optimized intersection geometries are almost identical across active-space and basis-set changes, and what matters instead is correctly describing the electronic states involved at the crossing. The one structural outlier noted is thymine, where the (4,3) space puckers much more heavily around the O=C2-N3-C4=O frame than any other optimized structure. What does change with active space is the topographical CLASSIFICATION - peaked versus sloped and single-path versus bifurcating - with the smaller (4,3) and (2,2) spaces misclassifying intersections as sloped by overestimating P.
reference_short: Characterising conical intersections in DNA/RNA nucleobases with multiconfigurational wave functions of varying active space size
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). Metal-free organic nucleobases. One of the more directly useful papers for this database: it quantifies how conical-intersection character itself is an artefact of active-space size below a threshold.

geometry_source: SA6-CASSCF(4,7)/ANO-S-VDZP optimized structures along the NBD to QC photoisomerization, benchmarked against EOM-CCSD/aug-cc-pVDZ

active_space_protocol: Explicit extension of a literature space to capture Rydberg character. Antol had proposed (4,5) - four pi electrons in four pi orbitals with restricted single excitations to an auxiliary 3s orbital. Because the low-lying photochemistry involves an n to 3s Rydberg excitation (absorption at 212 nm / 5.85 eV), this work uses (4,7) adding 3s, 3px and 3py, the Rydberg orbitals selected on the basis of the lowest four excitations. Benchmarked against EOM-CCSD/aug-cc-pVDZ, and run as SA6-CASSCF(4,7)/ANO-S-VDZP.

The active space must carry Rydberg character: the 212 nm (5.85 eV) absorption is an excitation into the 3s Rydberg state, so a valence pi-only space cannot represent the relevant states, and (4,7) with 3s, 3px and 3py is used instead of the literature (4,5).
reference_short: Multiconfigurational calculations and photodynamics describe norbornadiene photochemistry
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). Metal-free organic. A clear case where diffuse Rydberg orbitals, not extra valence orbitals, are what the active space is missing.

method: CASSCF followed by single-state (SS) and multi-state (MS) CASPT2 with a level-shift-corrected perturbation; TDDFT (B3LYP, PBE1PBE) computed alongside for comparison

compound_name: ethene-water heterodimer, C2H4..H2O (weakly bound OH..pi complex)
geometry_source: MP2/6-31+G* optimized dimer geometry; single-point NEVPT2 also carried out at four further optimized geometries denoted G1-G4, each with its own basis set
method: CASSCF followed by NEVPT2 in its strongly contracted (SC) and partially contracted (PC) variants, with Boys-Bernardi counterpoise correction for basis set superposition error; benchmarked against CCSD(T)
software: GAMESS-US for the CASSCF; Dalton 2.0 for the SC- and PC-NEVPT2

electronic_structure_description: Intermolecular OH..pi interaction energy. Literature and experiment place the C2H4-H2O binding energy at 1.50-2.0 kcal/mol; the counterpoise-corrected NEVPT2/6-31+G* interaction energies agree well with that range, with PC-NEVPT2 performing slightly better than SC-NEVPT2 in this relatively small basis. Other: PC-NEVPT2 is more accurate and efficient than SC-NEVPT2 throughout; at the (2,2) active space the two variants give identical accuracy.

ligand_set: two bridging oxo ligands and one bridging acetate, with terminal ligands completing each Mn coordination sphere
geometry_source: experimentally characterized complex; the paper works from its crystallographically known structure
method: DMRG-CASCI and spin-state-averaged DMRG-CASSCF, with DMRG-NEVPT2 for dynamic correlation; broken-symmetry DFT computed for comparison
software: ORCA interfaced with the BLOCK DMRG code; MOLBLOCK used for the DMRG-NEVPT2 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: localized Mn 3d orbitals together with the 2p orbitals of the two oxo bridges (three orbitals per bridging oxygen) - the smallest active space that switches on the superexchange mechanism
active_space_protocol: (7,10) Mn 3d only, which gives J = -1.6 cm-1 and is qualitatively wrong; (19,16) adding localized O 2p bridge orbitals, giving J = -28.8 cm-1 by DMRG-CASCI without reoptimization and J = -59.0 cm-1 with spin-state-averaged DMRG-CASSCF orbital optimization; (23,18) which changes nothing further (J = -58.5 cm-1); (19,32) the complete metal 3d+4d and oxygen 2p+3p set, giving an average J of -60.4 cm-1
multiplicities_studied: all spin states of the coupled Mn(III,IV) dimer, from S = 1/2 to the high-spin state
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over all spin states involved
electronic_structure_description: Heisenberg exchange coupling constant J. Experiment gives J = -90.0 cm-1 (antiferromagnetic). Metal-only CASSCF(7,10) gives -1.6 cm-1, which is qualitatively wrong; adding the oxo-bridge 2p orbitals as DMRG-CASCI(19,16) gives -28.8 cm-1, and orbital optimization via spin-state-averaged DMRG-CASSCF(19,16) more than doubles the coupling to -59.0 cm-1. Enlarging further to (23,18) or the full (19,32) metal 3d+4d / oxygen 2p+3p space changes little (-58.5 and -60.4 cm-1). Broken-symmetry DFT spans an enormous range: BP86 -161.7, TPSSh -95.1, M06-2X -18.2 cm-1. The natural orbital occupations of the O 2p orbitals fall to about 1.85 for the in-plane orbitals, confirming their genuine involvement.
Other: Two operational conclusions are the paper's point: orbital optimization is essential for stabilizing the antiferromagnetic state, and a state-averaged treatment over all spin states is required - state-specific optimization gives the correct state ordering but artificial deviations from isotropic Heisenberg behaviour. Quantitative accuracy needs DMRG-NEVPT2 on a full-valence metal-plus-ligand active space.

software: MOLPRO for the CASSCF and CASPT2; TURBOMOLE for the MP2 and CC2

method: stochastic-CASSCF, i.e. FCIQMC used as the CI eigensolver inside a CASSCF orbital optimization; DMRG and generalized active space (GAS) calculations for comparison; a preliminary Stochastic Generalized Active Space Self-Consistent Field method is introduced here

This mechanism is absent from small-active-space calculations and is not recovered by second-order perturbation theory such as CASPT2 applied on top of a small-active-space reference - which is the paper's argument that large active spaces are essential here. Localized-orbital analysis is used to interpret the role of the charge-transfer configurations, and the new Stochastic GASSCF method is used to isolate the pi-backdonation stabilization by controlling which excitations are allowed.
Other: Fe(II) porphyrin spin-state ordering is a long-standing benchmark problem; this paper's contribution is that the answer depends on charge-transfer configurations only accessible in a large active space.

ligand_set: histidine-derived nitrogen donors and bridging oxygen species of the trinuclear copper site
method: two parallel treatments: CASSCF/CASPT2 with all fifteen d orbitals active, using multistate CASPT2 and averaging over the relevant ligand-to-metal charge-transfer states; and a small CASSCF(3,3) followed by difference-dedicated CI (DDCI2) or CI with single excitations for the exchange splittings

active_space_orbital_description: all fifteen d orbitals of the three copper centres with their 27 electrons; a second d shell is required for transition-metal complexes of this kind, and the state averaging must include the relevant LMCT states
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(27,15) with MS-CASPT2 and LMCT states in the average, which is the large treatment; CASSCF(3,3) followed by DDCI2 or CIS, which is the small treatment used to get reasonable quartet-doublet exchange splittings

method: CASSCF wavefunction corrected by partially contracted second-order NEVPT2; ground-state energies also from DFT (BLYP/TZP in ADF, CPMD); a polarizable continuum model calculation used to assess solvent effects on the relative stabilities
software: Dalton 1.2 for the CASSCF and NEVPT2; GAMESS for the same CAS with PCM; Gaussian for the B3LYP geometries; CPMD and ADF 2002.3 for the DFT energies

The neutral2 model is the exception, its trans form remaining about 0.1 eV more energetic than the cis.
Other: Two sets of models were used, differing in how much of the protein environment is retained; the complete set is tabulated in Table 1 of the paper. PCM was used to separate solvent effects on relative stability.

method: state-averaged CASSCF with CASPT2 single points using the SA-CASSCF wavefunction as reference; the internally contracted implementation for doubly external configurations was used
basis_set: cc-pVTZ for carbon and hydrogen; for iodine, an effective core potential covering a 46-electron core (large-core [Kr]4d10) with the cc-pVTZ-pp valence basis of Peterson et al. for the seven valence electrons
relativistic_treatment: effective core potential on iodine, which also contains terms for evaluating spin-orbit coupling of the valence electrons
soc_included: yes (the iodine ECP includes spin-orbit terms, and both singlet and triplet manifolds are computed)

compound_name: small C4n carbon rings - open-shell transition state between closed-shell alternating and non-alternating minima
method: CASSCF(2,2) with second-order perturbation theory on top, compared against broken-symmetry DFT (B3LYP) and against more reliable wavefunction theory calculations

electronic_structure_description: The paper is a documented failure case for a minimal active space. The barrier separating the closed-shell alternating and non-alternating minima of small C4n rings passes through an open-shell transition state. CASSCF(2,2) over the HOMO/LUMO pair overestimates the barrier substantially, and adding second-order perturbation theory then cancels it entirely, placing the non-alternating geometry well below the alternating one. The authors attribute the failure to the collective character of the spin polarization, which a two-orbital space cannot represent.

point_group: C2v (ruffled/saddled distortions from C4v; the quintet states retain C4v)
geometry_source: DFT/PBE0 optimized (UDFT for 1A1 and 5A2, RODFT for 3B1); Mn-O distance additionally optimized at the CASPT2 level for the lowest states
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 and RASSCF/RASPT2 single-point calculations
software: MOLCAS 7.9 (CASPT2/RASPT2); TURBOMOLE v6.4 and GAUSSIAN 09 (DFT); MOLPRO v2012 (ROPBE0 structures)
basis_set: ANO-RCC contracted to [7s6p5d2f2g1h] for Mn, [4s3p2d1f] for C, N, O and F, [3s1p] for H
active_space_orbital_description: static correlation of the Mn 3d shell; the covalent Mn-O bonds Mn(3dz2)-O(2pz) (sigma_z, sigma*_z), Mn(3dxz)-O(2px) (pi_xz, pi*_xz) and Mn(3dyz)-O(2py) (pi_yz, pi*_yz); Mn(3dxy)-P(sigma_xy) (sigma_xy, sigma*_xy); the remaining non-bonding Mn 3d-delta orbital; plus the four Gouterman porphyrin pi MOs. The RAS extension adds all P(pi)/P(pi*) orbitals, 16 P(pi) in total.
active_space_protocol: (14,16) for the closed-shell 1MnVO(L) singlet, which has both pi*_xz and pi*_yz unoccupied so those are 4d correlating orbitals; (14,17) for 3MnVO(L) and for the 1,3MnIVO(L-radical) states, which have more open shells; (14,18) for the 5MnIVO(L-radical) quintets, with both 4dxz and 4dyz active; RAS(28,28-30) expanding the CAS with additional porphyrin pi/pi* orbitals, allowing up to double excitations out of RAS1 and into RAS3
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1A1 (MnV d2 closed-shell singlet, both 3d electrons paired in the non-bonding 3d-delta MO). The MnV singlet ground state lacks oxyl character and is kinetically inert; oxygen-atom-transfer reactivity is expected to proceed instead through thermally accessible triplet and quintet states with pronounced oxyl character, which arises when the Mn-O pi* orbitals become singly (triplet) or doubly (quintet) occupied. RASPT2 transition energies, all corresponding to the same 3d-delta -> pi* transition: 5.6 kcal/mol for MnV(3B1-1A1), 3.6 kcal/mol for MnIV(P-radical-a2u)(3B1-5A2), and 2.5 kcal/mol for MnIV(P-radical-a1u)(3B1-5A1). The lowest MnIV state is always a quintet (5A1 or 5A2) carrying two single Mn-O pi* electrons.
reference_short: Jannuzzi, Phung, Domingo, Formiga, Pierloot, Inorg. Chem. 2016
notes: Active space size is state-dependent, hence three values of N in CAS(14,N); the (14,16) recorded here is the one used for the 1A1 ground state. IPEA shift 0.25 hartree and imaginary level shift 0.1 hartree; all valence electrons plus the Mn (3s,3p) semi-core correlated at the CASPT2/RASPT2 levels; Cholesky decomposition threshold 1e-6; solvent effects included (dielectric constant 53.54, water/acetonitrile mixture). RASPT2 used as the benchmark against which a range of DFT functionals was tested; B2-PLYP overestimates the MnV(3B1-1A1) gap by ~44 kcal/mol.

compound_name: Cu(II) site of [Cu2La(HL)4(NO3)](NO3)2 (complex 1-La), the diamagnetic-lanthanide member of the {Cu2Ln} series
ligand_set: four monodeprotonated Schiff-base ligands HL (C15H15NO3) and a nitrate; dinuclear {Cu-Ln-Cu} motif
geometry_source: X-ray crystal structure
method: CASSCF followed by RASSI-SO for spin-orbit mixing; SINGLE_ANISO for local magnetic properties and g-tensors; POLY_ANISO to simulate the experimental susceptibility and extract Cu-Ln and Cu-Cu exchange
software: MOLCAS 8.2 (CASSCF/RASSI-SO/SINGLE_ANISO/POLY_ANISO); Gaussian at UB3LYP for NBO analysis
basis_set: ANO-RCC: [8s7p5d3f2g1h] for the lanthanide, [5s4p2d] for Cu/Zn, [3s2p] for C, [2s] for H, [3s2p1d] for N and O
relativistic_treatment: ANO-RCC relativistically contracted basis sets with RASSI-SO spin-orbit treatment
active_space_orbital_description: the five Cu(II) 3d orbitals; the magnetic orbital is 3dx2-y2
active_space_protocol: one paramagnetic metal centre computed at a time with every other metal replaced by its closest diamagnetic analogue (Cu(II) by Zn(II), Ln(III) by La(III)), so the active fragment is Cu(II)-La(III)-Zn(II) for the copper site and Zn(II)-Ln(III)-Zn(II) for the lanthanide site; (9,5) on Cu(II) using the five 3d orbitals, and (n,7) on each Ln(III) using the seven 4f orbitals with n set by the 4f^n configuration
nroots_per_mult: 5 doublet excited states for each Cu(II) ion, used to extract the spin projection on the copper centres in all complexes 1-La to 7-Ho
electronic_structure_description: La(III) is 4f0 and diamagnetic, so 1-La contains only the two paramagnetic Cu(II) ions; its susceptibility is slightly higher than expected for two uncoupled Cu(II) ions. The central result of the paper: the Cu(II)-Ln(III) exchange is antiferromagnetic for lanthanides with fewer than 4f7 electrons and ferromagnetic for 4f7 and beyond, while the net magnitude of J decreases steadily from f1 to f13. The mechanism proposed is orbital-symmetry based: of the seven 4f orbitals only two share the irreducible representation of the Cu(II) 3dx2-y2 magnetic orbital and can therefore contribute to the antiferromagnetic term, whereas the ferromagnetic term JF arises from charge transfer into 5d orbitals and from orthogonality between the 4f and 3d orbitals.
reference_short: Ahmed, Sharma, Spillecke et al., Inorg. Chem. 2022
notes: Active space, basis and root counts are stated only in the Supporting Information, not the main text. Only a limited number of CASSCF states could be mixed by spin-orbit coupling in the RASSI-SO step for the lanthanides, due to hardware limitations (stated by the authors). This row records the copper active space, which is identical across the whole 1-La to 7-Ho series.

software: MOLCAS 8.0 (CASSCF/RASSI-SO/SINGLE_ANISO/POLY_ANISO); Gaussian 09 with B3LYP for the DFT exchange calculations
basis_set: ANO-RCC: [8s7p5d3f2g1h] for the lanthanide, [3s2p1d] for O; diamagnetic lanthanide positions modelled with Lu
relativistic_treatment: Douglas-Kroll Hamiltonian, with spin-orbit coupling through RASSI-SO
active_space_orbital_description: five d-based orbitals of the Mn(III) ion
active_space_protocol: the active space comprises five d-based orbitals, with three electrons for Mn(IV) in a CAS(3,5) setup and four electrons for Mn(III) in a CAS(4,5) setup
nroots_per_mult: five quintet and forty-five triplet excited states , used to compute the zero-field splitting
electronic_structure_description: Manganese contribution to the magnetic relaxation mechanism of the {MnIVMnIII2LnIII2} family; the zfs of the manganese centres combines with the lanthanide anisotropy to determine whether SMM behaviour survives at zero field.
reference_short: Vignesh, Langley, Moubaraki, Murray, Rajaraman, Inorg. Chem. 2018
notes: Heterometallic pentanuclear family [MnIVMnIII2LnIII2O2(benz)4(mdea)3(NO3)2(MeOH)] (benz = benzoate, mdeaH2 = N-methyldiethanolamine), Ln = Dy(1), Tb(2), Gd(3), Eu(4), Sm(5), Nd(6), Pr(7), plus an O-toluate analogue 8-Gd. Each paramagnetic centre was computed separately on the mononuclear fragment.

compound_name: cobalt(II) site of the mixed-valence chain {[CoII(MeOH)2][(mu-NC)2CoIII(dmphen)(CN)2]2}n·2nH2O (compound 1), a chain of vertex-sharing {CoIII2CoII2} squares
ligand_set: two methanol ligands and four bridging cyanide N-donors from the [CoIII(dmphen)(CN)3]- metalloligand; dmphen = 2,9-dimethyl-1,10-phenanthroline
geometry_source: experimental (X-ray) geometry used directly
method: CASSCF/NEVPT2 with zero-field splitting extracted through an effective Hamiltonian
basis_set: Ahlrichs def2-TZVP with the corresponding auxiliary basis sets; RIJCOSX (RI + chain-of-spheres) acceleration
active_space_orbital_description: the five cobalt(II) 3d orbitals
active_space_protocol: seven electrons in five d orbitals; the starting wavefunction was taken from a previous complete active space calculation
nroots_per_mult: contributions to the zfs from 10 quartet and 20 doublet excited states, included through an effective Hamiltonian
electronic_structure_description: Mixed-valence 1D coordination polymer in which only the Co(II) sites are paramagnetic (the Co(III) centres are low-spin d6 and diamagnetic). Single-ion-magnet behaviour with large easy-plane anisotropy; simultaneous fit of magnetisation at different dc fields and temperatures gave best-fit D = +67.0 cm-1.
reference_short: Alexandru, Visinescu, Shova, Cano et al., Magnetochemistry 2023
notes: Built from the Ph4P[CoII(dmphen)(CN)3] metalloligand. Same group and same computational protocol as the heterobimetallic chains in 10.3390/magnetochemistry6040066.

geometry_source: experimental geometries taken from the literature (references given in Table I)
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 (second-order perturbation theory with the CASSCF wavefunction as reference); CASSI for transition properties

active_space_orbital_description: pi active space specified per symmetry in D2h as (3,1,1,1,2,2,1,0) = 11 active orbitals holding the 2 pi electrons, the extra orbitals carrying the 3s, 3p and 3d Rydberg series
active_space_protocol: only the pi electrons active, all sigma electrons inactive, carbon 1s frozen in the ground-state SCF form; separate active spaces for the pi-pi* and the pi-sigma* manifolds, the latter adding sigma orbitals to the pi set
electronic_structure_description: Calculations comprised the two valence states plus all singlet and triplet Rydberg states of 3s, 3p and 3d character, with errors in computed excitation energies smaller than 0.1 eV. The V state is noted as a case where the CASSCF wavefunction is not a very good reference.
reference_short: Serrano-Andres, Merchan, Nebot-Gil, Roos, Fulscher, J. Chem. Phys. 1993
notes: Only the pi electrons were active, with all sigma electrons inactive and the carbon 1s electrons frozen in the ground-state SCF form. active_space_norb is the SUM of the per-symmetry active-orbital counts printed in Table I; that table is partially garbled in the PDF text extraction, though the counts are self-consistent with the point group (8 irreps for D2h, 4 for C2h). Wavefunctions were optimised for each state individually; both state-averaged and state-specific approaches gave very similar excitation energies. RMS error over 32 excitation energies is 0.13 eV.

compound_name: [DyL1], the dysprosium(III) complex of 1,4,7-tris[(6-carboxypyridin-2-yl)methyl]-1,4,7-triazacyclononane, a PARASHIFT MRI shift agent, in solution
ligand_set: 1,4,7-tris[(6-carboxypyridin-2-yl)methyl]-1,4,7-triazacyclononane (L1), a nonadentate triazacyclononane-based ligand with three carboxypyridyl arms
geometry_source: snapshots from a 90 ps ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) trajectory in solution; one structure per 1 fs timestep
method: CASSCF with spin-orbit coupling by state interaction (CASSCF-SO), performed independently on every AIMD frame
basis_set: ANO-RCC-VTZP for Dy, ANO-RCC-VDZP for the donor O and N atoms, ANO-RCC-VDZ for all other atoms; two-electron integrals Cholesky-decomposed
relativistic_treatment: second-order Douglas-Kroll Hamiltonian for scalar relativity; atomic mean-field integral (AMFI) approximation for spin-orbit coupling
active_space_orbital_description: nine electrons in the seven 4f orbitals of Dy(III) (4f9)
active_space_protocol: minimal active space of nine electrons in the seven 4f orbitals, with the 18 lowest-energy roots of the ground S = 5/2 spin state (the 6H and 6F terms) treated with equal weighting
nroots_per_mult: 18 lowest-energy roots of the ground S = 5/2 (sextet) spin state, equally weighted, corresponding to the 6H and 6F terms
electronic_structure_description: The magnetic susceptibility tensor chi and the spin Hamiltonian parameters were obtained at each AIMD timestep, giving the time-dependent zero-field splitting D(t) and hence a direct simulation of the electron spin dynamics of [DyL1] in solution; these were used to compute nuclear relaxation and paramagnetic relaxation enhancement, with the ligand-field correlation time tau_LF and its root-mean-square magnitude Delta_LF as the key quantities.
reference_short: Thompson, Alnami, Skelton, Chilton, J. Am. Chem. Soc.
notes: Unusual protocol worth noting: rather than one calculation on a static geometry, a CASSCF-SO calculation is run on every 1 fs frame of a 90 ps AIMD trajectory, so the active space is applied tens of thousands of times to sample solution dynamics. The AIMD was run with Gd3+ in place of Dy3+ and the lanthanide substituted for the electronic-structure step. Active space, basis and root count are stated only in SI Section S2. d/f electron count 4f9 added 2026-08-05: arithmetic from the Dy(3) oxidation state recorded in this row, not a value stated by the paper.

compound_name: [Tm{N(SitBuMe2)2}3]- (complex 3), the first structurally characterised trigonal-planar Tm(II) tris(silylamide) complex, with a [K(2.2.2-cryptand)]+ counter-cation
ligand_set: three bis(silylamide) ligands N** = {N(SitBuMe2)2}, trigonal-planar three-coordinate
geometry_source: single-crystal X-ray diffraction structure
method: CASSCF with spin-orbit coupling by state interaction (CASSCF-SO)
basis_set: ANO-RCC basis sets: VTZP quality on Tm, VDZP on the three N atoms, VDZ on all other atoms
active_space_orbital_description: the seven 4f orbitals populated by the 13 electrons of Tm(II) (4f13)
active_space_protocol: active space of the seven 4f orbitals with the 13 Tm(II) electrons; all 7 doublets included both in the orbital optimisation and in the spin-orbit state interaction
nroots_per_mult: all 7 doublets, used in both the orbital optimisation and the spin-orbit mixing
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: J = 7/2. The trigonal-planar ligand field stabilises the expected electron distribution: the ground J = 7/2 multiplet is split across ca. 1300 cm-1 with a ground state composed of pure mJ = +/-7/2, which is why complex 3 could show slow relaxation of the magnetisation. Complex 3 is EPR silent because the delta_mJ = +/-7 transition within the ground doublet is forbidden.
reference_short: Goodwin, Chilton et al., Inorg. Chem. 2017
notes: Part of a series of trigonal-planar Ln(II) tris(silylamide) complexes (Ln = Sm, Eu, Tm, Yb) made with the smaller bis(silylamide) {N(SitBuMe2)2}; the CASSCF-SO active space is specified in the SI for the Tm(II) member, which is the f13 Kramers ion of interest here. Sm(II) is f6, Eu(II) f7 and Yb(II) f14 (diamagnetic). d/f electron count 4f13 added 2026-08-05: arithmetic from the Tm(2) oxidation state recorded in this row, not a value stated by the paper.

ligand_set: two ethylene-1,2-dithiolate (dithiolene) ligands
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 and RASSCF/RASPT2, using the multistate option (MS-CASPT2 / MS-RASPT2); compared against HF, DFT, UCCSD and UCCSD(T)
basis_set: all-electron relativistic ANO-RCC: Ni [6s5p3d1f], S [5s4p2d], C [4s3p1d], H [2s1p]
active_space_orbital_description: labelled 12/4242 in C2v subspace notation: four sigma, two pi, four sigma* and two pi* MOs. Built to contain at minimum the highest- and lowest-lying pairs of pi orbitals (two pi and two pi*) plus the four bonding and four antibonding orbitals of the weak and large Ni-S bonds.
active_space_protocol: initial space 12/4242 (4 sigma, 2 pi, 4 sigma*, 2 pi*) = 12 electrons in 12 MOs, constructed to include at least the highest- and lowest-lying pi/pi* pairs and the bonding/antibonding orbitals of the Ni-S bonds; analysis of the active space then pointed to adding strongly correlating pi-pi* MOs, enlarging it to 16/4444 and further spaces with 4 or 6 additional pi* MOs
electronic_structure_description: Excitation energies and oscillator strengths for 16 excited states, computed as part of a study of the linear and nonlinear optical properties of Ni-dithiolenes; the extensive pi-electron delocalisation and low-lying excited states are what make these complexes attractive NLO materials.
reference_short: Serrano-Andres, Avramopoulos, Li, Labeguerie, Begue, Kello, Papadopoulos
notes: The active-space label 12/4242 gives the number of active MOs per C2v symmetry subspace alongside the electron count, an explicit example of a paper specifying its space by symmetry blocks rather than by an (nel,norb) pair alone. The PDF encodes many glyphs as /H208xx escapes, so the text is noisy but the active-space statements are unambiguous.

geometry_source: geometries given in the paper's supplementary material
method: multiconfigurational short-range DFT (CAS-srDFT) for NMR shielding constants with gauge-including atomic orbitals (GIAOs); an equivalent set of CASSCF calculations was run for comparison, alongside HF-srDFT and DFT
software: a local development version of Dalton with GIAOs implemented for the relevant two-electron integrals; also the Dalton Project python platform
active_space_orbital_description: six pi orbitals
active_space_protocol: active spaces selected from MP2-srPBE natural occupation numbers; the paper reports them in the order (orbitals, electrons) as (6,6) for adenine, (4,4) for thymine and (7,6) for TMS. For the nucleobases the active spaces contain pi orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: Nuclear magnetic shielding constants. CAS-srDFT performs on average the best of the tested methods for the nucleobases, much better than CASSCF and only marginally better than HF-srDFT.
reference_short: Multiconfigurational short-range DFT for NMR shielding constants with GIAOs, J. Chem. Phys. 2022
notes: IMPORTANT ordering caveat: this paper prints its active spaces as (orbitals, electrons), the reverse of the usual (electrons, orbitals) convention. The values here are transposed accordingly - TMS is 6 electrons in 7 orbitals, not 7 in 6. Adenine and thymine are unaffected since their pairs are symmetric.

ligand_set: nine chloride ligands, tricapped trigonal prismatic, embedded in point charges
geometry_source: crystallographic structure of PrCl3; the cluster is embedded in point charges (+3 for Pr, -1 for Cl) at crystallographic sites within a radius of 8 A
method: spin-free CASSCF followed by spin-orbit state interaction with RASSI (SO-CASSCF); Ln-ligand distance optimised with CASPT2 for the sandwich complexes
software: MOLCAS 7.8; NWChem 6.1 for the DFT-B3LYP ligand geometry optimisations
relativistic_treatment: Douglas-Kroll-Hess transformation for scalar relativity; spin-orbit integrals via the atomic mean-field (AMFI) approximation
active_space_orbital_description: two electrons spread over the seven 4f orbitals of Pr(III) (4f2)
active_space_protocol: two electrons in the seven 4f orbitals; a step-by-step deconstruction was then run - without spin singlets in the SOC step, without embedding, replacing Cl- by point charges or by point charges with ECPs, and with a minimal basis set or a single 4f Slater function on Pr - in order to separate electrostatic from covalent contributions to the crystal-field parameters
nroots_per_mult: 21 spin-triplet and 28 spin-singlet states included in the spin-orbit coupling step
electronic_structure_description: Crystal-field parameters evaluated at three levels - 4f canonical (l = 3), SF-CASSCF (L = 5) and SO-CASSCF (J = 4) - to quantify how much of the crystal field is electrostatic and how much is covalent bonding. Covalency contributions to the CFPs are confirmed non-negligible.
reference_short: Alessandri, Zulfikri, Autschbach, Bolvin, Chem. Eur. J.
notes: Methodological study on the origin of the crystal field in rare-earth complexes. The step-by-step stripping of embedding, basis and ligand description is an unusually explicit protocol for separating electrostatic from covalent effects. d/f electron count 4f2 added 2026-08-05: arithmetic from the Pr(3) oxidation state recorded in this row, not a value stated by the paper.

compound_name: model lanthanide sandwich complexes of Dy(III): [Dy(eta5-C5H5)2]+ (LnCp), [Dy(eta6-C6H6)2]3+ (LnBz) and [Dy(eta8-C8H8)2]- (LnCOT)
ligand_set: two aromatic carbocyclic ligands in sandwich geometry: cyclopentadienide (Cp-), benzene (Bz) or cyclooctatetraenide (COT2-)
geometry_source: ligand geometry optimised at DFT-B3LYP/cc-pVTZ with NWChem 6.1 and verified by frequency analysis; the Ln-ring distance then optimised at CASPT2 with the ligand geometry frozen
method: spin-free CASSCF followed by spin-orbit state interaction with RASSI (SO-CASSCF); Ln-ligand distance optimised with CASPT2 for the sandwich complexes
software: MOLCAS 7.8; NWChem 6.1 for the DFT-B3LYP ligand geometry optimisations
basis_set: ANO-RCC of TZP quality on Ln and DZP on C and H; in the step-by-step procedure the ligands were replaced by three layers of point charges and Ln described by an 8s4p2d3f2g1h basis (TZP*) or a single 4f Slater function
relativistic_treatment: Douglas-Kroll-Hess transformation for scalar relativity; spin-orbit integrals via the atomic mean-field (AMFI) approximation
active_space_orbital_description: the seven Dy(III) 4f orbitals (4f9 configuration)
active_space_protocol: for a lanthanide of configuration 4f^N a CAS(N,7) is used; here CAS(9,7) for Dy(III)
electronic_structure_description: Series chosen because the interaction between Ln(III) and aromatic ligands is difficult to describe with a purely electrostatic crystal-field picture: these aromatic ligands form covalent bonds with the metal ion, so a quantitative description requires treating metal-ligand covalency explicitly. reference_short: Alessandri, Zulfikri, Autschbach, Bolvin, Chem. Eur. J.
notes: Three ligand types (Cp, Bz, COT) are studied for this lanthanide; the CASSCF active space is identical across them and depends only on the 4f^N configuration, so they are condensed into one row. d_electron_count left empty: the active space is the 4f shell. Superseding that: d/f electron count 4f9 added 2026-08-05: arithmetic from the Dy(3) oxidation state recorded in this row, not a value stated by the paper.

active_space_protocol: CAS[14,14] chosen to span all valence and bonding orbitals of the Ti-N-C-N core
electronic_structure_description: Natural orbital occupations from the CASSCF wavefunction: HOMO 1.68, LUMO 0.33 (beta = 0.312). Occupations below about 0.4 correspond to Ti(IV), so the complex is better described as Ti(IV) than Ti(III). notes: Active space written CAS[14,14] with square brackets rather than parentheses. Used here not for energetics but to settle a bonding question - which of three limiting resonance structures describes the Ti-C interaction - via natural-orbital occupations and Mayer bond orders.

notes: active_space_nel left EMPTY: the paper specifies the orbital content (five pi orbitals plus one sigma*, hence 6 orbitals) but never states the number of active electrons. geometry_source: DFT geometries (M06-2X, B3LYP, wB97X) from Gaussian 09
method: CASSCF and CASPT2, with DMRG for the larger active spaces; DFT-based unrestricted broken-symmetry as a cross-check
basis_set: two different basis sets compared for the CASSCF(12,12)/CASPT2(12,12) calculations
active_space_orbital_description: the pi space of the dimerising system; the maximum pi space for the reactant complex comprises the full set of pi orbitals and pi electrons of the two monomer units
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(12,12) and CASPT2(12,12) for the reactants, transition states and intermediates of the dimerisation step, with a larger (20,18) space accessible through DMRG; DMRG is expected to and does decrease the triplet-singlet gap relative to the smaller CAS
electronic_structure_description: Diradical character of the p-quinodimethane monomers and of the intermediate dimers along the Gilch polymerisation route. Complete-active-space methods were used precisely because DFT cannot describe the diradical character; specific substituents alter the monomer electronic structure and thereby the polymerisation mechanism.
reference_short: Nikolic, Wouters, Romanova et al.
notes: Records the (12,12) CAS used for the reported CASSCF/CASPT2 energies; a larger (20,18) space was reached with DMRG and is noted in the protocol. ground_state_mult left empty because the singlet-triplet ordering is itself the quantity under investigation and varies with substituent.

method: CASPT2//CASSCF

Optimised structures and minimum energy paths were computed with no geometric constraints imposed.
reference_short: Giussani, Merchan et al.
notes: A case where the active space needed no justification beyond the chromophore itself: the entire pi system is active.

ligand_set: two pentamethylcyclopentadienyl (Cp*) ligands and the 4,5-diazafluorene N-donor ligand
method: CASSCF with a perturbative PT2 correction; state-specific calculations

The active space was subsequently expanded to include additional pi* configurations on the substituted bipyridine ligand, with a perturbative PT2 correction added.
electronic_structure_description: Two open-shell singlets are calculated to lie BELOW the triplet state, and the observed temperature-dependent magnetism results from a Boltzmann equilibrium between those two open-shell singlet configurations - consistent with the low effective magnetic moment measured. metal_ox_state left empty: the multiconfigurational ground state is an intermediate-valence mixture rather than a single integer oxidation state, which is the point of the study.
reference_short: Nocton, Booth, Maron, Andersen
notes: Explicit documented equivalence test between a small and a large active space - (4,4) versus (12,8) - with the smaller one adopted after being shown to give similar results. That kind of stated justification is exactly what active_space_protocol is for.

For the A-type structure the O-O bond basin population V(O1,O2) is close to 1.3 electrons with the spin-integrated density almost fully localised in the C(Cu) and V(Cu,O) basins, indicating good electronic pairing of the O-O bond. NH3 ligands are noted as unable to accept strong charge transfer from Cu because of their saturated valence shell.
reference_short: Piquemal and Pilme
notes: active_space_nel left EMPTY: the six active orbitals are individually named by symmetry label but the number of active electrons is never stated. The paper is unusually explicit that the active space was chosen for comparability with DFT geometries, not on accuracy grounds.

electronic_structure_description: Electronic properties and 4f->5d transitions of the Ce3+ activator in Lu2SiO5, the emission mechanism underlying the LSO:Ce scintillator. method: CASSCF; DFT with the B3PW91 hybrid functional for comparison
basis_set: all-electron 6-31G(d,p) double-zeta on the light atoms

reference_short: Nocton, Booth et al.

compound_name: Ni(II) spin-crossover-related complex studied for second-order spin-orbit coupling between spin states
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 energies placed on the diagonal of the spin-orbit Hamiltonian
active_space_orbital_description: eight electrons and five orbitals of Ni 3d character
active_space_protocol: a minimal active space of eight electrons in five orbitals of Ni 3d character, which the authors note had already been shown to give rather accurate estimates of the spin-orbit interactions - i.e. the minimal space is adopted on the strength of prior validation rather than re-tested here
electronic_structure_description: Effect of second-order spin-orbit coupling on the interaction between spin states in spin-crossover systems. CASPT2 energies were placed on the diagonal of the spin-orbit Hamiltonian so that dynamic correlation and spin-orbit mixing are combined.
reference_short: Sousa et al., Chem. Eur. J.
notes: Contrast with the [Fe(bpy)3]2+ row from the same paper, which needed a much larger space: the minimal metal-only space suffices for the Ni(II) case but not where MLCT states matter.

method: CASSCF with CASPT2 energies placed on the diagonal of the spin-orbit Hamiltonian
active_space_orbital_description: the standard active space used for spin-state energetics in transition-metal complexes (metal 3d plus the 3d' double shell and ligand sigma donors), EXTENDED with a pi* orbital on one of the bipyridine ligands specifically to enable description of the metal-to-ligand charge-transfer states
active_space_protocol: ten electrons in thirteen orbitals: the standard spin-state-energetics active space for transition-metal complexes, extended by one bipyridine pi* orbital so that MLCT states can be described. The extension is made for a stated physical reason, not for convergence.
electronic_structure_description: Second-order spin-orbit coupling between the low-spin and high-spin states of a classic Fe(II) spin-crossover complex, with the MLCT manifold included because it mediates the interaction.
reference_short: Sousa et al., Chem. Eur. J.
notes: Good example of a space enlarged by exactly one orbital for an identified physical purpose (MLCT), rather than by a general convergence sweep. Same paper as the Ni(II) row, which uses a minimal (8,5).

method: state-specific CASSCF (SS-CASSCF); UHF for comparison of diradical character
active_space_orbital_description: a (6,5) space spanning the pi system of the distibabenzene ring bearing the diradical character
active_space_protocol: state-specific CASSCF with a (6,5) active space for the S0 ground state of 5; occupation patterns rather than a single configuration are reported, and further minor patterns are listed in the Supporting Information
electronic_structure_description: The S0 ground state with the (6,5) active space has natural-orbital occupation pattern 22200 (95%) with 21111 contributing 3%, i.e. predominantly closed-shell with measurable open-shell admixture. The diradical character of the dication (6)2+ is 36% by SS-CASSCF and 39% by UHF, and the open-shell singlet lies below the closed-shell singlet.
reference_short: Steffenfauseweh, Rottschafer, Vishnevskiy et al.
notes: Reports occupation PATTERNS (22200, 21111) with weights rather than a single dominant configuration, which is the natural way to quantify diradical character from a CAS wavefunction. Main-group (antimony) diradicaloid, no metal centre.

basis_set: def2-SV(P) for the CASSCF MECI optimisations; 6-31+G(d,p) for the DFT work
active_space_orbital_description: an (8,7) space spanning the pi system involved in the S0/S1 crossing
active_space_protocol: MECIs located at the CASSCF(8,7)/def2-SV(P) level; the CASSCF role is confined to locating the S0/S1 conical intersection geometries, with energies taken from TD-DFT
electronic_structure_description: Highly emissive fluorophores in solution and solid state. The S0/S1 MECI geometries of compounds 4 and 5 differ drastically, which is what explains their contrasting fluorescence behaviour - the accessibility of the conical intersection, not the vertical energies, controls emissivity.
reference_short: 2-methoxy and 2-morpholino pyridine fluorophores
notes: A common division of labour worth recording: CASSCF used ONLY to locate conical intersections, with all energetics from TD-DFT. The active space therefore needs to describe the crossing, not the whole spectrum.

compound_name: thorocene, ThCOT2 (bis(eta8-cyclooctatetraenyl)th), an actinocene sandwich complex
ligand_set: two eta8-cyclooctatetraenyl (COT) dianion rings in a sandwich arrangement
geometry_source: An-to-ring-centroid distance optimised against CASPT2 energies, with the COT ligand geometry held fixed
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 for the geometry optimisation and RASSI for state interaction; QTAIM topological analysis of the resulting densities
active_space_orbital_description: 16 orbitals: the highest occupied COT pi orbitals of au, b1u, ag and b1g symmetry; the seven actinide f orbitals of au (f-delta), b1u (f-sigma, f-delta), b2u (f-pi, f-phi) and b3u (f-pi, f-phi) symmetry; and five d orbitals of ag (d-sigma, d-delta), b1g (d-delta), b2g (d-pi) and b3g (d-pi) symmetry
active_space_protocol: a single 16-orbital active space is held FIXED across the whole Th-to-Cm series - COT pi donors plus the actinide 7f and 6d manifolds - with only the electron count changing, from 8 for Th to 14 for Cm. Written by the authors as CASSCF(n,16). The An-to-COT-centroid distance was optimised against CASPT2 energies with the COT ligand geometry held fixed.
electronic_structure_description: Ground-state electron density of thorocene, ThCOT2 computed at CASSCF and analysed topologically (QTAIM) to quantify the covalent contribution of f-orbital participation to An-COT bonding across the series. The multiconfigurational character of these complexes is assessed explicitly.
reference_short: Kerridge, f-orbital covalency in the actinocenes
notes: A seven-member isostructural series sharing one 16-orbital active space, so the (n,16) family maps directly onto the actinide 5f occupation. Because dynamic correlation enters via CASPT2 and spin-orbit via RASSI, the authors note it was not possible to generate total electron densities amenable to QTAIM from those steps, so the topological analysis is performed on the CASSCF densities. This compound is also studied in other papers already in this database under different DOIs; those are independent studies, not duplicates. d/f electron count 5f0 added 2026-08-05: arithmetic from the Th(4) oxidation state recorded in this row, not a value stated by the paper.

notes: One of the clearest stepwise active-space constructions in this database: valence d shell, plus the 3d' double shell, plus the ligand-field orbitals whose occupation changes between spin states - each addition justified by what the LS/HS comparison requires. compound_name: Cp'2Th(bipy), a bipyridyl thorium metallocene (Cp' = substituted cyclopentadienyl, bipy = 2,2'-bipyridine)

electronic_structure_description: Photodissociation channels of cyanoacetylene, relevant to the haze chemistry of Titan. In the T1 state the dissociation products are H(2S) + CCCN(X 2Sigma+) and HCC(X 2Sigma) + CN(X 2Sigma+); at CASPT2(14,13)//CASSCF(14,13)+ZPE the barriers for adiabatic dissociation of the C4-H5 and C2-C3 bonds are 6.11 and 6.94 eV in S1, and 5.71 and 6.39 eV in T1.
reference_short: Luo, Du, Duan et al.
notes: Another small-space-for-hard-geometries case: the full (14,13) is used for optimisations and energies, but conical-intersection/crossing-point searches fall back to (8,8).

Attempts to optimise the CUMULENIC geometry - at CASSCF(8,8) and at every functional tested - always yielded a saddle point with one or more imaginary frequencies (1900i cm-1 at CASSCF(8,8)), indicating the cumulenic form is not a minimum; CASSCF(8,8) gives alternating bond lengths of 1.199 and 1.356 A.
reference_short: Baryshnikov, Valiev, Kuklin et al.
notes: A case where CASSCF and DFT AGREE on a negative result - the cumulenic structure is a saddle point at every level tested, with a very large imaginary frequency at CASSCF(8,8).

compound_name: NO2, nitrogen dioxide - bent and cyclic forms
geometry_source: geometry optimisations at six levels of theory, guided by HF/3-21G scans
method: CASSCF at two active-space sizes; HF and MBPT(2), MBPT(3), MBPT(4) for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: an (8,8) valence space; a smaller CAS(4,6) was also used
active_space_protocol: two active spaces compared directly on the same question: CAS(4,6) and CAS(8,8), both with the 6-31+G(d) basis. The relative energies of the bent and cyclic forms shift substantially between them - the barrier from the linear form is 86.56 kcal/mol at CAS(4,6) but 76.85 kcal/mol at CAS(8,8) - so the space size materially changes the answer.
electronic_structure_description: Can NO2 exist in bent or cyclic forms? Stationary points located at 180 degrees (linear), around 86 degrees (bent) and around 42-47 degrees (cyclic). At CAS(8,8) the bent form lies 76.85 kcal/mol above and the cyclic form higher still; the corresponding CAS(4,6) values are 86.56 kcal/mol and 175.13 kcal/mol, and the HF values differ again (108.33 and 209.37 kcal/mol).
reference_short: Fuzery, Burcl, Torday, Csaszar et al.
notes: Useful as a direct demonstration that active-space size changes a chemical conclusion: the bent-form barrier moves by nearly 10 kcal/mol between CAS(4,6) and CAS(8,8) on the same geometry and basis.

method: CASSCF, used as a check on the basis-set and method dependence of the computed molecular properties
basis_set: ANO-S basis used for the check; HF orbital energies obtained with 6-31G** for the active-space selection
active_space_orbital_description: twelve orbitals selected around the frontier region; HOMO-3 through HOMO-5 lie within 0.41 eV of one another and were therefore included together rather than split
active_space_protocol: the active space was selected by STUDYING HF ORBITAL ENERGIES of neutral EDO-TTF with the 6-31G** basis: because HOMO-3 to HOMO-5 are close in energy (within 0.41 eV), they were kept together in the space rather than truncated between them - an explicit energy-gap criterion for where to cut the space.
electronic_structure_description: Ab initio molecular properties of the isolated EDO-TTF donor compared with those in the (EDO-TTF)2PF6 charge-transfer crystal, which undergoes a well-known photoinduced phase transition.
reference_short: Linker, van Loosdrecht et al.
notes: A rare explicit statement of the CRITERION used to choose where to truncate an active space: near-degeneracy of HF orbital energies, with a stated 0.41 eV window keeping HOMO-3 to HOMO-5 together.

geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimisations and vibrational analyses

reference_short: Chudoba et al., Chem. Phys. Lett. 1999
notes: Numeric fields left EMPTY: the space is described by which frontier orbitals it contains rather than by counts. Recorded for two reasons - the space is enlarged specifically for the TICT geometries by adding the orbital whose occupation changes, and the authors explicitly validate the small space against extended ones instead of merely asserting it.

method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by multistate CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) with an applied level shift of 0.4

active_space_protocol: eight electrons correlated in thirteen active orbitals, with state averaging over eight roots of A' symmetry and seven roots of A'' symmetry. nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over eight roots for the A' symmetry and seven roots for the A'' symmetry
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: a 1A', configuration (3dxz)2(3dxy)2(sigma Mn-CH3)2(3dyz)2. Multiconfigurational study of the low-lying excited states governing the photochemistry - the competition between Mn-CH3 homolysis and CO loss.
reference_short: Gonzalez and Daniel
notes: Notable for stating that the MULTISTATE form of CASPT2 is mandatory here rather than optional - a documented case where single-state CASPT2 is insufficient because of strong interaction between nearby excited states.

compound_name: Ce3+ centre in the CaF2 alkaline-earth fluoride crystal (also SrF2 and BaF2 hosts), a scintillator activator site
ligand_set: fluoride coordination environment of the substitutional Ce3+ site in the fluorite lattice
geometry_source: geometry optimisation performed at the CASSCF level on an embedded QM cluster; the classical region represented by ab initio model potentials (AIMPs), with bare Coulomb potentials beyond
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2, with spin-orbit and scalar relativistic effects included via RASSI
basis_set: ANO-RCC all-electron basis for Ce, F and Ca inside the QM cluster
relativistic_treatment: scalar relativistic effects with spin-orbit interaction included
active_space_orbital_description: an active space containing the 4f, 5d and 6s orbitals of the Ce ion - seven 4f, five 5d and one 6s, thirteen orbitals in total, holding the single 4f1 electron of Ce(III)
active_space_protocol: the active space is specified by naming the orbital shells it contains - 4f, 5d and 6s of Ce - rather than by counts; state-averaged CASSCF over the ground and excited states of the defect, with correlation added at CASPT2
electronic_structure_description: First-principles model of the spatial and electronic structure of Ce3+ centres in alkaline-earth fluoride crystals, including both scalar relativistic and spin-orbit effects. Including 4f, 5d and 6s in one space is what allows the interconfigurational 4f-5d transitions responsible for scintillation to be described.
reference_short: Ce3+ centres in alkaline-earth fluorides, IOP Conf. Ser.
notes: Same [4f,5d,6s] shell-naming convention as the Ce:Lu2SiO5 row elsewhere in this database; active_space_norb = 13 is the size of the named shells (7+5+1) and nel = 1 follows from the Ce(III) 4f1 configuration. Embedded-cluster model of a dopant site with AIMP representation of the host. d/f electron count 4f1 added 2026-08-05: arithmetic from the Ce(3) oxidation state recorded in this row, not a value stated by the paper.

software: MOLCAS (CASSCF/MS-CASPT2); in-house NEVPT2 code interfaced to MOLCAS; ORCA (NEVPT2 geometry optimizations)

electronic_structure_description: Ground state S0 is a multiconfigurational singlet with three dominant electron configurations, at a saddled geometry; T0 is planar and lies above it. Energy differences (kcal/mol): XMS-CASPT2(4e,5o) dE(S0-T0) 2.1, dH 2.1, dG 1.3; RASPT2(28e,2h,2e; 12o,5o,8o)/ANO-RCC dE 2.8, dH 2.8, dG 1.2. Between the two singlets, dE(S0-S1) 7.3, dH 7.5, dG 6.6. At the planar T0 geometry S0 and T0 become degenerate. Along the LIIC between the S0 and T0 minima the S0 multiconfigurational character falls off as the saddling angle decreases, while T0 stays single-reference. DFT dE(S0-T0) for comparison: PBE0-D3 -4.6, M06 -2.4, B3LYP-D3 -2.3, TPSSh-D3 3.0, M06-L 5.4, TPSS-D3 8.3, BLYP-D3 8.5, PBE-D3 9.6
Other: Saddling arises from electron transfer from a corrole pi orbital into the Cu d(x2-y2). Only TPSSh-D3 (10% HF exchange) approaches the XMS-CASPT2 energetics, and even then its singlet is the closed-shell state rather than the correct multiconfigurational one; increasing HF exchange favours the triplet. XMS-CASPT2 overestimates saddling while all the DFT functionals underestimate it. The XMS-CASPT2 dE(S0-T0) computed on TPSSh geometries differs by only 0.1 kcal/mol from that on the XMS-CASPT2 structure

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2F7/2. Ground Kramers doublet is 99.93% mJ = |+/-7/2| at CASSCF (99.7% at XMS-CASPT2), stabilized by 1054 cm-1 (CASSCF) / 1400 cm-1 (XMS-CASPT2). g-values: CASSCF 7.963, 0.087, 0.085; XMS-CASPT2 7.927, 0.336, 0.324; experiment 7.755, 0.512-0.540, 0.484-0.499. The g1 quantization axis lies 0.6 degrees from the normal to the ON2 coordination plane. Excited 2F5/2 states calculated (CASSCF/XMS-CASPT2) at 10,500/10,600 cm-1 for mJ = |+/-5/2|, 11,700/12,100 for |+/-3/2| and 12,100/12,500 for |+/-1/2|, in excellent agreement with the observed transitions. Room-temperature chi-T: free-ion 2.57, SQUID 2.58, CASSCF 2.21/2.15 cm3 mol-1 K
Other: CASSCF alone reproduces the ground-state composition seen by EPR but underpredicts the transverse g-values (<0.09); adding dynamic correlation via XMS-CASPT2 reproduces the magnetic data and brings the transverse g-values close to experiment. Despite the sizable crystal field and the highly pure prolate mJ = |+/-7/2| ground state expected from the equatorial coordination motif, the state mixing and large transverse g-values mean 2-Yb shows no single-molecule-magnet behaviour
reference_short: Gransbury, Nicholas, Murphy, Emerson-King, Vonci, Goodwin, Winpenny et al., Inorg. Chem. (2024)
notes: 4f13 is arithmetic from the stated Yb(III) oxidation state, recorded in d_electron_count per the corpus convention for lanthanides. ligand_set: 2x bis(tri-isopropylsilyl)amide N(Si iPr3)2- + 1x TEMPO- (2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidin-1-olate) anion; approximately trigonal planar N2O donor set

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 3H6. CASSCF gives a highly pure ground pseudodoublet, 49.98% |+6> + 49.98% |-6>, split by only 0.043 cm-1 and stabilized by 393 cm-1, with g1 = 13.95 (14 for a pure mJ = |+/-6|) oriented 0.3 degrees from the normal to the coordination plane. Isothermal reduced magnetization saturates at 2.80 N-mu-B, below the 3.50 N-mu-B of a pure mJ = |+/-6| state, indicating mixing
Other: Tm3+ is a non-Kramers ion, so the ground pseudodoublet is formally nondegenerate. The calculation reproduces the gradual chi-T decrease from 300 to 10 K but not the sharp downturn below 10 K nor the saturation magnetization: the experimental data and the absence of an EPR signal imply a ground-state splitting above 0.32 cm-1, whereas CASSCF gives 0.043 cm-1. The authors state plainly that computational methods cannot reach this sub-wavenumber accuracy and likely underestimate the ground-state mixing. XMS-CASPT2 was computationally prohibitive for Tm3+ because of the number of states
reference_short: Gransbury, Nicholas, Murphy, Emerson-King, Vonci, Goodwin, Winpenny et al., Inorg. Chem. (2024)

The full pi system of the parent free-base porphyrin would be (26,24) and was judged computationally too demanding; since the Gouterman four-orbital model is robust for porphyrins, the active space was restricted to those four frontier orbitals
electronic_structure_description: Lowest triplet state ZFS parameters from CASSCF(4,4)/def2-TZVP//B3LYP-D3(BJ)/TZ2P: D = 208e-4 cm-1, E = 5e-4 cm-1, against the TR-EPR simulation values D = 391e-4 cm-1 and E = -76e-4 cm-1. Relative triplet sublevel populations from the isotropically excited TR-EPR spectrum: px = 0.3, py = 0.6, pz = 0.1. The lowest triplet absorption is computed at 1.6739 eV (B2u), 97% HOMO -> LUMO+1. The ZFS Z axis is confirmed to lie along the out-of-plane direction and D is positive, as for other free-base analogues
Other: Stated by the authors to be the first calculation of a ZFS tensor for a porphyrin from a CASSCF wavefunction. DFT reproduces the spin density and hyperfine tensors well but gives unsatisfactory ZFS tensor elements, which is what motivated the multiconfigurational treatment; the small Gouterman active space already gives good semiquantitative results and the authors expect further improvement from adding dynamic correlation. The imposed D2h symmetry describes H2P well but represents only one conformer of H2TPPS4-, whose phenyl rings are forced perpendicular to the porphyrin plane
reference_short: Barbon, Dal Farra, Ciuti, Albertini, Bolzonello, Orian & Di Valentin, J. Chem. Phys. 152, 034201 (2020)
notes: Metal-free organic compound: metal_center = none, metal_ox_state / d_electron_count / ligand_set deliberately empty.
