geometry_source: DFT/TD-DFT optimized geometries (minima verified by frequency calculations, analytical Hessian in the ground state and numerical Hessian in the excited states); the S1-S0 conical intersection optimized at TD-B3LYP using first-order non-adiabatic coupling matrix elements and electron translation factors
method: single-point root-optimized CASSCF(10,10) with fully internally contracted DLPNO-NEVPT2 dynamic correlation
software: ORCA 5.0.3 (CASSCF, NEVPT2, MICD); Gaussian 09 for the DFT/TD-DFT geometries and NICS indices
basis_set: def2-TZVPP for the CASSCF/NEVPT2 wavefunctions; 6-311+G** and def2-TZVP used elsewhere in the DFT work
active_space_orbital_description: azulene's five pi and five pi* orbitals
active_space_protocol: (10,10) all-pi active space. An (U)MP2 wavefunction at the optimized geometry was used as the starting guess; a no-iteration run was performed first and the active space then rotated to contain azulene's 5 pi and 5 pi* orbitals, after which the full CASSCF(10,10)/def2-TZVPP with DLPNO-NEVPT2 was run. Root-optimized wavefunctions were converged separately for S1 and S2
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF(10,10) wavefunctions computed for S0, S1, S2, T1 and Qu1, with relative energies referenced to S0. The paper's Figure 4 caption pairs the S1 and S2 relative energies with the UV-vis absorption bands at 318 nm and 647 nm respectively. Aromaticity assignment from the CASSCF aromaticity indices: S1 is antiaromatic and S2 is aromatic, with S1 resembling T1 and S2 resembling Qu1 in energy, geometry, aromaticity index and EDDB value. The root-optimized S2 wavefunction has significant multireference character, assigning near-degenerate unpaired-electron occupancy to HOMO-1/LUMO and to HOMO/LUMO+1
Other: Magnetically induced current density at the CASSCF(10,10) level, plotted 1 au above the molecular plane, shows a diatropic ring current around the perimeter for S2 (as for S0) and a paratropic ring current for S1, localized mainly within the cyclopentadienyl and cycloheptatrienyl rings. Relaxation of S1 through the S1-S0 conical intersection provides unimolecular antiaromaticity relief, whereas the aromatic S2 is stabilized, undergoes little geometric relaxation and stays high in energy - which is the paper's explanation for azulene's anti-Kasha S2 fluorescence. CASSCF aromaticity indices were also computed at the optimized conical-intersection geometry
reference_short: Dunlop, Ludvikova, Banerjee, Ottosson & Slanina, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 145, 21569-21575 (2023)
notes: Metal-free organic compound: metal_center = none, metal_ox_state / d_electron_count / ligand_set deliberately empty. Method, software and basis set come from the Supporting Information (ja3c07625_si_001.pdf), fetched and read - the main text states none of them. multiplicities_studied '1,3,5' (numeric 2S+1) covers the S0/S1/S2 singlets, T1 and the quintet Qu1 that the paper compares. The state-to-wavelength pairing in electronic_structure_description is quoted exactly as the Figure 4 caption prints it; note that it is the reverse of azulene's conventional band assignment (weak S1 band in the visible near 650 nm, strong S2 band near 320 nm), so the caption may be transposed - no correction has been applied and no numerical relative energies are asserted, since those appear only inside the figure. nroots_per_mult left empty: states were separately root-optimized, not state-averaged over a stated number of roots.

compound_name: [FeIII(pzTp)(CN)3]-, a heteroleptic tricyanido iron(III) complex (pzTp = tetrakis(pyrazolyl)borate)
ligand_set: tetrakis(pyrazolyl)borate (pzTp, tridentate sigma-donor) + 3x cyanide (monodentate sigma-donor / pi-acceptor)
geometry_source: DFT-optimized geometry reproducing the single-crystal XRD structure of the 2MC state
method: CASSCF(5,5) with fully internally contracted NEVPT2 (FIC-NEVPT2); DFT/TD-DFT used in parallel for the state energies
software: not stated in the main text (details deferred to the Supporting Information)
basis_set: not stated in the main text (details deferred to the Supporting Information)
active_space_orbital_description: five electrons in five orbitals - the Fe(III) d5 manifold; the paper does not further specify the orbital composition in the main text
electronic_structure_description: The 4MC state is stabilized by 1.85 eV relative to the 2LMCT state (E0-0 = 2.38 eV = 19,230 cm-1), a result obtained by DFT and reproduced by CASSCF(5,5)/FIC-NEVPT2 (SI Table S2, Figure S4). This ordering contrasts with related Fe(III) complexes, where the 4MC state lies slightly above the 2LMCT state. Experimentally the complex shows a broad emission band centred at 600 nm at room temperature, assigned to radiative decay from the 2LMCT state, with a luminescence quantum yield of 0.02% and an 80 ps lifetime in chloroform

The 2LMCT excited state is reactive bimolecularly and photo-oxidizes several alcohols, with a cyanide-H bonded species identified as a key intermediate, establishing [Fe(pzTp)(CN)3]- as a photo-oxidant and a candidate emissive Fe-based photosensitizer
reference_short: Luminescence and Excited-State Reactivity in a Heteroleptic Tricyanido Fe(III) Complex, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 146, 954-960 (2024)
notes: d5 is arithmetic from the stated Fe(III) oxidation state. The main text mentions the CASSCF(5,5)/FIC-NEVPT2 result only in passing and puts the numbers in SI Table S2 and Figure S4; software, basis set and active-space composition are all deferred to the SI, which was not retrievable for this record, so those fields are left empty rather than guessed. The 1.85 eV stabilization and the 2.38 eV E0-0 are quoted from the main text. multiplicities_studied '2,4' (numeric 2S+1) covers the doublet LMCT and quartet MC states discussed.

geometry_source: ab initio energies computed on Jacobi-coordinate grids (R, r, theta), with the angular grid at Gauss-Legendre quadrature points over 0 <= theta <= 90 degrees by symmetry; grid details in SI Tables S1 and S2
method: MRCI with the Davidson correction (MRCI+Q) on CASSCF orbitals, and full configuration interaction (FCI) as an independent reference; both surfaces fitted with a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) representation
basis_set: aug-cc-pV6Z for the MRCI+Q surface; aug-cc-pV5Z for the FCI surface
active_space_orbital_description: the three 1s orbitals of the two hydrogen atoms and the helium atom
active_space_protocol: initial orbitals for the MRCI calculations came from a CASSCF with the three H and He 1s orbitals in the active space
electronic_structure_description: A new analytical full-dimensional potential energy surface for H2+-He built from an extensive set of ab initio energies at both MRCI+Q and FCI level. For the MRCI surface the long-range region is described by analytical functions smoothly joined to the short-range RKHS representation. All ro-vibrational states of the ground vibrational manifold were computed, with the focus on the near-dissociative states. The adiabatic surface is expressed as a many-body expansion in the three internuclear distances
Other: The system is a three-electron cation, so FCI is affordable and serves as an exact benchmark against which the MRCI+Q surface is judged - unusual for a PES paper and the reason two surfaces are reported
reference_short: Koner, San Vicente Veliz, van der Avoird & Meuwly, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. (2019)
notes: Triatomic system, so admitted under the standing convention that excludes bare diatomics and free atoms but admits triatomics and larger. metal_center = none (no metal); metal_ox_state / d_electron_count / ligand_set deliberately empty. active_space_norb = 3 is stated by the paper ('three 1s orbitals of H and He in the active space'); active_space_nel = 3 is arithmetic from the composition of HeH2+ (2 electrons from He, 1 from H2+) and is not written out as (3,3) in the text - flagged here rather than presented as a quotation.

compound_name: [Fe2RuCl4(mu3-O)(mu-OMe)(mu-pz)2(NO)(Hpz)2] (complex 6), a mu3-oxido heterotrinuclear diiron(III)-ruthenium(II) nitrosyl cluster, neutral form [6]0

software: ORCA 4.2.0 (CASSCF/NEVPT2 with the RIJCOSX approximation); le_pychemy_go and IQmol used to process and visualize the TD-DFT spectrum
active_space_orbital_description: 10 electrons in 10 orbitals accounting for the d electrons of the two iron atoms
active_space_protocol: (10,10) for the neutral species - the d electrons of the two Fe atoms; the oxidized species uses 9 electrons correlated in 10 orbitals and the reduced species (11,11), the latter extended to include the interaction within the [RuIII(NO)]3+ moiety
electronic_structure_description: Spin-state ladder of [6]0 relative to the S = 5 (multiplicity 11) state, which is lowest. B3LYP/def2-SVP relative energies (kJ/mol): 13[6]0 101.1; 11[6]0 0.0; 9[6]0 37.0; 7[6]0 96.7; 5[6]0 155.0. BLYP: 119.4; 0.0; 1.5; 32.0; 73.0. CASSCF relative energies (kJ/mol): 9[6]0 -0.3; 7[6]0 -0.6; 5[6]0 -0.8. NEVPT2: -0.7; -1.4; -1.9. Exchange coupling J for the neutral species, extracted for S = 5 with dE relative to S = 0: CASSCF -0.067 kJ/mol (-5.6 cm-1), NEVPT2 -0.159 kJ/mol (-13.3 cm-1); BLYP gives -39.0 cm-1 and the experimental value is -49.4 cm-1

CASSCF gives smaller low-spin/high-spin gaps than B3LYP; NEVPT2 agrees closely with B3LYP for the oxidized and reduced forms but is still smaller by a factor of two for the neutral complex. reference_short: Stepanenko, Mizetskyi, Orlowska, Bucinsky, Zalibera et al., Inorg. Chem. (2021)
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count left empty: the cluster is mixed-metal (two Fe plus one Ru) with a redox-noninnocent {RuNO}6 nitrosyl, so no single oxidation state or d count describes the row - the paper's own point is that the NO ligand's redox state is ambiguous. multiplicities_studied is the numeric 2S+1 ladder actually tabulated in Table 2 for [6]0. Low-spin states were preferentially targeted in the state-specific CASSCF for the neutral and reduced species. correlation_correction NEVPT2 follows from the method.

compound_name: o-LHBI, a locked ortho-hydroxybenzylidene-imidazolinone GFP model chromophore (truncated o-LHBDI without the two methyl groups)
geometry_source: minima, conical intersections, minimum-energy potential energy profiles and nudged-elastic-band paths optimized at state-averaged CASSCF with equal state weights; initial structures from B3LYP DFT
method: state-averaged CASSCF(10,8) for geometries and paths, MS-CASPT2//CASSCF single points for energies (no IPEA shift, 0.2 au imaginary shift, Cholesky decomposition with unbiased auxiliary basis sets); semiempirical OM2/MRCI for the nonadiabatic surface-hopping dynamics

active_space_protocol: (10,8) for the ab initio work - seven pi/pi* orbitals carrying eight pi electrons plus one n lone-pair orbital with two electrons, chosen as a balance between accuracy and efficiency for CASSCF excited-state geometry optimization of a medium-size molecule. The separate semiempirical OM2/MRCI active space is 14 electrons in 13 orbitals: the six highest doubly occupied orbitals, the two singly occupied orbitals and the five lowest unoccupied orbitals, with three reference configuration state functions (the SCF configuration and the two closed-shell configurations derivable from its HOMO and LUMO) and all single and double excitations from them
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation to S1 at the enol Franck-Condon point (S0-ENOL): 82.1 kcal/mol at MS-CASPT2 and 81.7 kcal/mol at OM2/MRCI, against an experimental 73.5 kcal/mol for o-LHBDI in toluene. Vertical emission at the S1 keto minimum (S1-KETO): 42.4 kcal/mol at MS-CASPT2 and 45.8 kcal/mol at OM2/MRCI, against 48.9 kcal/mol experimentally. At the Franck-Condon point S1 is primarily the HOMO -> LUMO configuration, the two orbitals being bonding and antibonding respectively across the C2-C3 bond, and this character is unchanged at S1-KETO. The two enol-type S1/S0 conical intersections S0S1-ENOL-1 and S0S1-ENOL-2 lie 12.2 kcal/mol below the enol S1 minimum and 24.3 kcal/mol below the S1 energy at the Franck-Condon point at MS-CASPT2 level; their central C2-C3 bond is much longer than at the S1 enol minimum (1.442 vs 1.395 A). The S1 enol-keto tautomerization is essentially barrierless; deactivation from S1-ENOL to S0S1-ENOL-1 is barrierless at OM2/MRCI and has small barriers of about 5 and 3 kcal/mol at CASSCF and MS-CASPT2//CASSCF
Other: 2 ps OM2/MRCI trajectory surface-hopping dynamics show excited-state intramolecular proton transfer averaging 35 fs, after which the chemical locking prevents the S1 keto species from reaching the keto S1/S0 conical intersections, so most trajectories stay trapped in the S1 keto region for the whole simulation - this trapping is what enhances the fluorescence quantum yield relative to unlocked o-HBI. For the para-substituted models p-HBI and p-LHBI, locking barely affects the efficient cis-trans-isomerization deactivation, so their quantum yields stay very low. The OM2/MRCI and CASSCF S1/S0 profiles have similar shapes, with the OM2/MRCI energies closer to the more accurate MS-CASPT2//CASSCF values

geometry_source: B3LYP-D3(BJ) optimized structures (Turbomole v7.4); symmetry-constrained optimizations that turned out to be transition states were reoptimized without symmetry so all ground-state structures are true minima
method: DMRG-CASSCF with DMRG-CASPT2 (IPEA shift 0.25 au, imaginary shift 0.1 au), semicore correlation added by UB3LYP-CCSD(T) in a spin-unrestricted CASPT2/CC scheme; localized-orbital (R)CASCI for the valence-bond analysis; B3LYP and B3LYP* for comparison
software: OpenMolcas interfaced with the CheMPS2 DMRG library; Turbomole v7.4 (B3LYP-D3(BJ) geometry optimizations); ORCA v4.2 (UB3LYP-CCSD(T) semicore correction)
basis_set: ANO-RCC contracted to [7s6p5d3f2g1h] for the metals, [4s3p2d1f] for C, N and O, [5s4p2d1f] for Cl and [3s1p] for H; Cholesky decomposition of the two-electron integrals at 1e-6 au; def2-TZVP (metals) / def2-SVP (ligands) for the geometry optimizations
active_space_orbital_description: five Fe(3d) orbitals, a maximum of five Fe(4d) correlating orbitals, one sigma(Fe-N) orbital, and all corrole pi orbitals except the eight localized on the corrole beta-carbons
active_space_protocol: CAS(24,25) or CAS(24,26) depending on whether the problematic Fe(4d) orbital is retained. General construction rule stated by the authors: all metal nd orbitals, all correlating (n+1)d orbitals for the double-shell effect, and all ligand orbitals able to interact with the metal nd orbitals. Where a state has an empty metal nd orbital the corresponding (n+1)d orbital rotates out and was removed, which is why several complexes carry two active-space sizes. A separate set of minimal localized-orbital (R)CASCI spaces was used for the valence-bond analysis: CAS(4,4) Fe[Cor]Cl, CAS(5,5) Mn[Cor]Cl, CAS(6,5) Fe[Cor]Ph, CAS(7,6) Mn[Cor]Ph, CAS(6,6) Fe[Cor](NO), CAS(6,6) Ru[Cor](NO), CAS(3,3) Mo[Cor]Cl2, each built from the singly occupied metal d orbitals, one corrole pi orbital and the axial-ligand orbitals that mix strongly with the metal d orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: Second most noninnocent of the seven complexes. The ferromagnetically coupled Fe(III)-Cor(2-) radical state lies about 10 kcal/mol above the antiferromagnetically coupled ground state at DMRG-CASPT2, but it is not the first excited state: that lies only 4.4 kcal/mol up and is a high-spin (locally S = 5/2) Fe(III) centre antiferromagnetically coupled to a corrole A' radical
Other: Roos et al. previously studied this molecule at CASPT2/ANO-RCC-TZVP with CAS(14,13) and CAS(14,14). Their relative energies are systematically higher than the DMRG-CASPT2/CC values here, from about 1 kcal/mol for the 5A''-3A'' gap up to 19 kcal/mol for the 1A''-3A'' gap, which the authors attribute to those active spaces being too small. The two small spaces also disagree with each other - the 3A'-3A'' gap is 18.6 kcal/mol with CAS(14,13) but 26.1 kcal/mol with CAS(14,14) - leading the authors to conclude that as many macrocycle pi orbitals as possible must be active to compare noninnocent states
reference_short: Phung, Muchammad, Yanai & Ghosh, JACS Au (2021)
notes: DMRG bond dimension m = 4000 in all calculations; the Fe[Cor](NO) triplet-singlet splitting is stated to converge to within 0.1 kcal/mol already at m = 2000. Core and semicore electrons frozen in CASPT2 (through 3s/3p for Mn and Fe, 4s/4p for Ru and Mo), with the semicore contribution added separately by UB3LYP-CCSD(T) and found to be about 1 kcal/mol in every complex. metal_ox_state is deliberately left empty for the noninnocent cases: quantifying how far the oxidation state is ill-defined is the paper's entire subject, so assigning one would contradict the source. Energies are in kcal/mol as reported.

ligand_set: 4x bridging formate (paddle-wheel); CO2 adsorbed at the open axial metal site
geometry_source: M06-L/cc-pVDZ optimized cluster models; CO2-Cu distance fixed at 2.4 A for both the linear and tilted conformations
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 (imaginary shift 0.1 au, default IPEA shift 0.25 au); ROS-MP2, which the authors note is equivalent to (2,2) CASPT2; M06-L and M06 DFT for comparison

DFT/ROS-MP2 used cc-pVDZ, aug-cc-pVDZ, cc-pVTZ and aug-cc-pVTZ
active_space_orbital_description: the larger space explored is 10 electrons in 10 orbitals; the minimal (2,2) space contains the two electrons and two orbitals of the Cu-Cu interaction, for which CASSCF is equivalent to restricted open-shell HF and CASPT2 to ROS-MP2
active_space_protocol: (2,2) minimal space capturing the Cu-Cu interaction - equivalent to ROS-HF at CASSCF level and to ROS-MP2 at CASPT2 level; (10,10) the larger space tested. Both singlet and triplet lowest spin states were explored, and calculations were run without symmetry
electronic_structure_description: The singlet is the ground state in every case, lying 3 kJ/mol below the triplet - in good agreement with the experimental MOF-11 values of 3.4 kJ/mol (water-bound) and 5.3 kJ/mol (anhydrous). CASPT2 interaction energies between Cu2(formate)4 and CO2 for the singlet ground state, in kJ/mol, counterpoise-corrected with uncorrected values in parentheses, for BS1 / BS2 / BS3: linear (2,2) -15.0 (-43.2) / -18.7 (-33.5) / -20.2 (-31.7); linear (10,10) -14.8 (-46.6) / -18.6 (-36.8) / -20.1 (-35.0); tilted (2,2) -17.7 (-49.3) / -23.5 (-40.0) / -25.8 (-39.6); tilted (10,10) -15.8 (-51.1) / -21.8 (-41.7) / -23.9 (-41.1)
Other: The dicopper singlet ground state is genuinely multiconfigurational and needs a multiconfigurational treatment; the monocopper system is single-configurational and adequately described by MP2, as is the triplet state of the Cu2 system. Enlarging the active space from (2,2) to (10,10) changes the interaction energy by only about 1-2 kJ/mol, which is what justifies the authors' use of the much cheaper ROS-MP2 to parametrize a new UFF pairwise potential. Conventional DFT, even with dispersion corrections, severely underestimates the Cu paddle-wheel/CO2 interaction; the reparametrized force field reproduces the experimental CO2 adsorption isotherms of HKUST-1 and is transferable to other copper paddle-wheel MOFs

metal_ox_state: II in the reactant, III in the product
ligand_set: 2x iodido + 4x tetrahydrofuran (explicit first solvation shell); acetone as the electron acceptor
geometry_source: PBE0-D3(BJ) optimized gas-phase structures; ACE-SmII I2 optimized with ECP52MWB-II and ACE(radical)-SmIII I2 with ECP51MWB-SV
method: all-electron CASSCF and CASPT2 including scalar relativistic effects; PBE0-D3(BJ) and a small-core Stuttgart-Dresden ECP benchmarked against them
software: not named in the extracted text
basis_set: all-electron basis with scalar relativistic treatment for the CASPT2; ECP52MWB-II and ECP51MWB-SV small-core pseudopotentials for the DFT geometries
relativistic_treatment: scalar relativistic effects included in the all-electron CASPT2
soc_included: no - spin-orbit coupling is explicitly stated to be excluded, along with thermal corrections and the second solvation shell
active_space_orbital_description: the seven Sm 4f orbitals plus the ligand orbital of interest, extended by five further correlating orbitals expected to represent the Sm 5d shell (higher angular momentum functions mix in during orbital optimization)
active_space_protocol: (6,8) initial space - the seven 4f orbitals plus the ligand orbital of interest with the appropriate electron count; (6,13) adds five correlating orbitals expected to be the 5d shell. The larger space changed the triplet-quintet spin-splitting energies appreciably, so only (6,13) results are reported
electronic_structure_description: Gas-phase single-electron-transfer energy dE = E(ACE-radical-SmIII I2(THF)4) - E(ACE-SmII I2(THF)4), in kJ/mol: CASSCF(6,13) 51.94; CASPT2(6,13) 48.94. The transfer is therefore endothermic and the equilibrium lies on the acetone side, not the ketyl-radical side. The perturbative correction is only 3.00 kJ/mol, which the authors read as CASSCF(6,13) already accounting well for dynamic correlation. DFT comparisons (kJ/mol): TPSS-D3 12.76; PBE-D3 28.91; TPSSH-D3 27.28; PBE0-D3 53.19; B3LYP-D3 55.40; BHLYP-D3 38.42; B3PW91-D3 69.66; B3PW91 40.02
Other: Lewis structures routinely imply a ketyl radical forms when SmI2 binds a carbonyl; these calculations say the equilibrium sits on the unreduced acetone side. PBE0-D3(BJ) with a small-core ECP reproduces the CASPT2 energy closely (53.19 vs 48.94 kJ/mol) while non-hybrid PBE and TPSS are far too low. compound_name: QMspin carbene chemical space - approximately 8,000 diverse carbene scaffolds derived from QM9 (H, C, N, O, F)
geometry_source: carbene scaffolds combinatorially derived from the QM9 chemical space, optimized separately in the singlet and triplet states; spin gaps reported both vertically at each spin state's geometry (dE(s-t)//t and dE(s-t)//s) and adiabatically
method: state-averaged CASSCF over the two spin states with a (2e,2o) active space, followed by explicitly correlated MRCISD+Q-F12 (Davidson-corrected)
active_space_orbital_description: the two electrons in the two non-bonding orbitals of the divalent carbene carbon, denoted r and s; natural orbitals of the one-particle state-averaged density matrix in this space reproduce the chemical picture of the carbene lone pair and empty p orbital
active_space_protocol: (2,2) throughout - CASSCF state-averaged over the singlet and triplet, with the two non-bonding carbene orbitals active, then MRCISD+Q-F12 on that reference. The minimal space is deliberate: it is what allows the singlet's resonance stabilization to be measured directly as the mixing of two closed-shell configurations
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over the two spin states (one singlet, one triplet)
electronic_structure_description: A hard upper limit on the singlet-triplet gap emerges at about 30 kcal/mol across every carbene class in this chemical space, which the authors attribute to strong electron correlation. Within many individual classes the spin-gap ranges are much larger: over 100 kcal/mol vertically and over 60 kcal/mol adiabatically. The singlet ground state is described by two closed-shell configurations with coefficients cR and cS on the non-bonding orbitals r and s; their mixing is quantified by an entanglement angle theta = arctan(|cS|/|cR|) with cR >= cS, ranging from 0 degrees (weak resonance stabilization) to 45 degrees (maximum stabilization, two equally weighted configurations). The triplet-state bond angle at the carbene centre distributes around 130 degrees
Other: Carbene classes group into (a) sigma-electron-withdrawing, pi-electron-donating alpha-substituents such as oxo- and amino-carbenes, which strongly stabilize the singlet; (b) aliphatic and aromatic alpha-substituents such as vinyl-, alkynyl-, alkyl- and aryl-carbenes, which stabilize the triplet or give a near-zero gap; and (c) moderately sigma- and pi-withdrawing substituents such as cyano- and carbonyl-carbenes, where carbonyl-carbenes show strong conformational effects. For almost 90% of the initial candidates the divalent carbon was confirmed to have two well-localized non-bonding orbitals, i.e. to be a genuine carbene
reference_short: Schwilk, Tahchieva & von Lilienfeld, Large yet bounded: spin gap ranges in carbenes
notes: Metal-free organic compounds: metal_center = none, metal_ox_state / d_electron_count / ligand_set deliberately empty. This is ONE condensed row for a chemical-space study of about 8,000 carbenes and roughly 13,000 MRCI calculations, not one row per compound - the same treatment given to other benchmark-set papers in this database. Per-compound spin gaps live in the QMspin dataset released with the paper and are not transcribed here. The row is admissible under the bulk-table policy because both tests pass: the DOI genuinely sources the calculations (this paper performed them) and the active space is explicitly stated, unlike the Excited_states_energy.csv table that was rejected. compound_name, formula and point_group describe the space rather than a single molecule, by necessity.

'Participating atoms' are those on which the frontier orbitals reside - the substituent carbons of systems 6 and 7 count, the substituents of 3, 4 and 5 do not. Each CASSCF level has a matching RASSCF valence-pi and limited-pi partition. For this system: eCPO (20,22), 6e10 singlet CSFs - too large to run as CASSCF; mCPO (12,14), 2e7 CSFs; piCPO (4,6), 105 CSFs; nCPO (2,4), 10 CSFs. electronic_structure_description: The first five excited states were compared across the three active spaces. CASSCF places the states in the same order as Amatatsu et al and therefore disagrees with the ADC(2) calculations of Kramer et al: B3g comes out with energies consistently similar to B2u, with B1u not far away. RS2C perturbation corrections lower the state energies but do not change the ordering. DFT-MRCI instead places B1u as S1, and since DFT-MRCI agrees with both ADC(2) and TDDFT, the authors conclude B1u is likely the true S1. 1B2u and 1B3g are characterised as primarily pi-pi* excitations, consistent with Amatatsu

The HOMO-4 in-plane acetylene pi bond is reassigned here to B2g rather than the B2u of the earlier work. software: OpenMolcas (CASSCF/CASPT2/RASSI); ADF 2013.01 (PBE/TZ2P geometry, SAOP absorption spectrum)

active_space_protocol: CAS(6,7) - the authors describe the active-space choice for a Ln(III) ion as trivial (all n 4f electrons in the seven 4f orbitals) and argue that the genuinely difficult and usually undocumented parameter is instead the dimension of the configuration-interaction matrices, i.e. how many states per spin multiplicity to include. The CASPT2 correlation orbital space was restricted to the central Eu(III) ion and the ligand donor atoms via the AFREeze keyword
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 7F0. State energies in cm-1 (TD-DFT/LB94 / CAS(6,7) / CAS(6,7)PT2 / experimental Eu complex / experimental free Eu3+ ion): 7F0 0/0/0/0/0; 7F1 860/359/384/392/379; 7F2 1171/1029/1091/1119/1043; 7F3 1935/1929/2025/1955/1896; 7F4 2934/2977/3088/2898/2869; 7F5 3995/4110/4214/-/3912; 7F6 6440/5294/5370/-/4992; excited 5D0 16339/22789/20214/17302/17227. Each 7FJ term at the CASSCF level is taken as the barycentre of the manifold generated by crystal-field splitting
Other: The paper's target is a systematic evaluation of J-J mixing and of how many states must enter the CI matrices - a choice it notes is usually made heuristically or not discussed at all in the literature. The Eu(III) 4f6 configuration gives 3003 microstates, whose degeneracy is lifted by electron repulsion, then spin-orbit coupling, then the crystal field in decreasing order of magnitude. The authors also highlight the shortcomings of DFT for systems with high spin multiplicity and strong correlation: TD-DFT places 5D0 at 16339 cm-1 against an experimental 17302, while CAS(6,7)PT2 gives 20214
reference_short: Babetto, Carlotto, Carlotto, Rancan, Bottaro, Armelao & Casarin, Inorg. Chem. 60, 315-324 (2021)
notes: 4f6 is arithmetic from the stated Eu(III) oxidation state, recorded in d_electron_count per the corpus convention for lanthanides. multiplicities_studied '7,5' are the numeric 2S+1 values of the 7FJ ground manifold and the 5D0 emitter state. nroots_per_mult is deliberately left empty despite being the paper's central topic: it reports a systematic scan of how many states per multiplicity to include rather than a single production value, and the per-multiplicity counts are given in the Results discussion rather than as one setting. The row describes the simplified model complex the CASSCF was actually run on, not the full experimental complex.

active_space_orbital_description: one orbital per irreducible representation of D2h: the 12ag, 11b1u, 2b1g, 2b2g, 3b3u, 10b2u, 2au and 9b3g molecular orbitals, being the four highest occupied and four lowest unoccupied orbitals

MRCI describes in a balanced way the manifold of electronic states derived from the dangling bonds created by removing two neighbouring carbon atoms from the graphene network. Unrestricted DFT agrees with MRCI on the 1Ag ground state and on the assignment of the lowest excited states, and the linear interpolation curves between unrelaxed and relaxed defect structures also agree well

The authors' earlier MRCI work on the single vacancy found a complex set of closely spaced states driving geometry relaxation with carbon-carbon bond formation, and showed the state manifold to be significantly more complicated than previously anticipated, with avoided crossings between states

notes: Metal-free carbon system: metal_center = none, metal_ox_state / d_electron_count / ligand_set deliberately empty. ligand_set: 2x pentaisopropylcyclopentadienyl (CpiPr5), no ligand truncation
method: CASSCF with spin-orbit coupling by RASSI state interaction (CASSCF-SO-RASSI) for an effective S = 1/2, with the relativistic hyperfine Hamiltonian to DKH1/DKH2

compound_name: O2-O2 van der Waals dimer - interaction of two rigid ground-state O2(3Sigma-g) monomers
geometry_source: rigid-rotor intermolecular grid: monomers held at re = 2.28 bohr, 1170 points computed for each spin state over the intermolecular coordinates (H/rectangular D2h, X, T-shape and skewed geometries all sampled)
method: CASSCF-based internally contracted MRCI+Q and CASPT2 for the interaction energies, counterpoise-corrected, with the asymptotic size-consistency residual at R = 70 bohr subtracted; combined with RCCSD(T) into the composite CC-MRCI and CC-PT2 surfaces
basis_set: 5s4p3d2f atomic natural orbital basis plus a (3s3p2d1f) bond-function set placed at the midpoint of the complex

CC-PT2 and CC-MRCI give very similar singlet and triplet curves, CC-PT2 being slightly more attractive: well-depth differences of about 0.5 meV (4%) for the singlet and 0.3 meV (3%) for the triplet. Against the empirical Perugia potential the largest discrepancy is for the singlet, whose Perugia well is about 1.8 meV deeper than CC-PT2, with best agreement for the quintet. The triplet surface has its absolute minimum at the rectangular H geometry near R = 6 bohr; the quintet has a global minimum at the X geometry and a local minimum at a planar skewed structure.
Other: The size-consistency error is about an order of magnitude smaller for CASPT2 (about 50 meV before subtraction) than for MRCI. Davidson's correction was added to the MRCI energies. Triplet-singlet splittings are dominated by the (000), (448), (202), (224) and (6410) spherical-harmonic components, the (448) relevance tracing to the nodal character of the singly occupied pi_g monomer orbitals.

notes: Mined from the OA text. compound_name: formyl radical HCO and the H...CO transition state of the H + CO addition reaction
geometry_source: structures optimized at each correlated level (MP2, RCCSD, RCCSD(T), MRCI, MRCI+Q) with cc-pVXZ, X = D, T, Q; surfaces fit with SURVIB (26 points for the H...CO TS and HCO) and VIBROTN (9 points for CO)

Reaction ergicities at the CBS limit (kcal/mol): MRCI+Q -13.7, RCCSD(T) -13.8, RCCSD -13.3, MRCI -11.5, MP2 -17.99. The measured barrier is 2.0 +/- 0.4 kcal/mol, about 2 kcal/mol below the best computed value; the 0 K bond energies from measured enthalpies, 14.3 and 13.9 kcal/mol, agree well with MRCI+Q and RCCSD(T).

geometry_source: roughly 67 000 MRCI/cc-pVTZ energies fitted to a global surface; stationary-point configurations optimized at the MRCI level
method: multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) with the Davidson correction for quadruple excitations, used uniformly over the whole surface rather than stitching CCSD(T) and MRCI regions together

point_group: linear, centrosymmetric (D-infinity-h); the excited-state optimizations were constrained to be linear and centrosymmetric
geometry_source: ground-state geometry from RCCSD(T) with a composite sp(aug-cc-pVTZ)/1df(cc-pVTZ) basis; excited-state geometry separately optimized at RHF, RCCSD and RCCSD(T) with the same composite basis
method: internally contracted MRCI with the Davidson correction on a CASSCF reference wave function, for vertical excitation energies; RHF, RCCSD and RCCSD(T) for the geometries
basis_set: spd part of aug-cc-pVQZ for the CASSCF/MRCI vertical excitations; composite sp(aug-cc-pVTZ) + 1df(cc-pVTZ) basis for the geometry optimizations
active_space_orbital_description: nine electrons distributed over an active space composed of the 8sigma_g, 7sigma_u, 2pi_g and 2pi_u orbitals
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X2Pig. The two lowest dipole-allowed transitions of C7- are to 2Piu states. The A2Piu state is dominated (about 81%) by the ...8sigma_g^2 7sigma_u^2 1pi_g^4 2pi_u^3 2pi_g^2 configuration, with similar-magnitude contributions from the other space occupations of the 2pi_u and 2pi_g orbitals. The computed vertical excitation energy including the Davidson correction is 2.3 eV, within 0.3 eV of the observed A2Piu-X2Pig band origin.

compound_name: ozone O3 - oxygen K-edge core-excited states (worked example of the CVS-MRCI scheme)
point_group: C2v (the distinct-row-table example is labelled Cs, the symmetry used to build the reference configuration space)
geometry_source: ground-state geometry optimized with multireference second-order perturbation theory (MRPT2)/aug-cc-pVTZ
method: GUGA-based MRCISD with the core-valence separation approximation (CVS-MRCI): ground-state MCSCF orbitals, target core orbital rotated into the active space, CVS-MCSCF for the core-excited states, then a CVS-MRCI expansion with single and double excitations and non-core/redundant configurations eliminated
software: BDF program package (CASSCF and Xi'an-CI modules)
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ; relativistic aug-cc-pVTZ-DK used for the scalar-relativistic corrections
relativistic_treatment: second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess scalar relativistic correction (core-orbital energy lowering averages -0.408 eV for O 1s)
active_space_orbital_description: valence CAS(6,6) for the ground state; the reference configuration space for the core-excited calculation is the restricted space RAS(8,7), i.e. 8 electrons in 7 orbitals, formed by appending the 1s core orbital of the central O atom (the target core orbital) to the valence space and requiring it to be empty or singly occupied
active_space_protocol: (6,6) valence CAS for the ground state; extended to RAS(8,7) by rotating the target core orbital into the active space, with configurations having the core orbital doubly occupied eliminated to enforce core-valence separation
electronic_structure_description: Oxygen K-edge core excitations. The 529.1 eV feature of the ozone X-ray absorption spectrum, nominally a terminal-oxygen 1s excitation, is assigned by these CVS-MRCI calculations as a two-electron excited state - electrons promoted from Ot(1s) and 9a' into 3a'' respectively - rather than a single core excitation.
Other: The authors argue multi-electron excitation character is widespread in core-excited states of small molecules and requires a multiconfigurational treatment; the same reassignment is made for the 538.9 eV O2 peak, conventionally read as O 1s -> 3s sigma_g. Core-valence correlation in the basis set had negligible effect on the simulated spectra.
reference_short: GUGA-based MRCI with core-valence separation (CVS) for core-excited states (2023)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Method paper; ozone is the one system whose active space is stated explicitly (CAS(6,6) -> RAS(8,7)), so it gets the single row. The broader benchmark is reported as deviation distributions over first- and second-row elements without per-molecule active spaces, and O2 is discussed but is a bare diatomic. The 529.1 eV value is the absorption feature being assigned; the text does not separate a computed number from the measured one, so it is described rather than filed as a computed excitation energy.

compound_name: NaFH reactive system (1A' ground state) for Na(3S) + HF(v,j) -> NaF + H, covering the van der Waals well and the late saddle point
point_group: Cs (all calculations performed within Cs symmetry)
geometry_source: 37 000 ab initio points spanning the interaction region and both the Na + HF and NaF + H asymptotes, fitted by three-dimensional cubic spline interpolation
method: internally contracted MRCI with the Davidson correction (icMRCI+Q) on state-averaged CASSCF reference configuration state functions, the average taken with equal weights over the 1 2A' and 2 2A' states; about 2.0e6 contracted (6.6e7 uncontracted) configurations
active_space_orbital_description: seven electrons in eight valence orbitals: the 3s and 3p orbitals of Na, the 2p orbitals of F and the 1s orbital of H; inner orbitals constrained doubly occupied but fully optimized
electronic_structure_description: Ground doublet surface, with the CASSCF reference state-averaged over 1 2A' and 2 2A'. Energetics on the new surface: endoergicity dE = D0(HF) - D0(NaF) = 1.02 eV, against an experimental estimate of 0.87-0.93 eV; van der Waals well depth -0.082 eV relative to the Na(3S) + HF asymptote (the earlier TTCPP-B surface gives -0.074 eV); barrier height 1.002 eV relative to the same asymptote, well below TTCPP-B (1.270 eV) and the semiempirical surface (1.266 eV) and close to Lagana's corrected value (0.811 eV). The saddle point is later and less bent than on TTCPP-B, with theta(NaFH) near Lagana's 75 degrees.
Other: Equilibrium geometries and dissociation energies of the separated HF and NaF diatomics agree closely with experiment. The surface is smooth from asymptotic to interaction regions and so flat near the saddle point that the barrier is inconspicuous, matching earlier MRCI and MBPT(2) observations. Quantum wave-packet dynamics on the new surface improve agreement with measured rates for HF(v = 2), consistent with the earlier surface having overestimated the barrier.
reference_short: Yan, Tan, Lin, Shi et al., RSC Adv. (2023)
notes: Mined from the OA text (PMC). Triatomic reactive system, so in scope; the separated HF and NaF diatomics are characterized only as asymptotes and get no rows of their own under the standing bare-diatomic convention. ground_state_mult left empty - the surface is the ground doublet of the reactive system rather than a state manifold with an assigned ground term.

ligand_set: four phenolate (OPh-) ligands
geometry_source: geometries (a) and (b) from the experimental crystal structures, which differ only in counter ion and crystallization solvent
method: four-component Dirac-CASSCF and Dirac-NEVPT2 (MS-MR contraction) with the Dirac-Coulomb-Gaunt/Dirac-Breit Hamiltonian, compared against scalar-relativistic CASSCF/CASPT2 followed by state-interaction spin-orbit (SI-SO)
basis_set: mixed ANO-RCC: cobalt decontracted in the four-component results, TZP contraction on the chalcogen, DZP on carbon and DZ on hydrogen. The Table III subset uses a reduced set - DZP on the chalcogen and DZ on carbon
relativistic_treatment: four-component Dirac-Coulomb-Gaunt / full Dirac-Breit Hamiltonian, contrasted with a scalar-relativistic treatment plus state-interaction spin-orbit
soc_included: yes (the zero-field-splitting parameters D and E are the observables)
active_space_orbital_description: seven electrons in the five cobalt 3d orbitals, and in a larger variant the same seven electrons in ten orbitals adding a second correlating d shell
active_space_protocol: (7e,5o) using only the cobalt 3d shell; (7e,10o) adding a second, correlating set of d orbitals. State averaging run two ways: over the ground quartet alone, and over the full d5 manifold (10 quartets and 40 doublets)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: quartet (S = 3/2, pseudotetrahedral Co(II) d7). Axial and rhombic ZFS in cm-1. Geometry (a), Dirac-CASSCF ground-quartet / Dirac-CASSCF full-d5 / scalar+SI-SO full-d5: with (7e,5o) D = -9.5 / -13.6 / -13.5, E = 1.4 / 2.1 / 2.1; with (7e,10o) D = -10.1 / -13.5 / -12.6, E = 1.4 / 1.9 / 1.8; experiment D = -11.1(3), E = 0.0. Geometry (b), (7e,5o): D = -15.1 / -24.6 / -24.5 with E = 0.0 throughout; (7e,10o): D = -16.2 / -22.5 / -22.5, E = 0.0; experiment D = -23.8(2), E = 0.0. Smaller-basis Table III for geometry (a) with (7e,5o): Dirac-CASSCF D = -13.9 (E = 2.1), scalar CASSCF+SI-SO D = -13.9 (E = 2.1), Dirac-NEVPT2 D = -11.3 (E = 1.5), CASPT2+SI-SO D = -13.1 (E = 1.7).
Other: Balancing the orbitals by state-averaging over the full d5 manifold matters much more than the second d shell: the ground-quartet-only Dirac-CASSCF is the main outlier against experiment, while adding the correlating d orbitals typically shifts the splitting by a few wavenumbers or less. Structures differing only in counter ion and crystallization solvent give dramatically different conformations and ZFS.
reference_short: Reynolds, Shiozaki (2019)
notes: Mined from the OA text. One row per anion, with both crystallographic conformations reported inside the row, following the one-row-per-compound rule. D and E are in cm-1; the two four-component columns of Table II are the ground-quartet and full-d5 state-averaging choices. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are the paper's own (pseudotetrahedral cobalt(II), so d7), and the quartet ground state is consistent with that. The chalcogen diatomics O2/S2/Se2/Te2 benchmarked in the same paper with an (8e,6o) space get no rows under the standing bare-diatomic convention.

compound_name: N,N'-dimethylpiperazine radical cation (DMP+), mixed-valent charge-localized versus charge-delocalized structures, and the 3s-Rydberg state of neutral DMP
geometry_source: pre-generated pathway interpolating between the delocalized (D) and localized (L) structures; energies reported relative to the delocalized minimum
method: CASSCF and MRCI+Q using the CW-contracted CISD routine with Davidson size-consistency correction, run both state-specific and state-averaged (two lowest doublet states, equal weights); additional RASSCF calculations restricting holes in the doubly occupied and electrons in the virtual part of the active space to two and four respectively; non-orthogonal CI over three UHF solutions as a quasidiabatic basis for comparison
software: MOLPRO 2022.2 for all CASSCF-based work; Q-Chem 5.0 for the NOCI; TURBOMOLE, ORCA and CP2K for the supporting calculations
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ (aug-cc-pVDZ/C auxiliary sets for the density-fitted steps)
active_space_orbital_description: 11 electrons in 12 orbitals, taken identically to the earlier study: the two nitrogen lone pairs, their respective double-shell orbitals, the two C-C bonding orbitals and the two N-Me bonding orbitals together with the corresponding antibonding orbitals
active_space_protocol: (11,12) as in the earlier work; a RASSCF variant restricting the hole and electron counts to two and four, then a larger (19,20) space adding the bonding and antibonding orbitals of all sigma C-N bonds
electronic_structure_description: Two lowest doublet states of DMP+ along the delocalized-to-localized pathway, energies in eV relative to the delocalized minimum (curves in Fig. 1, not tabulated in the text). The apparent barrier separating localized and delocalized minima reported in earlier MRCI work is shown to be an artifact of unphysical curve crossings of the state-specific reference wave functions: state-averaged MRCI removes the discontinuity, leaving no barrier and hence no localized minimum for the bare cation. In the observed 3s-type Rydberg state of neutral DMP, by contrast, the Rydberg electron binds more strongly to a localized positive charge distribution and does produce a localized minimum, matching the experimental increase of about 0.11 eV in the Rydberg electron binding energy from the delocalized to the localized structure.
Other: CASSCF Mulliken spin densities at the hole-bearing nitrogen, taken from the first-order density matrix of the doublet ground state, track the localization along the path and are reported alongside the energies. Per-state electronic energies are in Supplementary Data 3.
reference_short: Reimann et al., Nat. Commun. 15, 293 (2024)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Metal-free organic radical cation, so metal_center is 'none'. active_space_nel/norb hold the primary (11,12) space used for the reported CASSCF and MRCI+Q curves; the RASSCF-only (19,20) variant is recorded in the protocol rather than the numeric columns. Energies live in Fig. 1 and Supplementary Data 3, so no per-point numbers are transcribed - only the 0.11 eV experimental binding-energy shift stated in the text.

compound_name: Li2H triatomic - lowest three adiabatic and lowest two diabatic surfaces for the H + Li2 reaction
geometry_source: global grid in Jacobi coordinates covering the H + Li2 and Li + LiH arrangements, fitted to a diabatic surface
method: MCSCF (CASSCF) references followed by internally contracted MRCI for the three lowest adiabatic states, then a diabatization of the lowest two; the lowest five states are used as reference energies when reducing the three reported adiabatic surfaces
active_space_orbital_description: of the 7 electrons in the system, 4 sit in 2 closed-shell orbitals (2 A' + 0 A''), leaving 3 electrons in the valence space across 13 active orbitals (10 A' + 3 A''); 319 external orbitals (192 A' + 127 A''). The MCSCF function comprises 570 determinants and 1014 intermediate states; in the MRCI step the 2 closed orbitals become core, giving 705 202 contracted configurations (420 internal, 28 548 single-external, 676 234 double-external)
electronic_structure_description: Three lowest adiabatic states of Li2H mapped globally, with the lowest two transformed to a diabatic representation - the first accurate diabatic surface for nonadiabatic H + Li2 dynamics. The reaction is exothermic with relatively deep wells along the reaction path, and the conical intersection geometry lies near the bottom of the potential well.
Other: Earlier surfaces the authors compare against: Siegbahn and Schaefer (SCF + full CI, 1975), Kim and Herschbach (well depth 3.812 eV), Maniero et al. (full CI, 394 points, 6-311G(2df,2pd), giving a barrierless exothermic H + Li2(X1Sigma-g+) -> Li + LiH(X1Sigma+) releasing 1.474 eV), Skomorowski et al. (CCSD(T), conical intersection reported), Song et al. (CASSCF/MRCI, 3726 points) and Yuan et al. (CASSCF/MRCI-F12, 29 842 points, cc-pVTZ).
reference_short: Yin, Gao, Cao, Li, Wang et al., RSC Adv. (2020)
notes: Mined from the OA text (PMC). Triatomic, so in scope. The active-space numbers are the paper's own decomposition - 7 total electrons, 4 in two closed-shell orbitals, 3 active across 13 orbitals - transcribed rather than re-derived. Multiplicity fields left empty: the paper labels the surfaces by adiabatic state index and Cs symmetry rather than by spin multiplicity. Well depths and reaction energies quoted are those the paper attributes to earlier surfaces; its own numbers are presented as figures.

compound_name: HAsO (and its deuterated isotopologue DAsO) - X1A' and A1A'' states behind the single-vibronic-level emission spectra
geometry_source: geometries optimized separately for each state at CASSCF/NEVPT2, RSPT2-F12 and MRCI-F12 (and CCSD(T*)-F12b for the closed-shell X1A'); potential energy functions then built from 334 and 320 CASSCF/MRCI-F12/CVQZ-F12 energies for X1A' and A1A'' over the ranges 1.2-2.8 A in r(HAs), 67-157 and 55-145 degrees in theta(HAsO), and 1.4-2.5 / 1.5-2.6 A in r(AsO)
method: CASSCF with a full valence active space followed by MRCI-F12, RSPT2-F12 and NEVPT2; CCSD(T*)-F12a/b for the closed-shell ground state. Some MRCI-F12 calculations correlate the As 3d10 core (core,4,1) on top of the frozen-core CASSCF full-valence orbitals, with the geminal Slater exponent raised from 1.0 to 1.5 as recommended for core-valence F12 work
basis_set: F12-designed basis sets (see the paper's Table 1); for NEVPT2, aug-cc-pVQZ on O and H with the ECP10MDF effective core potential and aug-cc-pVQZ-PP on As. For the core-correlated MRCI-F12, uncontracted tight 4d (12.0, 4.0, 1.3333333, 0.444444), 2f (14.0, 6.0) and 2g (9.6, 2.4) functions were added on As, giving 278 contracted functions for HAsO (denoted CVQZ-F12)
relativistic_treatment: ECP10MDF effective core potential on arsenic (accounting for As 1s2 2p2 2p6)
active_space_orbital_description: full valence active space at the CASSCF level (stated as 'full valence', with no (nel,norb) pair given). Sizes of the resulting MRCI-F12 expansions: 1 516 432 contracted / 138 334 504 uncontracted configurations with the default frozen core, rising to 15 388 677 / 3 175 152 080 with the As 3d10 electrons active
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X1A'; the emitting state is A1A'', an open-shell singlet for which single-reference methods such as B3LYP and CCSD(T) are inadequate. MRCI-F12 gives a T0 (adiabatic transition energy with zero-point correction) in good agreement with the experimental value and markedly better than the other multireference methods tried here or earlier computed values; T0 values of 11731 and 14225 cm-1 (1.454 and 1.764 eV) are quoted from the earlier level of theory being improved upon.
Other: Anharmonic vibrational wavefunctions from the fitted potential energy functions gave Franck-Condon factors including anharmonicity and Duschinsky rotation, which reproduce the vibrational structure of the observed single-vibronic-level emission spectra of both HAsO and DAsO but suggest a loss of intensity in part of the spectrum.
reference_short: Simulation of the single-vibronic-level emission spectra of HAsO and DAsO (2016)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Triatomic, in scope. active_space_nel/norb left empty: the paper specifies the space only as 'full valence' and never writes an (n,m) pair, so nothing is derived. The 11731 and 14225 cm-1 T0 values in the text belong to the earlier calculations the paper improves on; the paper's own MRCI-F12 T0 is described as agreeing with experiment but the number sits in a table that is not reliably readable in the extracted text. DAsO is the deuterated isotopologue of the same species and shares this row.

compound_name: HOF / FOH system (hypofluorous acid and its isomers) - global potential energy surfaces for the F(2P) + OH reaction

basis_set: aug-cc-pVnZ (AVnZ) with n = T, Q, 5 and CBS extrapolation

compound_name: LiCaF triatomic - ground-state surface for the Li + CaF -> Ca + LiF reaction under cold conditions
geometry_source: about 11 000 geometries lying below 4.5 eV relative to the global minimum, fitted analytically with a many-body expansion in the three internuclear distances
method: state-averaged CASSCF over the 1 1A', 1 3A' and 1 1A'' states followed by internally contracted MRCI with the Davidson correction (MRCI+Q); coupled-channel quantum reactive scattering in hyperspherical coordinates on the fitted surface
basis_set: aug-cc-pVQZ on Li and F; cc-pwCVQZ-PP on Ca, whose core electrons are described by a pseudopotential
active_space_orbital_description: full valence space: 10 active electrons in 9 active orbitals, comprising the 2s and 2s2p orbitals of Li and F and the 4s4p orbitals of Ca; the Li and F 1s orbitals and the Ca 3s3p orbitals are closed in the CASSCF and cored in the MRCI
electronic_structure_description: Ground singlet surface of the reactive system, with the CASSCF state-averaged over 1 1A', 1 3A' and 1 1A''. The reaction populates several low-lying vibrational levels and many rotational levels of the LiF product.
Other: Quantum scattering on the fitted surface shows the reaction is inefficient in the 1-100 mK regime, so cold Li atoms can sympathetically cool CaF rather than destroy it. An exothermicity of about -4440 cm-1 is quoted from the literature for the analogous process.
reference_short: da Silva et al., The Li + CaF -> Ca + LiF chemical reaction under cold conditions (2023)
notes: Mined from the OA text (accepted manuscript). Triatomic reactive system, so in scope; CaF and LiF appear only as asymptotic diatomics and get no rows. ground_state_mult left empty - the surface is the ground state of the reactive system and the paper does not assign a ground term.

compound_name: nitrosyl chloride ClNO - 1 and 2 1A' surfaces for photodissociation of the B band

electronic_structure_description: Cost-scaling benchmark rather than a spectroscopic study: NEVPT4 shows the same scaling behaviour as NEVPT3, the similar cost tracing to the u-vector step, which amounts to one calculation of the closely related FIC-MRCI method scaling as N^6. compound_name: sulfur hexafluoride SF6 - A1g, Eg, T2g and T2u normal-mode vibrational frequencies from a symmetry-determined potential curve

method: complete active space self-consistent field to define the reference configuration, then MRCI for the potential curve and the frequencies. The four normal modes fully determined by the equilibrium structure and Oh symmetry - A1g, Eg, T2g and T2u - were computed at MRCI/6-311G*, and the authors report the smallest relative errors against experiment among the methods compared. The 21-dimensional displacement space of the seven nuclei reduces to A1g, Eg, T1u, T1u, T1u, T1g, T2g and T2u.
Other: The approach is first demonstrated on the B2 mode of water, for which a frequency of 3869.74 cm-1 is obtained. Its point is that computing frequencies from a symmetry-constrained potential curve saves enough effort to afford a higher-level method and larger basis.
reference_short: Xu, Guo, Wang, Acta Phys. Sin. 71, 093101 (2022)

compound_name: HeHHe+ - proton-bound helium dimer, hydrogen tunneling splitting
method: nuclear-electronic orbital multireference configuration interaction (NEO-MRCI): NEO-SA-MCSCF orbitals optimized with equal weights on the two lowest vibronic states, then a NEO-MR-SDenCI expansion of single-electron, single-proton and double electron-proton excitations from that reference. The transferring hydrogen is quantized and represented by two proton basis function centers whose positions come from conventional CCSD optimizations
basis_set: even-tempered 8s8p8d8f protonic basis; aug-cc-pVTZ electronic basis on He (cc-pVTZ on He in one variant); cc-pV5Z* on the quantum proton
active_space_orbital_description: no electronic active space is used - only a full protonic active space
active_space_protocol: electronic (2e,2o) of the in-phase sigma and sigma* orbitals together with a full protonic active space; for HeHHe+ no electronic active space is needed at all
electronic_structure_description: Two lowest vibronic states, the tunneling doublet of the bridging proton, computed at a range of fixed He-He distances.
Other: Tunneling splittings computed at fixed geometries over a range of donor-acceptor distances, and reproduced for deuterium as well. The paper's conclusion is that relatively large electronic and protonic basis sets plus a (2e,2o) sigma/sigma* space suffice to describe the vibronic tunneling states, and that NEO-MRCI handles both linear and non-linear tunneling paths.
reference_short: Computing hydrogen tunneling splittings with nuclear-electronic orbital MRCI (2025)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Multicomponent (nuclear-electronic) multireference method, so the active space has an electronic and a protonic part; active_space_nel/norb record the electronic part only and the protonic part is described in words. Numerical tunneling splittings are reported in tables and SI tables that the extracted text does not render reliably, so no values are transcribed. All quantum-proton calculations use the cc-pV5Z* electronic basis on the transferring proton, where the asterisk marks the modified core contraction NEO requires.

ligand_set: nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA), an industrially relevant chelating agent

active_space_protocol: Several families of active space are compared: singly-occupied-plus-empty (SOE) spaces, SOE extended by the 3d and 4d shells (SOE union 3d4d), and larger spaces reaching 49 electrons in 36 orbitals. DMRG-NEVPT2 used a maximum bond dimension of 1000, reduced to 600 for the largest (49,36) spaces. The reported outcome is that adding the 4d shell to the SOE space gave NO improvement over the SOE spaces themselves - a documented case where enlargement does not help.
multiplicities_studied: spin states of the Fe(III)-NTA complex across the accessible manifold
electronic_structure_description: Assessment of electronic-structure methods against two industrially motivated properties of the chelating agent NTA: its selectivity across six different first-row transition-metal ions, and the spin-state energetics of its Fe(III) complex. Active spaces compared are the singly-occupied-plus-empty (SOE) family, SOE extended by the 3d and 4d shells, and spaces up to 49 electrons in 36 orbitals. The reported result is that the 3d4d extension gives NO improvement over the plain SOE spaces - a documented case where enlarging the active space does not help. DMRG-NEVPT2 used a maximum bond dimension of 1000, reduced to 600 for the largest (49,36) spaces.
reference_short: Chelate Complexes of 3d Transition Metal Ions—A Challenge for Electronic-Structure Methods?

compound_name: CuCl copper monochloride - low-lying excited states
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with the CASSCF wave function as reference, plus a first-order treatment of scalar relativistic effects; the Cu+ ion spectrum is analysed alongside for comparison

active_space_protocol: 11 orbitals initially; extended to (12e,12o) by adding the Cl 3p sigma orbital for the Sigma+ states

compound_name: p-block atoms B through I - spin-orbit splittings from four-component multireference methods
method: four-component CASSCF (4c-CASSCF) with the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian, state-averaged over all targeted and lower states to avoid biasing the orbitals and to prevent root flipping, followed by 4c-CASPT2 and 4c-MR-CISD+Q; 4c-Dirac-Hartree-Fock closed-shell orbitals provided the starting guess, using the corresponding anion for odd-electron atoms
basis_set: uncontracted Dunning basis sets; Dyall's optimized sets were also used
relativistic_treatment: four-component Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian, with Breit terms included
soc_included: yes (the spin-orbit splittings are the observable)
active_space_orbital_description: a 4-orbital active space corresponding to the valence s and p orbitals of the atom
electronic_structure_description: Spin-orbit splittings of the p-block elements B to I. Against experiment, 4c-MR-CISD+Q is best for the light elements, 4c-CASSCF best beyond fluorine, and 4c-CASPT2 best for the group 13 atoms; the heavier elements show little basis-set dependence.
reference_short: Spin-orbit coupling via four-component multireference methods (2018)

compound_name: first-, second- and third-row atoms and atomic ions - anisotropic dipole polarizabilities and quadrupole moments
method: CASSCF, built in two stages: the first uses the valence np space with the valence s shell inactive, making the reference equivalent to the corresponding open-shell ROHF wave function; the space is then extended using approximate natural orbitals from that ROHF calculation, retaining whole shells and keeping all orbitals with large occupation numbers
active_space_orbital_description: extended space built from the 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p and 3d orbitals for first-row systems; 3s, 3p, 4s, 4p, 4d for second-row; 4s, 4p, 5s, 5p, 5d for third-row. Inner-shell orbitals stay frozen in their ROHF form
active_space_protocol: stage 1: valence np space only, s shell inactive (ROHF-equivalent reference); stage 2: extend with ROHF natural orbitals, whole shells retained
electronic_structure_description: Dipole polarizabilities and quadrupole moments of open-shell atoms and ions. The authors note that although these relatively large CASSCF spaces already recover much of the correlation, neutral and negatively charged systems need a more sophisticated treatment.
reference_short: Anisotropic dipole polarizabilities and quadrupole moments of open-shell atoms and ions
